stories.title: India says trade talks with the US are still 'ongoing' — six months after Trump and Modi announced a tariff-cutting deal
stories.what_happened: At the Ministry of External Affairs' regular briefing on Tuesday, spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal told reporters that the **conversation between India and the US on the interim bilateral trade agreement is ongoing**, and that both governments have done substantial work toward finalizing it. He did not give a specific timeline for when a deal might be signed. This comes even as, separately, a coalition of **25 Democratic-led US states** has sued the Trump administration over a different set of tariffs — measures that place India in a 10% bracket — arguing they exceed the president's legal authority.
key_points: MEA spokesperson **Randhir Jaiswal** confirmed talks on an **interim bilateral trade agreement** are still ongoing
Both sides have done **'a lot of work'**, but no final deal has been signed yet
In **February 2026**, Trump and Modi announced a deal cutting US tariffs on Indian goods from **25% to 18%**
Separately, **25 US states** are suing the Trump administration over broader tariffs that include India in a **10% bracket**
The comments came at the MEA's routine **bi-weekly media briefing** in New Delhi

depth.background: India and the US have been negotiating a broader trade agreement for over a year, aiming to cut tariffs and expand market access for goods on both sides. In **February 2026**, Presidents Trump and Modi jointly announced they'd reached a deal lowering US tariffs on Indian exports from 25% to 18% — but that was described as a first step, not the final comprehensive agreement both sides say they still want. Since then, momentum on the full interim agreement has been slower than expected, with earlier reports in the summer describing prospects as **'dimming'** ahead of an August 1 informal deadline that passed without a deal.

stories.title: Jomel Warrican's six-wicket haul leaves the Pakistan-West Indies Test in Trinidad on a knife edge
stories.what_happened: Pakistan were eventually **bowled out for 387**, giving them a **43-run first-innings lead** over West Indies' 344. Left-arm spinner **Jomel Warrican** was the standout bowler for West Indies, finishing with figures of **6 for 112** to break through Pakistan's middle and lower order after the big partnership. The foundation of Pakistan's total was a long stand between **Abdullah Shafique (160)** and **Babar Azam (88)**, which dragged Pakistan from a shaky position into a healthy lead. With two days left in the five-day Test, the match remains **finely poised** heading into West Indies' second innings.
key_points: Pakistan were bowled out for **387** in their first innings at Queen's Park Oval, Trinidad
That gives them a **43-run lead** over West Indies, who had scored 344
West Indies spinner **Jomel Warrican took 6 for 112**, doing the bulk of the damage
**Abdullah Shafique scored 160** and **Babar Azam made 88** in a long partnership that built the lead
The 2nd Test (August 2-6) heads into its final two days **finely poised**

depth.background: Pakistan are touring the West Indies for a Test series, with this the **2nd Test at Queen's Park Oval in Trinidad**, scheduled to run August 2-6. West Indies batted first and posted 344 in their first innings. Pakistan's reply was built around a long, patient stand between opener **Abdullah Shafique** and star batter **Babar Azam**, who steadied the innings after Pakistan had looked in some early trouble.

stories.title: Pakistan stretch their reply to West Indies past 279 as Shafique and Babar's marathon stand keeps the 2nd Test finely poised in Trinidad
stories.what_happened: Pakistan extended their first-innings reply to West Indies' 344 to **279 for 2** by the close of Day 3 of the second Test at Trinidad's Queen's Park Oval, still trailing by 65 runs with eight second-innings wickets in hand. The platform was set on Day 2, when Abdullah Shafique brought up his sixth Test century — his first since 2024 — finishing the day unbeaten on 107 off 185 balls, while captain Babar Azam remained not out on 86, edging toward a century he hasn't scored in four years. Their unbroken third-wicket partnership had already reached 168 runs by the end of Day 2 and carried Pakistan from a precarious position to within touching distance of West Indies' total. Pakistan's bowling attack, led by Sajid Khan's 4 for 85, had earlier restricted West Indies to 344, with contributions of 73 from Justin Greaves and 70 from captain Roston Chase.
key_points: Pakistan reached **279 for 2** at the close of Day 3, trailing West Indies' first-innings **344 by 65 runs**.
**Abdullah Shafique (107* overnight)** and **Babar Azam (86* overnight)** had already put on an unbroken **168-run stand** through Day 2.
Shafique's century was his **sixth in Tests** and his first since 2024, after being recalled following Shan Masood's finger injury.
Babar was closing in on his **first century in four years** as the partnership carried into Day 3.
The match, at Trinidad's **Queen's Park Oval**, runs through August 6 with the series level at 0-0 after the first Test.

depth.background: Pakistan and West Indies are playing a two-Test series, with the tourists looking to respond after West Indies posted a competitive first-innings total of 344. Abdullah Shafique was only recalled to the side after regular opener Shan Masood picked up a finger injury, slotting into the unfamiliar number-three position — a return to the side after losing his place following Pakistan's home series against South Africa last October. Babar Azam, Pakistan's captain, came into the match still searching for his first Test century in four years, making his and Shafique's partnership a redemption story for both batters as much as a match-defining one.

thread.previously: Shafique and Babar Azam's unbroken 168-run partnership had taken Pakistan to 266 for 2 at the end of Day 2, trailing West Indies' 344 by 78 runs, with Shafique on 107* and Babar on 86*.
thread.changed: Play continued into Day 3, with Pakistan extending to 279 for 2 (trailing by 65) as the same pair carried their partnership forward, closing in on a first-innings lead.

stories.title: Sergio Perez says there's 'no loyalty' in F1, reflecting on being dropped by his old team after saving it from collapse
stories.what_happened: In new comments, Perez discussed his complicated history with the team now known as **Aston Martin**, saying that despite everything he did for the outfit — including helping push it into **administration proceedings** to protect jobs after its former owner, Kingfisher Airlines, collapsed in 2018 — he was ultimately let go. **'I was like, look, there is no loyalty in this sport,'** he said, adding that he didn't take the move personally and instead focused on performing on track. He pointed to winning the **2020 Sakhir Grand Prix** — the team's first win in any guise, and the first for the Force India/Racing Point lineage since Jordan's last win in 2003 — as the highlight that came from that focus. Perez said he maintains a good relationship with people at Aston Martin despite the way things ended.
key_points: Sergio Perez opened up about being **dropped by Racing Point (now Aston Martin)** despite having helped **save the team from administration** years earlier.
He said plainly: **'There is no loyalty in this sport'** — but added he didn't take the dismissal personally.
Perez credited his own **Sakhir Grand Prix win** — the team's **first-ever victory**, and its first since Jordan in 2003 — as a turning point he's proud of.

He traced his history with the outfit back to **2014**, when it was still called **Force India**, and described leading efforts to save it from financial collapse after Kingfisher Airlines' collapse in **2018**.
The comments come as Perez now drives for **Cadillac**, F1's newest team, reflecting on a career that has spanned multiple team identities and ownership changes.

depth.background: Sergio Perez's F1 career has been intertwined with one team through several rebrands: he joined as **Force India** in 2014, stayed on through its financial troubles and rescue in **2018** (when it became Racing Point), delivered the team's breakthrough win at the **2020 Sakhir Grand Prix**, and then watched it transform into **Aston Martin** under new ownership before being dropped. He's now racing for **Cadillac**, F1's brand-new American team that joined the grid this season. His comments reflect a broader truth in Formula 1: team ownership, sponsorship, and driver line-ups change fast, and even drivers who help save a team from extinction aren't guaranteed a long-term seat.

stories.title: Michigan votes today in a primary that will help decide control of a critical 2026 Senate and governor's race
stories.what_happened: Michigan voters are casting ballots today in **primary elections** for governor, U.S. Senate, and all 13 U.S. House seats, with polls open **7am to 8pm local time**. Because Gov. Whitmer cannot seek a third nonconsecutive term and Sen. Peters chose not to run again, both races are **open contests** without an incumbent, which typically draws bigger, more crowded fields of candidates. On the Democratic side, U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens and epidemiologist Abdul El-Sayed are among the notable candidates competing for the Senate nomination. Early and absentee voting has been active in the run-up, with reports of tens of thousands of absentee ballots already received in Detroit alone. Winners of today's primaries advance to face their opponents in the **November 3, 2026 general election**.
key_points: Polls are open **7am to 8pm local time today** across Michigan for the state's **2026 primary election**.
Governor **Gretchen Whitmer is term-limited** and cannot run again, leaving the governorship **wide open** for the first time in years.
Democratic Senator **Gary Peters is retiring**, and Michigan's open Senate seat is considered one of the **most competitive nationally** in November.
Democratic Senate hopefuls include Rep. **Haley Stevens** and epidemiologist **Abdul El-Sayed**, competing for the nomination.
All **13 Michigan U.S. House seats** are also technically on today's primary ballot ahead of the November general election.

depth.background: Michigan is one of the most closely watched **swing states** in American politics — it has flipped between parties in recent presidential and Senate elections, making it a bellwether for the national mood. Both the governor's mansion and a Senate seat becoming open at the same time is unusual and raises the stakes: whoever wins these primaries today will carry their party's hopes into a **general election battleground** in November. Control of the Senate can hinge on just a handful of races like this one, since the chamber is often narrowly divided.

stories.title: BSE's profit more than doubles to ₹539 crore as India's exchange operator rides a derivatives and mutual-fund boom
stories.what_happened: BSE Ltd reported its April–June quarter (Q1 FY27) results on Tuesday, showing consolidated profit after tax surging **103% year-on-year to ₹539 crore**, up sharply from the same quarter last year. Consolidated revenue rose **59% to ₹1,045 crore**, while operating EBITDA — a measure of core operating profitability before interest, tax, and depreciation — jumped **122% to ₹626 crore**, pushing EBITDA margin to **65%**. The company credited the strong showing to robust derivatives trading volumes, its growing mutual-fund distribution business, and continued investment in its international arm, India INX, which operates out of Gujarat's GIFT City. BSE is scheduled to hold its earnings call with analysts and investors this evening.
key_points: **BSE Ltd's** consolidated profit jumped **103% year-on-year to ₹539 crore** in the June quarter.
Revenue climbed **59% to ₹1,045 crore**, driven by derivatives trading and mutual fund distribution.
Operating **EBITDA rose 122% to ₹626 crore**, with margins expanding to a strong **65%**.
Growth was fueled by **robust derivatives trading**, mutual-fund distribution, and BSE's international arm, **India INX**.
The results land the same week several other major Indian companies — Airtel, ONGC, ITC — are also reporting.

depth.background: BSE Ltd (formerly the Bombay Stock Exchange) is Asia's oldest stock exchange and, alongside the NSE, one of India's two dominant trading venues — it earns money by charging fees on every trade, especially the fast-growing options and futures ('derivatives') segment. Exchanges like BSE are effectively a bet on how much India trades: when retail and institutional investors are active, especially in high-frequency derivatives, exchange revenue rises sharply because fees scale with volume. India's derivatives market has exploded in size over the past few years, making exchange operators one of the more direct ways to track that boom's profitability.

stories.title: Government's ₹31,400 crore LIC share sale is oversubscribed 3.3 times by institutions — but the stock still tumbles 8.7%
stories.what_happened: The Indian government launched an OFS to sell up to **6.5% of its stake in LIC**, worth roughly **₹31,400 crore** at the floor price of **₹382 per share** — a price set at a **10.8% discount** to the previous day's closing price to attract buyers. The non-retail (institutional) portion of the offer was **oversubscribed 3.32 times on the opening day**, with bids worth **₹36,400 crore**, prompting the government to exercise its **greenshoe option** and expand the total sale to **822.25 million shares**. Despite the strong institutional demand, LIC's stock price fell sharply, dropping **8.7% to close at ₹391.30** on the NSE, as the market absorbed the discount and the dilution of government ownership. Even after the entire stake sale goes through, the **Centre will still hold close to 90%** of LIC.
key_points: The government offered to sell up to **6.5% of its stake in LIC**, India's largest state-owned insurer, through an **Offer for Sale (OFS)**.
The **institutional portion was oversubscribed 3.32 times**, with bids worth **₹36,400 crore** pouring in against the base offer.
The government **exercised its 'greenshoe' option** to sell an extra 4%, taking the total offer to **822.25 million shares**.
The floor price was set at **₹382 a share**, a **10.8% discount** to Monday's closing price — and LIC's stock fell **8.7% to ₹391.30** on the news.
Even after the full sale, the **government will still own about 90%** of LIC, down from its current 96.5% stake.

depth.background: LIC (Life Insurance Corporation of India) is India's largest insurer and one of its most valuable state-owned companies, and the government has been gradually **selling down its stake** over several years — partly to meet stock-exchange rules that require large listed companies to have a minimum public shareholding, and partly to raise revenue for the budget. An 'Offer for Sale' is a mechanism that lets a company's existing large shareholder — here, the government — sell shares directly on the stock exchange without issuing new ones. A 'greenshoe option' lets the seller sell additional shares beyond the original plan if demand is strong enough.

stories.title: Sensex and Nifty snap their 4-day rally, closing lower as a late Nifty comeback trims the losses
stories.what_happened: India's Sensex and Nifty closed lower on **Tuesday, August 4**, ending a four-day winning streak. The Sensex fell **210 points to 78,428.45**, and the Nifty dropped **159 points to 24,614.90**. The session had opened on a strong note, with the Sensex up nearly **494 points (0.62%)** at the open, but the gains faded through the day as investors turned cautious on mixed global cues. A late rally in the Nifty trimmed what would have been steeper losses. Stocks like **Trent, Bajaj Finance, BEL, Tata Steel, M&M, Bajaj Finserv and Titan** rose as much as **1.15%**, while **HUL, NTPC, HDFC Bank, Reliance Industries and IndiGo** fell as much as **1.7%**. Traders pointed to continued unease over Middle East geopolitical tensions and their potential to push crude oil prices — and the rupee — around.
key_points: Sensex fell **210 points to 78,428**; Nifty lost **159 points to 24,614.90** on Tuesday, August 4.
The drop **snaps a four-session winning streak** that had been driven by falling crude oil prices.
Markets opened higher — Sensex up nearly **494 points** — before **global caution** dragged indices down through the day.
Investors stayed wary of **Middle East tensions** and their knock-on effect on crude prices and the **rupee**.
**Trent, Bajaj Finance, BEL, Tata Steel** were among the gainers; **HUL, NTPC, HDFC Bank, RIL** led the losers.

depth.background: Indian benchmark indices had been on a rare four-session winning streak, lifted mainly by falling global crude oil prices — cheaper oil is good for India, which imports most of its oil, because it eases both inflation and the trade deficit. But that relief has been running into a countervailing risk: the escalating **US-Iran standoff over the Strait of Hormuz**, a chokepoint oil-tanker route, which threatens to push oil prices back up if the conflict disrupts shipping.

stories.title: Red Bull turns down a $3 billion offer to buy its junior F1 team, Racing Bulls
stories.what_happened: Red Bull was approached with an offer of roughly **$3 billion** to sell **Racing Bulls**, its junior F1 team, from a group of investment funds based in **Abu Dhabi**. The bid was fronted by financier **Andrew Harriott** and **Dean Attew**, who previously worked as an adviser to former F1 chief executive Bernie Ecclestone. Red Bull **turned the offer down**, choosing to keep its two-team structure intact. The decision signals that Red Bull sees greater long-term value in operating both teams — using Racing Bulls to develop future talent and test setups — than in cashing out, even at a price that would have been a landmark sale in F1 team history.
key_points: Red Bull **rejected a roughly $3 billion (about £2.2bn) bid** for its second F1 team, **Racing Bulls**.
The offer was reportedly backed by **Abu Dhabi-based investment funds** and fronted by financier **Andrew Harriott** and **Dean Attew**, a former adviser to ex-F1 boss Bernie Ecclestone.
Turning it down reaffirms Red Bull's commitment to its **two-team model**, which pairs its senior team with Racing Bulls as a driver-development pipeline.
The rejection comes as F1 gears up for **new engine regulations**, with Red Bull betting Racing Bulls' long-term value exceeds a short-term payout.
The scale of the offer — **$3 billion for F1's smallest-budget team** — underlines how much F1 team valuations have surged in recent years.

depth.background: Racing Bulls (formerly AlphaTauri/Toro Rosso) is Red Bull's second, smaller Formula 1 team, historically used to **develop young drivers** before they graduate to the main Red Bull Racing squad. F1 team valuations have climbed dramatically since the sport's global popularity boomed in the past several years, driven partly by Netflix's 'Drive to Survive' and new races in the US and Middle East, making even a junior, budget-conscious team like Racing Bulls attractive to outside investors. Investment interest from Gulf-region funds in sports franchises — football clubs, golf tours, and now F1 teams — has been a recurring theme in global sports finance.

stories.title: Pakistan Women salvage a consolation win over Sri Lanka, taking the 3rd T20I by 4 wickets as Sri Lanka claim the series 2-1
stories.what_happened: In the third and final T20I of the series at the **Rangiri Dambulla International Stadium** on August 4, Pakistan Women successfully chased Sri Lanka's total of **113/6**, reaching **115/6 in 18.2 overs** to win by 4 wickets with 10 balls remaining. **Ayesha Zafar's 39 off 31 balls** anchored the chase and earned her the Player of the Match award. The pitch played slow and low, and both sides lost six wickets each as neither found it easy to score freely — Pakistan's **spin bowlers** were credited with restricting Sri Lanka first before their batters ground out the target. The result gives Pakistan a **consolation win**, but Sri Lanka Women take the series **2-1** after winning the opening two matches.
key_points: Pakistan Women chased down **114** to win the 3rd T20I in **Dambulla**, finishing **115/6 with 10 balls to spare**.
**Ayesha Zafar** top-scored with **39 off 31 balls** and was named **Player of the Match**.
Both teams lost **six wickets each** on a slow, gripping Dambulla pitch that made scoring hard.
**Sri Lanka Women win the series 2-1**, having taken the first two matches before Pakistan's spin attack turned the tables in the decider.
It's Pakistan's only win of the tour, ending the series on a high note despite the overall series loss.

depth.background: This T20I series was part of Pakistan Women's tour of Sri Lanka, with Sri Lanka having already sealed the series by winning the first two matches through strong batting performances. This dead-rubber third match still mattered for momentum heading into both teams' next assignments, and Dambulla's slower pitches are notoriously difficult for aggressive T20 batting, rewarding disciplined spin bowling over power-hitting.

stories.title: Rajya Sabha adjourned twice today as Kharge accuses the government of handing 70+ acres to the Ram Temple trust and demands Amit Shah explain the student crackdown
stories.what_happened: The Rajya Sabha was adjourned twice on Tuesday, August 4, first and then again until 2 pm, as Opposition MPs pressed for a statement from Home Minister Amit Shah on two fronts: alleged police excesses against students during the July 20 protest march, and new allegations about land transfers to the Ram Temple trust. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge alleged the central government handed over **more than 70 acres of land** to the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, and separately raised concerns about the management of cash donations and offerings made to the trust. He questioned aloud why investigative agencies — the Enforcement Directorate, CBI, and Income Tax department — had not scrutinized the matter, saying "those who loot in the name of Lord Ram should apologize to the entire country." As Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Kharge attempted to raise the issue formally but was not permitted to speak before the presiding officer adjourned the House amid the disruption.
key_points: The **Rajya Sabha** (Parliament's upper house) was adjourned **twice on Tuesday**, till 2 pm, amid Opposition protests.
Congress president **Mallikarjun Kharge** alleged the government handed over **more than 70 acres of land** to the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust.
Kharge also demanded Home Minister **Amit Shah** personally explain the **police crackdown on students** during the July 20 Parliament march.
He asked pointedly where agencies like the **ED, CBI, and Income Tax department** were on the alleged land dealings.
Kharge, as Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, was **not allowed to speak** on the matter before the House adjourned.

depth.background: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust manages the Ram Temple in Ayodhya and has handled large volumes of land purchases and public donations since the temple's construction began. This clash follows weeks of Opposition anger over the **July 20 police crackdown on students** protesting the NEET-UG medical entrance exam paper leak at a Parliament march, which the Opposition has repeatedly tried to force the government to address on the floor of the House. The Rajya Sabha is Parliament's upper house, where laws are debated and the government is held to account through structured questioning — but sessions have been repeatedly disrupted this session by the same standoff.

stories.title: Pujara says Jadeja has changed his whole mindset as a bowler — from containing runs to hunting wickets
stories.what_happened: Speaking ahead of India's upcoming **Test series in Sri Lanka**, Pujara said Jadeja's evolution into a more **attack-minded bowler** has been one of the biggest factors behind his continued Test success. **'Earlier, his mindset was a little more defensive, but now he is delivering every ball with the purpose of taking a wicket,'** Pujara said, explaining that Jadeja now **uses the crease better, tries to go wider, and adjusts his length according to the batter** he's up against. Pujara framed this as a genuine mental shift — not just a change in skills — that has made Jadeja a more complete red-ball bowler over time.
key_points: Former India batter **Cheteshwar Pujara** says **Ravindra Jadeja's** biggest evolution as a bowler is **mental, not technical**.
Pujara explained Jadeja now bowls **'with the purpose of taking a wicket'** on every ball, rather than just trying to restrict runs.
Jadeja is reportedly using the **crease more, varying his angles wider, and adjusting his length** to each specific batter.
The comments come **ahead of India's two-match Test series against Sri Lanka**, starting **August 15**.
Jadeja's shift is framed as a key reason for his continued **success as a senior all-rounder** in India's Test side.

depth.background: Ravindra Jadeja has long been one of India's most reliable Test all-rounders, historically valued as much for his **tight, containing left-arm spin** as for his batting and fielding. Cheteshwar Pujara, a former India Test specialist known for his own defensive discipline, has become a respected analyst of the technical and mental side of red-ball cricket since retiring from the international side. His comments come as India is finalizing its bowling attack for the upcoming Sri Lanka tour, especially significant given that **pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah has just been ruled out** of that series with injury, putting more weight on spinners and all-rounders like Jadeja.

stories.title: Senate committee votes today on Todd Blanche as attorney general, after he scrapped a $1.8 billion DOJ fund to win over holdout Republicans
stories.what_happened: The Senate Judiciary Committee is meeting today, August 4, to vote on whether to advance Todd Blanche's nomination as U.S. attorney general to the full Senate. Blanche formally rescinded the Justice Department's controversial **$1.8 billion 'anti-weaponization fund'** this week, a concession explicitly aimed at unlocking his stalled nomination. In response, Republican Senators **John Cornyn and Thom Tillis** — two of the committee's key holdouts — said they now intend to back him. Senator **Lisa Murkowski** has not yet signaled support, saying she still wants to fully evaluate the nomination once it clears committee. The committee is expected to advance Blanche's nomination largely along party lines, after which it would proceed to a floor vote in the full Senate for final confirmation.
key_points: The **Senate Judiciary Committee** votes today on Trump's pick for attorney general, **Todd Blanche**.
Blanche **rescinded the DOJ's $1.8 billion 'anti-weaponization fund'** this week specifically to win over skeptical Republicans.
That move flipped two key holdouts, **Senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis**, who now back him.
**Senator Lisa Murkowski** has still not committed, saying she needs to evaluate the nomination further once it clears committee.
A committee win sends the nomination to a **full Senate floor vote** for final confirmation.

depth.background: Todd Blanche has been serving as **acting attorney general** while his permanent nomination has stalled amid unusual resistance from within his own party. The sticking point was a **$1.8 billion Justice Department fund** that critics — including some Republicans — worried could be used to target political opponents, hence the nickname 'anti-weaponization fund.' His committee vote was **postponed once already**, on July 29, in what was described as a major blow to his confirmation chances. Blanche is a former defense lawyer for President Trump personally, making his path to running the DOJ closely watched given his direct ties to the president he'd be serving.

stories.title: ONGC's profit more than doubles to ₹17,034 crore as the Middle East conflict pushes up what it earns per barrel of oil
stories.what_happened: ONGC reported **Q1 FY27 (April-June 2026) net profit of ₹17,033.81 crore**, more than double the ₹8,024.23 crore it made in the same quarter last year, and also well above the ₹6,649.97 crore it posted in the previous (January-March) quarter. The company's **profit before tax hit a record ₹22,848 crore** for a single quarter. Total income rose to ₹48,321.65 crore from ₹33,213.39 crore a year earlier. The key driver was price, not volume: ONGC's **net crude oil realisation** — what it actually earns per barrel after costs — rose to ₹99.45 from ₹66.13 a year ago, tracking the rise in global oil prices.
key_points: **ONGC's** net profit surged **112%** year-on-year to **₹17,033.81 crore** in the June quarter (Q1 FY27)
Profit before tax hit a **record quarterly high of ₹22,848 crore**
Total income rose to **₹48,321.65 crore**, up from ₹33,213.39 crore a year earlier
Net crude oil realisation jumped to **₹99.45 a barrel**, from ₹66.13 a year ago
The jump was driven by **higher global crude prices**, not higher production volumes

depth.background: **ONGC (Oil and Natural Gas Corporation)** is India's largest state-run oil and gas explorer, and its profits move closely with global crude oil prices since it sells the oil and gas it pumps at prevailing market rates. A year ago, in Q1 FY26, ONGC's profit was much lower at ₹8,024 crore because oil prices were weaker then. Crude prices have climbed sharply through 2026 amid escalating tensions in the Middle East, including attacks on shipping near the Strait of Hormuz and the broader Iran standoff — both of which have been rattling global energy markets.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu's opposition leader Udhayanidhi Stalin is arrested from his Chennai home, then ordered released by the Madras High Court
stories.what_happened: A team of **Thanjavur police personnel arrested Udhayanidhi Stalin** from his residence in Neelankarai, Chennai, on **Tuesday morning, August 4**, and took him to Thanjavur for questioning. The case originated from an FIR filed at **Thanjavur East Police Station**, based on a complaint from the organiser of the ruling TVK party's women's wing, accusing him of derogatory remarks about actor Trisha Krishnan made during a farmers' protest over Cauvery water sharing. The FIR cites sections related to **harassment of women, hate speech, the IT Act, and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita**. After he was taken in for questioning, the **Madras High Court intervened and ordered his release**, while directing him to continue cooperating with the investigation. The DMK has pushed back hard, calling the case a politically motivated 'false case' and organizing protests against what it calls a targeted arrest of its senior leader.
key_points: **Udhayanidhi Stalin**, DMK leader and **Leader of the Opposition in Tamil Nadu**, was arrested from his **Neelankarai residence in Chennai on Tuesday morning** by Thanjavur police.
The arrest stems from an **FIR in Thanjavur** over alleged derogatory remarks he made about actor **Trisha Krishnan** during a farmers' protest over Cauvery water.
The FIR invokes sections covering **harassment of women, hate speech, IT Act violations, and provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)** — India's newer criminal code.
The **Madras High Court ordered his release** after questioning, directing him to cooperate with the ongoing investigation.
The **DMK has called the case politically motivated**, or a 'false case,' and staged protests against the arrest.

depth.background: Udhayanidhi Stalin is the son of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister **M.K. Stalin** and a senior DMK leader who currently holds the position of **Leader of the Opposition** in the state assembly, following a change in Tamil Nadu's political alignment. Tamil Nadu has been gripped by tension over **Cauvery river water sharing with Karnataka**, which has triggered farmer protests in the state. The complaint against Udhayanidhi originated from the women's wing of the ruling **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)** party, alleging he made offensive remarks about actor Trisha Krishnan while addressing one such protest.

stories.title: Pakistan appoints former South Africa batter Michael Smith as its new men's batting coach
stories.what_happened: The **Pakistan Cricket Board confirmed on August 4** that it has appointed **Michael Smith**, a 46-year-old former South African cricketer, as batting coach for the men's national team on a **two-year contract**, covering both red-ball and white-ball cricket. Smith played 89 first-class matches, 72 List-A matches, and 16 T20s between 2003 and 2013, scoring **7,029 career runs** including nine centuries and 40 half-centuries, and holds a **Level 4 coaching qualification**. He has previously worked as batting coach for three PSL franchises — Islamabad United, Karachi Kings, and Multan Sultans — as well as with Australia's Hobart Hurricanes and Cricket Tasmania. He will begin his role ahead of Pakistan's upcoming **three-Test series against England**, which starts **August 19**.
key_points: The **Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB)** confirmed **Michael Smith**, a former South African first-class cricketer, as batting coach for a **two-year term**.
Smith, **46**, will work across **both red-ball and white-ball formats**.
He joins ahead of Pakistan's **three-match Test series against England**, starting **August 19**.
In his playing career he scored **7,029 runs** across first-class, List-A, and T20 cricket, with **9 centuries**.
He has coaching experience with **HBL PSL franchises** (Islamabad United, Karachi Kings, Multan Sultans) and Australia's Hobart Hurricanes.

depth.background: Pakistan's men's team has been under scrutiny for its **batting struggles in Test cricket**, including its current tour of the West Indies where the batting order has repeatedly needed long rearguard partnerships to avoid collapse. The PCB has cycled through several support-staff changes recently as it looks to stabilize a team preparing for a high-profile home Test series against England next month. Michael Smith's appointment fits a broader trend of PCB recruiting experienced international coaches with domestic T20 league experience, given his prior stints across multiple PSL franchises.

stories.title: Ireland and Afghanistan open a new era under new captains as a 5-match ODI series begins in Bready
stories.what_happened: The two sides begin a **5-match ODI series** on August 5, with the first two matches at **Bready Cricket Club** and the final three at the **Civil Service Cricket Club in Belfast**, running through August 15. Afghanistan will be led by their newly appointed ODI and Test captain **Rahmat Shah**, with explosive wicketkeeper-batter **Rahmanullah Gurbaz** as his deputy, while Ireland will be captained by veteran opener **Paul Stirling**. All five matches start at 10:45am local time. Afghanistan arrive as strong favorites, having won the last six ODIs between the two sides.
key_points: A **5-match ODI series** between Ireland and Afghanistan runs **August 5 to 15** across Bready and Belfast
Afghanistan are led by newly appointed captain **Rahmat Shah**, with **Rahmanullah Gurbaz** as vice-captain
Ireland are captained by **Paul Stirling**
**Afghanistan have won their last 6 ODIs** against Ireland heading into this series
First two matches at **Bready Cricket Club**, remaining three at **Belfast's Civil Service Cricket Club**

depth.background: Ireland and Afghanistan are both full ICC members who play each other periodically, with Afghanistan having built one of the world's stronger white-ball sides in recent years despite the country's limited domestic infrastructure. Both teams go into this series under **freshly appointed captains** — a notable change for each side as they look toward the next World Cup cycle. Afghanistan's recent ODI dominance over Ireland, with 6 straight wins, sets up this series as a real test of whether Ireland's new leadership can close that gap.

stories.title: Delhi Police stop Kejriwal's march to PM Modi's residence over E20 ethanol-blended petrol
stories.what_happened: On the morning of **August 4**, Arvind Kejriwal led roughly **100 AAP workers and leaders**, including Manish Sisodia and Jasmine Shah, on a march toward Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence. Their goal was to formally submit over **2.3 lakh petitions** gathered from citizens across India opposing the government's E20 ethanol-blended petrol policy, which they say is hurting vehicle owners. **Delhi Police intercepted and stopped the march** on Firoz Shah Road before it could reach the PM's residence, having deployed a heavy security presence of Delhi Police and paramilitary personnel in anticipation. Blocked from proceeding, Kejriwal and the other leaders **sat down in protest on the road**. Kejriwal said afterward that he would **intensify** the campaign against the E20 mandate rather than stand down.
key_points: **Arvind Kejriwal** and about **100 AAP supporters** tried to march to **PM Modi's residence** to hand over petitions against **E20 petrol**.
They carried more than **2.3 lakh (230,000) petitions** collected from citizens nationwide opposing the ethanol-blended fuel policy.
**Delhi Police stopped the march** on Firoz Shah Road, deploying heavy security including paramilitary forces.
Former Delhi deputy CM **Manish Sisodia** and AAP's **Jasmine Shah** sat down in protest after being blocked.
Kejriwal vowed to **intensify the campaign** against the Centre's E20 policy rather than back down.

depth.background: **E20 petrol** is petrol blended with **20% ethanol**, part of the central government's push to cut oil imports and vehicle emissions by mixing biofuel into every litre sold at the pump. AAP, which lost power in Delhi but remains a vocal opposition force, has campaigned against the mandate, arguing ethanol-blended fuel **damages engines and reduces mileage** in older vehicles, a claim the government disputes. Kejriwal, AAP's national convenor, has increasingly used street marches and petition drives to keep pressure on the BJP-led central government since leaving Delhi's chief ministership.

stories.title: Pro-Kannada groups call a Karnataka-wide bandh for August 13 over a fresh order to release Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu
stories.what_happened: Pro-Kannada organisations have called for a statewide bandh (shutdown) in Karnataka on **August 13**, running from **6am to 6pm**, to protest a CWMA directive ordering the state to release **3,500 cusecs of Cauvery water per day to Tamil Nadu for 15 days**. Activist Vatal Nagaraj said the shutdown has the backing of more than **1,600 Kannada organisations** and over **1,000 other groups** across the state, arguing that Karnataka itself is short on water and that the release will hurt local farmers who depend on the same river for irrigation. The Kannada film industry has also thrown its support behind the bandh call. The protest adds to a summer already marked by heavy flooding and monsoon disruption elsewhere in Karnataka and neighboring states.
key_points: Over **1,600 Kannada organisations** have called for a bandh across Karnataka on **August 13**, from 6am to 6pm.
The trigger: a **Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA)** order directing Karnataka to release **3,500 cusecs of water daily to Tamil Nadu for 15 days**.
Activists argue Karnataka itself is facing **water scarcity** and that the release would hurt local farmers.
The **Kannada film industry** has publicly extended support to the bandh call.
This is the latest flashpoint in a **decades-old inter-state dispute** over sharing the Cauvery river's water.

depth.background: The Cauvery river dispute is one of India's oldest and most politically charged inter-state water conflicts, pitting Karnataka (upstream) against Tamil Nadu (downstream) over how much river water each state can use, mainly for irrigation and drinking supply. The Supreme Court eventually settled the sharing formula and created the **Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA)** to enforce it, but on-the-ground compliance remains a recurring flashpoint whenever water levels run low, and past bandh calls over the issue have shut down Bengaluru and other Karnataka cities before.

stories.title: Kimi Antonelli opens up on how pressure 'destroyed' him during his brutal rookie F1 season
stories.what_happened: In an interview released **August 4** as part of SAP's 'Significant Figures' series, Antonelli spoke candidly about the toll of his rookie Formula 1 season, saying the sheer pace of new experiences felt like **'driving three seasons at once'** — overwhelming both physically and mentally. He said the pressure of the role at points **'kind of destroyed'** him, particularly during a difficult stretch in the European leg of the season when he felt he was letting down the people who had backed him, including Wolff, who fast-tracked him into the seat. Antonelli said he has since found ways to manage that pressure better and feels the experience has made him stronger going into the current season. Fellow young driver Arvid Lindblad separately praised Antonelli's 'pure racing instincts' in comments carried the same day.
key_points: Antonelli said the learning curve felt like **'driving three seasons at once'** — mentally and physically overwhelming.
He admitted the pressure of replacing **Lewis Hamilton** at Mercedes **'kind of destroyed'** him at points in his debut season.
The toughest stretch came during the **European leg** of the campaign, when he felt he was **letting down** those who believed in him.
He says the experience has made him **stronger** heading into this season.
The comments came in an **SAP-sponsored interview series** released **August 4**, during F1's summer break.

depth.background: Kimi Antonelli was thrust into one of the most scrutinized seats in Formula 1 when **Mercedes** picked him to replace seven-time champion **Lewis Hamilton**, who left for Ferrari — a decision Mercedes boss Toto Wolff made before Antonelli had even raced in Formula 2, the feeder series most drivers use to prove themselves first. That vote of confidence came with enormous pressure: comparisons to Hamilton, and to teammate **George Russell**, followed him into every race weekend of his rookie campaign.

stories.title: Europe starts enforcing its first-ever law forcing AI chatbots to tell you you're talking to a machine
stories.what_happened: As of **August 2, 2026**, any AI system that talks directly to people — chatbots, voice assistants, customer-service bots — must tell users they're interacting with AI, unless that's already obvious from context. The European Commission formally began enforcing this and other AI Act transparency requirements this week. A related rule requiring **machine-readable watermarks on AI-generated content** (like deepfake videos or AI images) also starts now, though tools already on the market before August 2 get a grace period until December 2026 to comply. Companies that ignore the rules face fines of up to €15 million or 3% of their worldwide annual revenue.
key_points: **Article 50 of the EU AI Act** took effect August 2, and enforcement began this week
AI chatbots and voice assistants must now **disclose they're AI**, unless it's already obvious
AI-generated or edited content — including **deepfakes** — must eventually carry machine-readable marks
Content-marking rules have a **grace period until December 2026** for tools already on the market
Violators risk fines up to **€15 million or 3% of global annual turnover**, whichever is higher

depth.background: The **EU AI Act** is the world's first comprehensive law regulating artificial intelligence, passed by the European Union to manage AI risks by how dangerous a given use case is. One part of that law, Article 50, focuses specifically on **transparency** — making sure people know when they're dealing with a machine rather than a human, and when content (photos, video, audio) has been artificially generated or manipulated. Big tech platforms and AI developers have spent the past two years adjusting products to comply ahead of this deadline.

stories.title: Red Bull reportedly offers to rip up Verstappen's exit clause with a $65m-a-year deal — Jos Verstappen shuts it down
stories.what_happened: According to Dutch media reports, **Red Bull has offered Max Verstappen a new one-year contract extension through 2029**, raising his salary to roughly **€65 million per season** in exchange for removing the exit clauses that have hung over the team all year. The clause currently gives Verstappen the right to leave between the summer break and October, since he finished the Hungarian Grand Prix weekend in **P6** in the standings — outside the top two threshold that would have kept the clause dormant. In response to the reports being shared on social media, **Jos Verstappen**, Max's father and a former F1 driver himself, flatly rejected them, posting **'You know absolutely nothing.'** The denial does not confirm or deny that talks are happening — it specifically challenges the accuracy of the reported terms, leaving observers unsure what to believe.
key_points: Red Bull is reported to have offered Max Verstappen a **one-year extension to 2029** worth around **€65 million a season**, with **no exit clauses**.
Verstappen's current contract lets him leave the team any time between the **summer break and October** if he isn't in the **top two of the standings** after the Hungarian GP.
After Hungary, Verstappen sits **P6** in the championship — meaning the exit clause is currently active and usable.
His father **Jos Verstappen** bluntly dismissed the reports on social media, writing **'You know absolutely nothing.'**
The denial leaves the F1 paddock guessing again just as Verstappen's Aston Martin and McLaren options were gathering momentum.

depth.background: Verstappen's Red Bull contract runs through **2028**, but it contains a rare **performance-linked exit clause**: if he isn't top two in the drivers' standings after the Hungarian Grand Prix, he can walk away from Red Bull between the summer break and October. That clause has fueled months of speculation since Red Bull's car has trailed **Mercedes and Ferrari** for much of 2026, with reported interest from **McLaren** and a surprise **Aston Martin** reunion with designer Adrian Newey. Red Bull, eager to keep its four-time champion, has been trying to negotiate the clause away before it can be triggered.

thread.previously: Verstappen's contract talks with McLaren were reported to have reached 'closing stages' as his Red Bull exit clause loomed, with a reunion with Adrian Newey at Aston Martin also floated as a shock third option.
thread.changed: Red Bull has now reportedly countered with a lucrative new offer to remove the exit clause entirely, but Jos Verstappen has publicly and bluntly denied the reported terms, leaving Verstappen's next move unclear.

prev_ref.title: Verstappen-McLaren contract talks reportedly reach 'closing stages' as his Red Bull exit clause looms

stories.title: Bharti Airtel reports Q1 results today, with analysts penciling in a ~45% profit jump
stories.what_happened: Bharti Airtel is set to announce its **April–June (Q1 FY27) results** on August 4, with its earnings call scheduled for the following day. Ahead of the announcement, analysts polled by financial outlets expect **net profit to jump 26–45% year-on-year**, with some estimates as high as **₹8,638.60 crore**, alongside roughly **15% revenue growth**. Brokerages are watching subscriber additions (expected around 50–60 lakh net adds for the quarter), a modest uptick in ARPU to about **₹261**, and progress in turning Airtel's heavy 5G investment into sustained profit. The results land on one of the busiest days of India's Q1 earnings season, with **114 companies** — including ONGC, Pidilite, Marico, DLF, Sun Pharma Advanced Research, Aditya Birla Capital, Bosch and Shree Cement — also due to report.
key_points: Airtel's board meets today, **August 4**, to sign off on results for the quarter ended June 30.
Analysts expect net profit to rise **26–45% year-on-year**, with some estimates near **₹8,639 crore**.
Revenue is expected to grow around **15%**, helped by steady subscriber additions and 5G rollout.
**ARPU** (average revenue per user) is forecast to tick up to roughly **₹261/month**, a key profitability gauge.
It's one of **114 companies** reporting results today as India's Q1 earnings season hits its peak, alongside ONGC, Marico and DLF.

depth.background: Bharti Airtel is India's **second-largest telecom operator** by subscribers, competing chiefly with Reliance Jio and Vodafone Idea in a market that consolidated from more than a dozen players a decade ago to effectively three. Airtel has spent heavily to roll out **5G networks** across India and has steadily raised prepaid and postpaid tariffs in recent years to improve profitability after a brutal price war in the 2010s nearly wiped out smaller rivals. ARPU — how much revenue the company earns per subscriber each month — is the industry's single most-watched number because it shows whether tariff hikes are sticking without driving customers away.

stories.title: Israel and Lebanon open a seventh round of US-brokered talks in Rome as Hezbollah calls them 'shameful'
stories.what_happened: Technical teams from Israel and Lebanon returned to Rome on **August 4** for a new round of US-brokered negotiations running through **August 6**. The talks are meant to advance the **framework peace agreement** the two countries signed last month, focusing on expanding the 'pilot zone' withdrawal-and-disarmament process and resolving outstanding **border disputes**. Lebanon's delegation, headed by diplomat Simon Karam and including military officers, ambassadors, lawyers and economic advisers, is pushing for a complete halt to Israeli military operations in southern Lebanon while talks are underway. Hezbollah publicly dismissed the negotiations as bringing "nothing but shame" on Lebanon and reiterated it will not disarm. Lebanon's prime minister hit back directly at Hezbollah, saying the group is the one that dragged the country into war in the first place. The US is pressing the Lebanese army to expand into pilot zones and the Israeli military to complete its withdrawal from them.
key_points: Technical teams meet in **Rome from August 4-6** for the **seventh round** of US-brokered talks.
Talks aim to implement a **framework peace agreement** signed last month, including phased **Israeli troop withdrawal** and Hezbollah **disarmament** in 'pilot zones'.
**Hezbollah** publicly rejected the process, calling it a source of 'nothing but shame' for Lebanon.
Lebanon's prime minister fired back, blaming Hezbollah for **dragging the country into war**.
Lebanon's delegation, led by diplomat **Simon Karam**, will demand a **full halt** to Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon during talks.

depth.background: Israel and Hezbollah fought a devastating war that ended with a ceasefire, and last month Lebanon and Israel signed a **framework agreement** meant to turn that truce into a lasting peace. The deal calls for Israel to withdraw from designated 'pilot zones' in stages while Lebanese forces disarm Hezbollah units inside them — a direct challenge to the Iran-backed group's decades-long status as an armed force operating outside the Lebanese state. Hezbollah, badly weakened in the war but still armed, has refused to accept being disarmed and calls the process illegitimate. This is now the **seventh round** of talks trying to translate that fragile framework into facts on the ground.

stories.title: Flavio Briatore wants every single F1 weekend to have a Sprint race — doubling the calendar to '24 and 24'
stories.what_happened: Speaking on **The Race podcast**, Briatore argued that Formula 1 should abandon or drastically cut back traditional Friday practice sessions — which he says offer spectators nothing worth watching, since teams just tweak car settings repeatedly — and instead hold a **Sprint race at every single Grand Prix weekend**, expanding from 6 sprints to 24. He said the alternative should be scrapping free practice altogether if it isn't going to be made more compelling for fans. Liberty Media, which owns F1, is reported to be more cautiously eyeing an expansion to around **12 Sprint weekends** over the longer term, not the full 24 Briatore wants. No change to the 2026 calendar is currently planned.
key_points: **Flavio Briatore** (Alpine's executive advisor) proposed running a **Sprint race at all 24 Grands Prix**
That's up from the current **6 Sprint weekends** per season — a four-fold expansion
He argues **Friday practice sessions** give fans nothing worth watching
**Liberty Media** (F1's owner) reportedly favors a smaller expansion, to around **12 Sprint weekends**
**No change is planned for 2026** — this is a proposal, not a confirmed rule

depth.background: A **Sprint race** is a shorter, roughly 100km race held on Saturday that gives out its own points and sets part of Sunday's grid, layered on top of F1's usual qualifying-and-race weekend format. F1 introduced Sprints in 2021 to add action to what was traditionally a quieter Friday/Saturday, and currently runs them at **6 of the season's 24 rounds**. **Flavio Briatore** is a veteran F1 team boss (previously at Renault and Benetton) now serving as Alpine's executive advisor, known for blunt, attention-grabbing proposals about the sport's direction.

stories.title: Europe's brutal heatwave sets off wildfires in Greece and France and pushes the Danube toward crisis lows
stories.what_happened: Firefighters are battling a wildfire in **Western Attica**, near Athens, that has been burning since **late July**, deploying more than 500 personnel and multiple helicopters; the effort took a tragic turn when **two helicopter crew members died** in a mid-air collision during water-dropping operations, and the fire has since jumped containment lines. In the UK, the Met Office confirmed **the driest July in almost two centuries**, deepening drought conditions. France has largely contained blazes in the Var region after weeks of fighting them, though officials warn strong winds can still cause flare-ups. Separately, the **Danube's water level has dropped to historic lows**, and Hungary came close to having to shut down its sole nuclear plant because there wasn't enough river water available for cooling — a step regulators try hard to avoid since it would strain the country's power supply.
key_points: Greece is battling a major wildfire west of Athens that has burned for **over a week**, after **two firefighting helicopter crew members died in a mid-air collision** while dropping water on it.
The UK just recorded its **driest July in nearly 200 years**, while France has managed to stop the spread of blazes in the southeastern Var region after weeks of fighting fire.
The **Danube river has hit historic low levels**, and Hungary came close to a **forced shutdown of its only nuclear power plant** because there wasn't enough river water to cool it.
Europe is warming at **more than twice the global average** since the 1980s, according to the EU's Copernicus climate service.
Strong winds in France caused flames to spread **'faster than a galloping horse'**, according to firefighters on the ground.

depth.background: Europe has spent much of this summer under an extended heat dome — weeks of unusually hot, dry weather that dries out vegetation and turns it into wildfire fuel. Greece, southern France, and Spain deal with wildfires most summers, but the **combination of prolonged heat, drought, and strong winds** this year has made blazes harder to contain, forcing water-dropping aircraft and thousands of firefighters into action across multiple countries at once. The Danube and Rhine are major European rivers that power stations, farms, and shipping all depend on; when their water runs low, it doesn't just affect drinking water but also **electricity generation**, since nuclear and coal plants use river water for cooling.

stories.title: Kerala's monsoon death toll climbs to 20 as red alert hits eight districts and thousands shelter in relief camps
stories.what_happened: India's meteorological department issued a **red alert for eight Kerala districts today**, warning of continued heavy rainfall, as the state's rain-related death toll climbed to **20** over three days of monsoon fury. **Pathanamthitta and Kottayam** districts have been hit hardest, with flooding and landslides inundating homes and cutting off infrastructure. Authorities have moved roughly **7,700 people** into about **275 relief camps**, and **five dams** are now on red alert as reservoir levels rise. Educational institutions have been shut in **10 districts** as a precaution. In neighboring Karnataka, a separate landslide has killed **3 people**, bringing the combined death toll across the two states to at least **23**, with rescue and search operations continuing for people still missing.
key_points: Kerala's rain-related death toll has risen to **20** over the past three days, with search operations still underway for missing people.
A separate landslide in **Karnataka** killed **3 more**, taking the combined southern-India toll to at least **23**.
India's weather office has issued a **red alert in eight Kerala districts** today, with **Pathanamthitta and Kottayam** worst affected.
Nearly **7,700 people** have been moved into roughly **275 relief camps** across the state.
**Five dams** are on red alert and schools are shut in **10 districts** as rain continues.

depth.background: Kerala and coastal Karnataka have been under sustained monsoon pressure for days, with earlier reporting putting the combined toll at 11 in Kerala plus 3 in a Karnataka landslide. Heavy, continuous rain since has pushed the Kerala figure alone to 20, with authorities racing to evacuate low-lying and hillside areas before more landslides hit. Kerala's hilly terrain, saturated soil from repeated rain spells, and dense population near rivers and reservoirs make it especially exposed to compounding flood and landslide risk each monsoon season.

stories.title: South Gujarat is under water: Valsad gets a metre of rain in 24 hours as NDRF scrambles
stories.what_happened: South Gujarat is facing a severe deluge, with **Valsad district recording over 100 centimetres of rainfall in a single 24-hour period** — an extreme, cloudburst-level total. The India Meteorological Department issued fresh **red alerts** for multiple districts as the rain intensified. Rivers are rising fast in **Navsari and Surat**, causing significant urban flooding in low-lying neighborhoods. State authorities have deployed the **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)** for rescue operations, and local administrations shut schools and colleges as a precaution. Forecasters expect heavy rain to continue for roughly another 18 hours, with **Dang and Tapi districts under watch for landslides**.
key_points: **Valsad district** recorded over **100 centimetres of rain in just 24 hours**.
The **IMD issued fresh red alerts** across multiple South Gujarat districts as monsoon activity intensifies.
Rivers are rising in **Navsari and Surat**, triggering significant urban flooding in low-lying areas.
**NDRF teams deployed** for rescue operations; schools and colleges shut for safety.
Forecasters warn of **heavy rain for another 18 hours**, with landslide watches for Dang and Tapi.

depth.background: India's economy and daily life run on the **southwest monsoon**, the seasonal rains that arrive from June to September and deliver most of the country's annual rainfall. Gujarat had already reported **flooding deaths and evacuations in the last week of July/early August** as heavy rain battered the state. Early August is typically a peak-intensity stretch of the monsoon, and this year's rains have already triggered major flooding in Kerala, Assam, and now Gujarat.

stories.title: IMD issues red alert for Rajasthan as a deep depression triggers major flood risk across central and western India
stories.what_happened: The IMD issued a **red alert for East Rajasthan**, its highest warning level, forecasting heavy to very heavy rainfall in the state. **Orange alerts** — the second-highest level — are in effect for Gujarat, West Rajasthan, Uttarakhand and East Madhya Pradesh, while yellow alerts cover a wide swath of states including Bihar, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Jammu & Kashmir. The system driving this is a **deep depression** that crossed the Odisha coast and is now moving inland, pumping large volumes of moisture into central India. It is combining with a separate **western disturbance** — a weather system moving in from the west that typically affects the Himalayan region — currently active over Jammu and Kashmir. The combination of the two systems is expected to strengthen rainfall across central, northwestern and western India in the coming days. Delhi-NCR itself is under a yellow alert and is expected to see continued wet weather.
key_points: India's weather office issued a **red alert for East Rajasthan**, warning of **heavy to very heavy rainfall**.
**Orange alerts** are in place for Gujarat, West Rajasthan, Uttarakhand and East Madhya Pradesh.
The trigger is a **deep depression** that crossed the Odisha coast and is pumping moisture across central India.
It's interacting with a separate **western disturbance** over the Himalayas, a combination that intensifies rainfall.
**Delhi-NCR** is under a yellow alert, with wet weather expected to continue.

depth.background: India's monsoon season, which typically runs from June to September, delivers roughly **70% of the country's annual rainfall** and is critical for agriculture, drinking water and hydropower. The India Meteorological Department (**IMD**) issues color-coded alerts — yellow (be aware), orange (be prepared), red (take action) — based on expected rainfall intensity and flood risk in each state. This year's monsoon has already caused serious flooding elsewhere, including in Assam, where floods have killed dozens of people in recent weeks. A **deep depression** — a strong low-pressure weather system, one step below a cyclone in intensity — forming over the Bay of Bengal and moving inland is a classic trigger for widespread, intense monsoon rain across central India.

stories.title: Israel's security cabinet meets as a military rift over the West Bank widens and settlers torch more Palestinian property near Nablus
stories.what_happened: Early on August 4, Israeli settlers set fire to vehicles near the villages of **Talfit and Jalud**, south of Nablus in the northern West Bank, the latest in a string of arson attacks since late July. Separately, the Palestine Red Crescent Society said a Palestinian was wounded by Israeli gunfire during an Israeli raid **east of Nablus** the same day. Israeli media also reported a **new internal dispute within the Israeli military** over how far to expand operations in the West Bank, without detailing which factions are on which side. Israel's security cabinet is scheduled to meet later today to discuss the fragile Gaza ceasefire alongside escalating tensions with Iran, putting West Bank policy on the agenda alongside two other live crises.
key_points: Israeli settlers set fire to vehicles in **Talfit and Jalud**, villages south of Nablus, in the early hours of **August 4**.
A Palestinian was wounded by Israeli gunfire during a separate raid **east of Nablus** the same day.
A **rift inside the Israeli military** has emerged over how far to expand West Bank operations.
Israel's **security cabinet** meets today to discuss both the Gaza ceasefire and rising tensions with Iran.
The UN has warned West Bank settler violence recently hit an **'all-time high.'**

depth.background: Violence in the occupied West Bank escalated sharply after a late-July firefight in the town of Tal, southwest of Nablus, that killed four Palestinians and two Israeli soldiers — each side disputing the other's account. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered a wide-scale military crackdown in response, with troops raiding towns and detaining hundreds of Palestinians, while Netanyahu said his government would accelerate legalizing existing and new Jewish settlement outposts in the West Bank. Israeli settlers have since carried out repeated arson attacks on Palestinian homes, vehicles and mosques across the region, which the United Nations says have pushed settler violence to record levels.

stories.title: Two firefighters die when a wall collapses while battling a blaze at a Greater Noida chip factory
stories.what_happened: Late on the night of **August 3**, a fire broke out at **ILGIM**, an electronics chip manufacturing company in the Ecotech-3 industrial area of Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh. At least **six fire brigade vehicles** were dispatched once the blaze was reported. While firefighters were working to put out the fire, a **wall and an iron beam inside the factory suddenly collapsed**, striking five of the firefighters. **Tirthpal Singh and Rohit Yadav died** in the collapse, while the other three injured personnel are in stable condition and being treated.
key_points: A fire broke out late Monday night at **ILGIM**, an electronics chip manufacturing unit in Greater Noida's **Ecotech-3 industrial area**.
A **wall and iron beam collapsed** on firefighters while they worked to douse the blaze, killing **2 and injuring 3 more**.
The two firefighters killed were identified as **Tirthpal Singh and Rohit Yadav**.
At least **six fire brigade vehicles** were rushed to the site once the blaze was reported.
The three injured firefighters are reported to be in **stable condition**.

depth.background: Greater Noida's **Ecotech-3** is a dense industrial zone housing electronics and manufacturing units on the outskirts of Delhi. Factory fires are a recurring hazard in India's rapidly built industrial parks, where structural safety standards and fire-response infrastructure can lag the pace of construction. Firefighters battling factory blazes routinely face risks beyond the fire itself, including structural collapse in buildings not designed to withstand prolonged heat and water exposure.

stories.title: Mick Schumacher says he now wants to stay in IndyCar through 2027, as his F1 comeback hopes fade
stories.what_happened: Mick Schumacher has said he now wants to **remain in IndyCar for the 2027 season**, having begun his rookie 2026 IndyCar campaign with Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing still holding out hope of eventually returning to Formula 1. That F1 hope took its biggest hit when Cadillac, the sport's newest team, picked **Sergio Perez and Valtteri Bottas** over him for its debut lineup. Since moving to IndyCar, Schumacher has recorded his **first top-ten finish** of the season at Nashville, and has said he is now **'100 percent' dedicated** to his IndyCar career. He has stopped short of ruling out F1 entirely, saying he **'wouldn't say no'** if a genuine opportunity appeared, but acknowledges a return is now a distant prospect.
key_points: **Mick Schumacher**, son of seven-time champion Michael Schumacher, says he wants to **remain in IndyCar for the 2027 season**.
He joined **Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing** in IndyCar for 2026 after failing to land another F1 seat when he left Haas.
His best chance at an F1 return — a seat with new team **Cadillac** — went instead to **Sergio Perez and Valtteri Bottas**.
He's already scored his **first top-ten finish** of the season, at Nashville.
He still says he **'wouldn't say no'** to an F1 return if a real opportunity arose, but admits it's now unlikely.

depth.background: Mick Schumacher raced for Haas in F1 from 2021-2022 but lost his seat and spent recent years as a reserve driver without a race seat, fueling years of on-again, off-again comeback speculation. When new F1 team **Cadillac** was building its inaugural 2026 driver lineup, Schumacher was seen as a leading candidate, but the team instead chose experienced drivers **Sergio Perez and Valtteri Bottas**. With no other F1 seat materializing, Schumacher moved to **IndyCar**, American open-wheel racing's top series, for the 2026 season — a switch that historically has made a return to F1 very rare.

stories.title: A Greek-owned bulker is hit by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, one crew member missing as fire breaks out
stories.what_happened: At around **22:00 UTC on August 3**, the crew of the **Minoan Pioneer** — a 93,283-tonne bulk carrier owned by Greece's Siena Seas and managed by Modion Maritime Management — sent a distress call reporting they'd been hit by an unknown projectile roughly 20 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, Oman. The strike hit the engine room, knocking out all power, and a fire broke out in the crew's accommodation block. The vessel's **third engineer is unaccounted for**; the rest of the crew abandoned ship and were awaiting rescue and firefighting assistance. No country or group has claimed the attack. It is the **fourth such incident close to the Musandam Peninsula in five days**, a stretch of coastline that had been considered a safer route than the main shipping lanes.
key_points: The **Minoan Pioneer**, a Liberian-flagged, Greek-owned bulk carrier, was struck by an **unidentified projectile** roughly **20 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, Oman**.
The strike hit the **engine room**, causing a total power blackout, and a **fire spread into the crew's living quarters**.
The ship's **third engineer is missing**; the rest of the crew abandoned ship and are fighting the blaze with outside help.
It is the **4th maritime security incident** near Oman's Musandam Peninsula in just **five days**, and no group has claimed responsibility.
It comes hours after **Trump gave Iran a 'last chance'** to sign a deal or face strikes — showing the threat is already spilling onto commercial shipping.

depth.background: The **Strait of Hormuz** is the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman that roughly **one-fifth of the world's oil** passes through by tanker. Tensions over it have escalated for weeks as the US and Iran traded threats and Trump moved to blockade Iranian oil exports; several vessels have already been abandoned or attacked in the area this year. Iran had separately said a deal with Oman to open an alternate shipping route through Omani waters was in its 'final stages,' a sign both sides know how economically damaging a closed or contested Strait would be. This attack undercuts that diplomatic track by hitting a ship on the supposedly 'neutral' Omani coastal route.

thread.previously: Trump had threatened strikes aimed at Iran's leadership if it didn't sign a deal, while Iran said a shipping-route deal with Oman was in its 'final stages.'
thread.changed: A commercial ship has now actually been hit on the supposedly safe Omani route, with a crew member missing — the conflict has moved from threats to a real attack on shipping.

stories.title: Shafique and Babar Azam century stands haul Pakistan back into the 2nd Test after West Indies' 344
stories.what_happened: After Pakistan's bowlers dismissed West Indies for **344** — Justin Greaves (73) and Roston Chase (70) leading the recovery, with spinner **Sajid Khan** taking **4 for 85** — Pakistan's reply started shakily before Shafique and Babar Azam dug in. **Abdullah Shafique reached his sixth Test century (107 not out)**, while **Babar Azam batted to an unbeaten 86**, edging closer to what would be his first Test hundred in four years. Together they built an unbroken **168-run partnership** that carried Pakistan to **266 for 2** at the close of Day 2 — leaving them just **78 runs** behind West Indies' first-innings total with eight wickets still in hand, putting Pakistan firmly back in a series-deciding Test they needed to win.
key_points: West Indies were bowled out for **344** — Justin Greaves (73) and Roston Chase (70) top-scored.
Pakistan's **Sajid Khan** took 4/85 with spin to help wrap up the innings.
**Abdullah Shafique** made his **sixth Test century** (107 not out) opening the batting.
**Babar Azam** was unbeaten on **86**, closing in on his first Test century in four years.
Shafique and Babar's unbeaten **168-run stand** left Pakistan just **78 runs behind** at Day 2's close.

depth.background: This is the **second and final Test** of Pakistan's tour of the West Indies, played at Port of Spain's **Queen's Park Oval** — a series-decider after the first Test finished level. **Babar Azam**, Pakistan's long-time talisman and former captain, has endured a well-documented **four-year century drought** in Test cricket, making this innings a personal comeback story as much as a team one. **Abdullah Shafique** has quietly become Pakistan's most reliable opener over the same stretch.

In reply, Pakistan's openers turned the game around: Abdullah Shafique made a century and Babar Azam batted his way to 86 not out, an unbeaten 168-run stand that took Pakistan to 266/2 at Day 2's close — just 78 runs behind, with the series on the line.

stories.title: Welsh Fire chase down Southern Brave with five balls to spare in The Hundred
stories.what_happened: **Welsh Fire** beat **Southern Brave** by **6 wickets** at Sophia Gardens in Cardiff on **August 3**, with 5 balls to spare. Batting first, Southern Brave were restricted to **115 for 8** in their 100 balls. Welsh Fire chased the target down comfortably, reaching **116 for 4** off 95 balls to seal the win. The result strengthens Welsh Fire's position as the group stage of the 2026 competition heads into its final rounds. The Hundred's knockout stage follows shortly after, with the **Eliminator on August 14** between the second- and third-placed teams, and the **Final at Lord's on August 16**.
key_points: **Welsh Fire** beat **Southern Brave** by **6 wickets**, with 5 balls remaining, at Cardiff.
Southern Brave were restricted to **115/8** batting first.
Welsh Fire chased the target down, finishing on **116/4** off 95 balls.
The win keeps Welsh Fire firmly in contention as **The Hundred's** group stage nears its end.
The tournament's knockouts begin with the **Eliminator on August 14** and the **Final at Lord's on August 16**.

depth.background: **The Hundred** is England's 100-ball franchise cricket tournament, launched in 2021 to attract new fans with a shorter, simplified format than traditional T20 cricket. Eight city-based men's and women's teams compete each summer, with the top three finishers in the group stage advancing to the knockouts — the second- and third-placed teams play an eliminator, with the winner facing the top team in the final. **Welsh Fire**, based in Cardiff, and **Southern Brave** are two of the tournament's eight men's franchises.

stories.title: Trump gives Iran a 'last chance' to sign a deal — or face strikes aimed at 'decapitating' its leadership
stories.what_happened: Speaking from the Oval Office, Trump told reporters Iran has **one final opportunity** to reach a peace deal before the US resumes large-scale strikes — this time explicitly aimed at Iran's leadership, command infrastructure and critical facilities, not just military assets. He said Middle East allies had asked him to hold off on new airstrikes to give diplomacy 'one more shot,' and that any deal should move in two phases, starting with reopening the Strait of Hormuz to shipping. Trump insisted negotiations were **'going on right now,'** but Iran's government has publicly and repeatedly denied that any talks are actually taking place, instead saying it is negotiating only with Oman over how ships pass through the strait. The contradiction — Washington claiming active talks, Tehran denying them — is now in its second straight day.
key_points: Trump says Iran has **one last chance** to sign a peace deal before facing large-scale strikes.

The threatened strikes would target Iran's **leadership, command infrastructure, and key facilities** — the same 'decapitation' logic used in February's strike that killed Supreme Leader **Ali Khamenei**.
He wants a **two-phase deal**, starting with reopening the **Strait of Hormuz**, the oil chokepoint Iran has been targeting since late July.
Trump insists talks are happening **'right now'** — but Iran's government keeps publicly denying that any session is underway.
This is a sharp escalation from Sunday, when Trump had paused a planned attack, citing progress toward a deal.

depth.background: The US and Israel have been at war with Iran for months, a conflict that escalated in late July when Iran began targeting oil tankers to effectively choke off the **Strait of Hormuz** — the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman that roughly a fifth of the world's daily oil supply passes through. In February 2026, a US strike codenamed Operation Epic Fury killed Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, a 'decapitation' strike against the regime's top leadership. Trump has repeatedly threatened to repeat that approach if Iran doesn't negotiate, while Gulf states have pushed hard for a diplomatic off-ramp instead.

thread.previously: We reported that Trump said direct US-Iran talks would begin Monday afternoon to nail down a deal on a 'total' reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and an end to Iran's nuclear program — but Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson denied any immediate plan for talks, saying Tehran was negotiating only with Oman.
thread.changed: Trump has now escalated from announcing talks to issuing an explicit ultimatum: sign a deal or face strikes aimed at 'decapitating' Iran's leadership, echoing the February strike that killed Khamenei. Iran is still denying that real negotiations are underway.
