stories.title: 25 Democratic-led states sue Trump over new tariffs, calling them a 'pretext' for taxes the Supreme Court already struck down
stories.what_happened: On **Monday, August 3**, a coalition of **25 states** — led by New York and including California, Illinois, Michigan and Pennsylvania — filed suit in the **US Court of International Trade**, arguing that tariffs the administration announced on **July 23** covering more than **80 countries** are illegal. The new tariffs, ranging from **10% to 12.5%**, were imposed using **Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1930**, a law that lets the president respond to specific unfair foreign trade practices, unlike the emergency law the Supreme Court had already struck down. The states argue the administration is simply using Section 301 as a substitute to reimpose the same sweeping, country-wide tariffs the courts already rejected, without doing the country-by-country investigations the law requires. Separately, the administration also invoked **Section 338** of a 1930 tariff law to hit Canada with **50% tariffs** on autos, alcohol and dairy, in a dispute over Canadian trade practices — a move that takes effect **August 19**. The lawsuit asks the court to block the new tariffs entirely and order refunds of duties already collected.
key_points: A coalition of **25 states** sued the Trump administration Monday over its latest round of tariffs.
The suit says the tariffs use **Section 301** as a workaround for tariffs the **Supreme Court already rejected**.
The rejected tariffs relied on the **IEEPA emergency law**, which the Court ruled doesn't let a president impose them.
This is the **third lawsuit** the same multi-state coalition has filed against Trump's tariffs since April 2025.
The states want the new tariffs blocked and **duties already paid refunded**.

depth.background: Since taking office, President Trump has used emergency and trade-law powers to impose sweeping tariffs — taxes on imported goods — on dozens of countries, arguing they protect American industry and jobs. A coalition of mostly Democratic-led states first sued in **April 2025**, arguing he had no legal authority to impose blanket tariffs using the **International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA)**, a law meant for genuine national emergencies, not routine trade policy. In **February 2026**, the **US Supreme Court agreed**, ruling IEEPA does not give the president that power. Rather than drop the tariffs, the administration reissued similar ones in July using a different law — Section 301 of the Trade Act — which is what triggered this third lawsuit.

stories.title: Amazon becomes the 5th company ever to hit a $3 trillion market value, riding an AI-cloud earnings beat
stories.what_happened: Amazon shares hit an all-time high near **$285** on Monday, August 3, giving the company a market capitalization of roughly **$3.08 trillion** and making it the fifth company in history — after Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia and Alphabet — to cross that threshold. The rally followed Amazon's second-quarter earnings report, in which **AWS revenue grew 36.7% year-over-year**, its fastest expansion in 18 quarters, driven by surging demand for AI computing capacity. Amazon reported adjusted earnings per share of **$1.97** versus the $1.82 analysts expected, on revenue of **$200.61 billion** against a $196.47 billion estimate. The company is now projecting **$220 billion** in 2026 capital expenditure, up from its earlier $200 billion forecast, as it races to build out AI and data-center infrastructure. The stock's gains over Friday and Monday's sessions combined topped **20%**.
key_points: Amazon's stock closed up **4%** on Monday, pushing its market value to about **$3.08 trillion**.
It's only the **5th company** ever to cross $3 trillion, after Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia and Alphabet.
The stock's **two-session gain topped 20%**, following a ~15% jump on Friday after Q2 earnings.
Cloud unit **AWS grew revenue 36.7% year-over-year** — its fastest pace in 18 quarters.
Amazon now expects **$220 billion in capital spending** this year, up from a $200 billion forecast in February.

depth.background: Amazon started as an online bookseller in **1994** and has grown into one of the world's largest companies through e-commerce, cloud computing (AWS), advertising and logistics. AWS, launched in **2006**, is Amazon's most profitable division and effectively rents out computing power and storage to other businesses — including the AI boom's biggest players, who need vast server capacity to train and run AI models. The **$3 trillion market-cap club** is an informal but closely watched milestone reserved for the world's most valuable public companies.

stories.title: Trump's own DOJ drops vandalism charges against 4 people accused of damaging the Lincoln Memorial pool — and Trump is furious about it
stories.what_happened: Pirro's office filed a motion to dismiss the case against Hearn, stating that the damage was actually caused by a **botched sealant installation**, not deliberate vandalism. Since the previous Friday, her office had already dropped charges against three other defendants — **Justin Carreno, Sophie Dennison-Gibby, and Cameron Thiers**. The filing says the sealant began peeling almost immediately after the pool's renovation was completed, and that the Department of the Interior did not give prosecutors the full picture when the case was first built. President Trump publicly criticized Pirro over the decision, saying she **'choked'** and made a mistake, and insisting the pool damage was still the work of vandals.
key_points: US Attorney **Jeanine Pirro** moved to dismiss charges against Olympic canoeist **David Hearn** and 3 others
DOJ's own filing says the damage came from **'flawed installation'** by a contractor, not vandalism
Sealant lining the Reflecting Pool's bottom had **'almost immediately' started peeling** after a renovation
**President Trump** publicly said Pirro **'folded like an umbrella'** and insisted vandals were to blame
Interior Department gave **'less than fulsome information'** at the outset of the case, per the DOJ motion

depth.background: Several people, including former Olympic canoeist David Hearn, were charged this year with vandalizing the Lincoln Memorial's Reflecting Pool in Washington, DC — a case the administration had held up as an example of cracking down on destruction of federal monuments. Jeanine Pirro, the Trump-appointed **US Attorney for the District of Columbia**, is the prosecutor who brought and is now unwinding the case. The pool had recently been renovated, and investigators have since found the sealant on its floor was already failing before any of the accused was even near it.

stories.title: India loses pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah for the entire Sri Lanka Test series with a knee injury
stories.what_happened: Bumrah sustained a **left knee injury** while fielding during the **second ODI against England** in Cardiff, and the discomfort forced him to sit out the series-deciding match at **Lord's**. He underwent assessment at the BCCI's **Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru on July 30**, where his fitness was measured at around **95%**, but the medical team determined he wasn't ready for the physical demands of Test cricket. Despite some discussion about him potentially joining the squad later for the **second Test in Colombo** if his recovery sped up, the **BCCI confirmed on Monday, August 3** that he will miss the series entirely, and uncapped pacer **Auqib Nabi** has been added to the squad as cover.
key_points: **Jasprit Bumrah** has been ruled out of India's **two-match Test series in Sri Lanka**, starting **August 15**, due to a **left knee injury**.
He was hurt while **fielding during the 2nd ODI against England** in Cardiff, and had already missed the series-deciding ODI at Lord's.
Bumrah was assessed at the **BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru on July 30**, and doctors decided not to rush his return.
Uncapped fast bowler **Auqib Nabi** has been named as his replacement in the squad.
There had been talk of Bumrah joining for the **second Test in Colombo** if he recovered faster, but the BCCI confirmed his recovery is taking longer than hoped.

depth.background: Jasprit Bumrah is India's **premier fast bowler** and has been managed carefully by the BCCI in recent years due to a history of back and workload-related issues, so any fresh injury draws close scrutiny. India is preparing for a **two-match Test series in Sri Lanka** as part of its build-up in the World Test Championship cycle, and losing its most important bowler is a significant blow to the squad's balance heading in.

stories.title: India's rupee grinds toward record lows as the RBI keeps selling dollars to defend it
stories.what_happened: The rupee was trading around **95.29 to the dollar** on August 3, down more than **8% over the past year**, even after a modest one-month recovery. Traders pointed to **continued RBI dollar-selling** to slow the decline, following what they described as aggressive intervention in the prior session. Market participants cautioned that further rupee strength could be capped if oil prices rebound amid the ongoing **US-Iran standoff**, since India imports the vast majority of the crude it consumes.
key_points: The rupee traded near **95.29 per dollar** on August 3 — down **over 8% in the past year**.
Traders say the **RBI intervened aggressively**, selling dollars to slow the currency's slide.
India's **forex reserves — the RBI's war chest** — have been falling as it defends the rupee.
The pressure is tied to **Trump's tariffs on Indian goods** and fears of rising oil prices from US-Iran tensions.
A weak rupee makes India's imports — especially **oil** — more expensive, feeding inflation.

depth.background: The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** doesn't fix the rupee's value, but it does step in — buying or selling dollars — to stop moves it sees as too sharp or disorderly. It has been under pressure for weeks: the US has layered fresh **tariffs on Indian exports** this year (part of a wider round of tariffs on dozens of countries), and Gulf tensions have kept a floor under oil prices, which matters hugely for India since it imports most of its crude.

stories.title: Prashant Kishor's Jan Suraaj wins its first big Bihar seat as bypoll results split three ways
stories.what_happened: Vote counting concluded on **August 3** for bypolls in three states. In Bihar's **Bankipur** constituency, Jan Suraaj's Prashant Kishor defeated BJP's Neeraj Kumar Sinha by more than **19,000 votes**, polling **63,203 votes** to Sinha's **44,250**, with RJD's Rekha Kumari trailing in third with about 14,000. In **Madhya Pradesh's Datia** seat, Congress won, and in **Gujarat's Manjalpur** seat, BJP retained control as expected. The Bankipur seat had fallen vacant after sitting BJP MLA and state party president Nitin Nabin was elected to the Rajya Sabha in April.
key_points: **Prashant Kishor's Jan Suraaj Party** won its first big electoral test, taking Bankipur in Patna.
Kishor beat BJP's Neeraj Kumar Sinha by more than **19,000 votes** (63,203 to 44,250).
RJD finished a distant **third** with around 14,000 votes — a blow to the opposition's Bihar strategy too.
**Congress won Datia** (Madhya Pradesh) and **BJP retained Manjalpur** (Gujarat) — no upsets there.
The seat opened up after BJP's state president **Nitin Nabin** vacated it to join the Rajya Sabha.

depth.background: **Jan Suraaj** ('Good Governance') is the political party launched by election strategist **Prashant Kishor** — the man who has advised winning campaigns for Congress, BJP, and several regional parties over the years — after he decided to build his own party in Bihar rather than keep working behind the scenes for others. Bankipur, a BJP stronghold in Patna represented by the party's own state president until he moved to the Rajya Sabha (parliament's upper house), was seen as a tough test: a symbolic win here for Jan Suraaj would signal it can actually convert Kishor's strategist fame into real votes, not just headlines.

thread.changed: The results are in: Jan Suraaj's Prashant Kishor won Bankipur decisively, defeating the BJP candidate by more than 19,000 votes — a landmark first major win for his two-year-old party. The other two seats split along expected lines: Congress won Datia in Madhya Pradesh, and BJP retained Manjalpur in Gujarat.

stories.title: Karnataka finally completes its Congress cabinet — with no woman minister and two resignations in protest
stories.what_happened: On Monday, **Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot** administered the oath of office to 19 new ministers at a ceremony at **Lok Bhavan in Bengaluru at 5 pm**. The Congress high command had actually cleared **20 names**, but Bhatkal MLA Mankal S Vaidya was dropped at the last minute to accommodate senior leader S S Mallikarjun, and MLC Gayathri Shanthegowda — the only woman on the list — was held back over a **pending Supreme Court-linked dispute over her own Council seat**, leaving the cabinet with no woman at all. The final lineup gives Lingayats and Vokkaligas 7 and 5 berths respectively, creates a first-ever slate of 7 SC ministers spanning different sub-categories, includes 3 ST ministers, and hands 3 Cabinet posts plus a top legislative post to Muslim leaders. Senior leaders including H K Patil, Dinesh Gundu Rao, Lakshmi Hebbalkar and N S Boseraju were **dropped from the ministry entirely**. Alongside the ministers, **GS Patil was named Assembly Speaker**, AS Ponnanna Deputy Speaker, and Saleem Ahmed Chairperson of the Legislative Council. Within hours, at least **two Congress MLAs resigned their party organisational posts** in protest at being excluded, and Shivakumar publicly promised disappointed MLAs "future chances."
key_points: **19 of 20 cleared MLAs** were sworn in as ministers, taking Chief Minister **DK Shivakumar's council to its full strength of 34**
The expansion came **nearly two months** after Shivakumar became CM under Congress's internal power-sharing deal with Siddaramaiah
The new council has **zero women ministers** — the one woman on the approved list was dropped over a pending legal case on her seat
Berths were split along caste lines: **7 Lingayat, 5 Vokkaliga, 7 Scheduled Caste and 3 Scheduled Tribe** ministers
**Two Congress MLAs resigned party posts** after being left out, and several senior leaders were dropped entirely

depth.background: Congress swept back to power in Karnataka in 2023 on the strength of an internal deal: **Siddaramaiah would be Chief Minister first**, and hand over to his rival **DK Shivakumar roughly halfway through the five-year term**. That handover happened on **June 3, 2026**, when Shivakumar was sworn in with just 13 ministers — a skeletal team meant to be a placeholder. Filling the remaining berths meant satisfying competing claims from Karnataka's powerful **Lingayat and Vokkaliga** communities, Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe legislators, Muslim leaders, and MLAs from every region of the state, which is why the full expansion took two more months of negotiation.

stories.title: Rajya Sabha passes bill giving small businesses real teeth to force overdue payments — as opposition disrupts the House over Amit Shah
stories.what_happened: The Rajya Sabha passed the **MSME Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026** by voice vote on Monday. The bill makes arbitral awards in favour of small businesses **enforceable as arrears of land revenue** and recognises them as legally binding debt under the **Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code**, giving suppliers a much faster route to actually collect what they're owed. Buyers who want to challenge an award in court must first **deposit 75% of the awarded amount**, and if their case is still pending after **six months**, courts can direct that **at least half the award be released** to the MSME supplier right away. States also get more flexibility in how they staff their Facilitation Councils, and the bill mandates that these councils be properly resourced and digitised so cases don't pile up. The bill's passage happened even as opposition MPs kept up **sustained sloganeering** in the House, demanding Home Minister **Amit Shah** explain the police crackdown — including use of pellet guns — on students protesting a NEET paper-leak issue at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on **July 20**, and address separate allegations of donation theft at the Ram temple in Ayodhya. TMC's Sagarika Ghose and Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge were among those demanding the Prime Minister and Home Minister address the House directly.
key_points: The **MSME Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026** passed the Rajya Sabha by voice vote, targeting India's chronic **late-payment problem** for small firms
A buyer challenging an arbitration award must now **deposit 75% of the amount** before a court will even hear their appeal
If that appeal drags on **past six months**, courts can order **at least 50% of the award** paid to the small business immediately
Unpaid awards become recoverable like **arrears of land revenue** — the same fast-track tool used to collect unpaid tax
MSMEs contribute **over 31% of India's GDP** and employ close to **39 crore people**, according to government data cited by ministers

depth.background: India's Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 already required large buyers to pay small suppliers within **45 days**, with unpaid disputes going to state-level **Facilitation Councils** for arbitration. In practice, buyers routinely dragged out that process for years by challenging awards in court, starving small businesses of cash they were legally owed. Union MSME Minister **Jitan Ram Manjhi** introduced this amendment bill in the Rajya Sabha on **July 29** specifically to close that loophole, calling it "the need of the present time." The bill passed today, during the Monsoon Session of Parliament.

stories.title: Kimi Antonelli builds a commanding 50-point championship lead as Verstappen can now formally trigger his Red Bull exit clause
stories.what_happened: After 11 rounds of the 2026 season, rookie Kimi Antonelli sits atop the F1 drivers' championship with **219 points**, a commanding **50-point lead** over second-placed Lewis Hamilton on 169, with George Russell third on 160. Antonelli's tally includes **six race wins and three further podiums**, a remarkable return for a driver in his first full F1 season. Meanwhile, Max Verstappen's underwhelming campaign at Red Bull means he has now missed the top-two standings threshold his contract required by the summer break, which formally activates an **exit clause** letting him leave the team for 2027 if he chooses. Verstappen's manager has publicly stated the four-time champion still intends to see out his Red Bull contract, despite persistent rumours linking him to Mercedes, McLaren, and even a reunion with designer Adrian Newey at Aston Martin.
key_points: Rookie **Kimi Antonelli** leads the F1 drivers' championship with **219 points** after 11 rounds.
He holds a **50-point lead** over Lewis Hamilton (169) and a bigger gap to George Russell (160).
Antonelli has taken **six grand prix wins and three podiums** in his debut season.
**Max Verstappen** can now formally trigger the exit clause in his Red Bull contract, after missing a top-two standings threshold by the summer break.
Verstappen's manager insists he still intends to **honor his Red Bull contract** despite the swirling exit rumours.

depth.background: Kimi Antonelli, a teenage Mercedes rookie, has had one of the most dominant debut seasons in modern F1 history, a stark contrast to Max Verstappen's uncharacteristically difficult campaign at Red Bull, the team he has won four consecutive world titles with. Verstappen's contract reportedly contains a **performance-linked exit clause** — a condition that lets him leave early if the team fails to keep him competitive for the title, specifically requiring a top-two standings position by the summer break to keep him bound to the deal. With Red Bull enduring what could be Verstappen's least competitive season since he joined the team, that clause has become the center of the sport's driver-market speculation this summer.

thread.changed: The clause has now formally activated after Verstappen missed the required top-two standings position by the summer break, and fresh standings data shows just how large the gap to championship leader Antonelli has grown, even as Verstappen's manager insists he intends to stay.

stories.title: A reunion with Adrian Newey at Aston Martin becomes a shock third option for Verstappen's 2027 future
stories.what_happened: F1 insiders are now floating a reunion between Verstappen and Newey at Aston Martin as a serious third option for the four-time champion's 2027 future, alongside the Mercedes and McLaren interest already being reported. One longtime F1 analyst argued that having Newey at the helm makes the Aston Martin project more attractive than joining a rival that's merely competitive. The speculation is fueled by Verstappen's current sixth-place championship standing, which has triggered the performance clause in his Red Bull deal, giving him a real opening to leave if he chooses. Verstappen's own future is expected to become clearer at his home race, the Dutch Grand Prix, when the sport returns from its summer break in three weeks.
key_points: Insiders are urging Max Verstappen to consider **reuniting with Adrian Newey** at Aston Martin for 2027.
This adds a **third option** alongside already-reported Mercedes and McLaren interest.
Verstappen currently sits **sixth** in the championship, which **triggers a performance clause** in his Red Bull contract.

Verstappen is expected to **clarify his future** at his home Dutch Grand Prix in three weeks.

depth.background: Max Verstappen is contracted to Red Bull through 2028, but that contract includes a performance-linked exit clause that can be triggered if he falls outside the top positions in the championship — which he currently has, sitting sixth. Design chief Adrian Newey, widely regarded as one of F1's greatest car designers, left Red Bull last year and has since taken on both team principal and technical partner roles at Aston Martin, where he has been steadily rebuilding the team's technical foundations.

stories.title: The largest cyclospora outbreak on record just claimed its first two US deaths, in Michigan
stories.what_happened: Michigan health officials announced on **Monday, August 3** that two people died after becoming ill with cyclosporiasis, marking the **first US deaths** confirmed in this year's outbreak; officials said both had serious pre-existing health conditions that dehydration from the illness likely worsened. The CDC says it has received **6,707 laboratory-confirmed, domestically acquired cases** since May 1, with more than **11,500 additional cases** reported but not yet confirmed — spread across **45 states**. Michigan has been hit hardest, logging **11,234 cases and 193 hospitalizations**; Ohio has reported over 4,000 cases and Indiana nearly 1,349. A related but separate cluster tied to **recalled Taylor Farms iceberg lettuce**, pulled from shelves in mid-July after being traced to a Mexican grower, has sickened at least **1,947 people** with **98 hospitalizations**, including illnesses linked to bagged salads and fast-food chains like Taco Bell.
key_points: Michigan confirmed the **first two US deaths** tied to this year's cyclospora outbreak, both patients with **significant underlying health conditions**.
The CDC has logged **6,707 confirmed cases** since May 1, plus over **11,500 more** still unconfirmed or under investigation — already the **largest cyclosporiasis outbreak on record**.
Cases have turned up in **45 US states**, with Michigan alone reporting **11,234 cases and 193 hospitalizations**.
A separate, related outbreak tied to **recalled iceberg lettuce** from a Taylor Farms supplier in Mexico has sickened at least **1,947 people**, including cases served at **Taco Bell**.
Cyclospora is a **microscopic parasite** spread through contaminated produce and water — not through person-to-person contact.

depth.background: **Cyclosporiasis** is an intestinal infection caused by the parasite *Cyclospora cayetanensis*, typically picked up from fresh produce — herbs, berries and leafy greens are common culprits — that was grown, washed, or handled with contaminated water. US cases normally ramp up every summer as imported fresh produce increases, but usually stay under **4,000 cases a year**; this year's case count has already blown past that. In mid-July, **Taylor Farms recalled iceberg lettuce** sourced from central Mexico after it was linked to illnesses, but health officials say that recall doesn't account for the full scope of this year's much larger, multi-state outbreak.

stories.title: A Kuki-Zo civil body gives Manipur's government 48 hours before threatening a total shutdown
stories.what_happened: The **Working Committee of Kuki Civil Society Organisations (WCKCSOs)-Ukhrul** issued a **48-hour ultimatum** to the Manipur government, demanding it end what the group calls a selective blockade that has allowed essential commodities bound for Kuki-Zo inhabited areas to be **confiscated and burned**. The group warned of a **total shutdown starting August 5** if the government does not directly address the issue. This follows the same body's own **counter economic blockade on National Highway-202**, in force since midnight of July 26, which it says will continue until the government guarantees free movement of essential goods — though it has carved out exemptions for medical emergencies, passenger travel, airport-bound travelers and security forces. Separately, a blockade on **National Highway-2** by Naga and Meitei groups near Senapati and Kanglatongbi has continued for nearly a month without effective government intervention.
key_points: The **WCKCSOs-Ukhrul**, a Kuki civil society body, has given the state government **48 hours** to end an alleged blockade on supplies to Kuki-Zo areas.
It has threatened a **total shutdown from August 5** if the issue isn't directly addressed.
The group accuses authorities of allowing the **confiscation and burning** of essential commodities headed to Kuki-Zo villages.
It follows a **counter economic blockade on National Highway-202** the same group imposed from July 26.
A separate blockade by Naga and Meitei groups on **National Highway-2** has continued for nearly a month with little government intervention.

depth.background: Manipur has been gripped by **ethnic conflict between the Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities since May 2023**, which killed hundreds and displaced tens of thousands, splitting the state into informally segregated zones. Kuki-Zo areas in the hills depend heavily on national highways passing through Meitei-dominated valley areas for essential supplies like food, fuel and medicine, making these highways frequent flashpoints and leverage points for both communities. Civil society organisations on both sides — rather than only political parties — have increasingly driven blockades and counter-blockades as a form of protest and pressure on the government.

stories.title: Tilak Varma named South Zone captain as BCCI announces Duleep Trophy 2026-27 squads
stories.what_happened: The BCCI announced squads for the **2026-27 Duleep Trophy**, with **Tilak Varma**, India's T20I vice-captain, named captain of South Zone and **Ricky Bhui** as his deputy. The South Zone squad also features experienced batter **Karun Nair** alongside a mix of domestic regulars. Separately, **Rajat Patidar** was confirmed as Central Zone's captain for the tournament. The competition — one of Indian cricket's oldest first-class events — will be held at the **BCCI Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru from August 23 to September 10**, giving contracted players a red-ball tune-up before India's international season resumes with the Sri Lanka Test tour later in August.
key_points: India T20I vice-captain **Tilak Varma** will lead South Zone in the season-opening Duleep Trophy.
**Ricky Bhui** is named vice-captain, with veteran **Karun Nair** also included in the 15-man squad.
**Rajat Patidar** has been named captain of Central Zone for the tournament.
The tournament runs **August 23 to September 10** at the BCCI Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru.
It's a first competitive red-ball assignment for several contracted India players before the international season resumes.

depth.background: The **Duleep Trophy** is one of Indian domestic cricket's oldest first-class tournaments, contested between zonal teams (North, South, East, West, Central) and traditionally used by selectors to assess players' red-ball form outside the more famous Ranji Trophy. It's often a proving ground for fringe India players and a place for established internationals to sharpen their game between series. Handing an India T20I vice-captain like Tilak Varma a first-class leadership role signals selectors see him as a longer-term leadership prospect, not just a white-ball specialist.

stories.title: IBM says it has finally proven 'quantum advantage' — and is daring rivals to disprove it
stories.what_happened: IBM, working with the **University of Chicago**, **RIKEN** in Japan, and quantum-software firms **Qedma, BlueQubit and Algorithmiq**, published three papers this week describing experiments it says clear the bar for genuine **'quantum advantage'** — the point where a quantum computer is confirmed to outperform classical computers on a trusted, checkable task. In the headline experiment, IBM's hardware completed a calculation in **about 15 minutes** using **70 error-corrected logical qubits**, executing **2,415 logical two-qubit operations**, at an error rate roughly **ten times lower** than the raw physical hardware — a result IBM says no classical simulation method could reproduce in a practical timeframe. In a second experiment, IBM combined a **77-qubit Heron chip** with **all 152,064 nodes of Japan's Fugaku supercomputer** to calculate the electronic structure of iron-sulfur clusters, a notoriously hard materials-chemistry problem, working alongside the Cleveland Clinic on a related 300-atom molecular simulation. IBM has submitted every circuit and result to a public tracker so outside scientists can attempt to beat the quantum result classically — a direct invitation to have the claim stress-tested rather than taken on faith.
key_points: IBM and the **University of Chicago** ran a computation on a quantum computer in about **15 minutes** that would take leading classical supercomputers **prohibitively long** to match.
The team encoded **70 logical qubits** using a new error-correction method — one of the **largest logical-qubit demonstrations** ever run.
A separate IBM experiment paired a **77-qubit Heron processor** with Japan's **Fugaku supercomputer** (all 152,064 of its nodes) to model a hard materials-science problem.
Unlike past 'quantum supremacy' claims, IBM has published the full circuits and **invited outside researchers to try to refute the results**.
IBM still says a **large-scale, fully fault-tolerant** quantum computer — one that could break real-world encryption — is not expected until **2029**.

depth.background: For over a decade, quantum computers have been a research curiosity: physically real, but not yet able to beat an ordinary supercomputer at anything useful, because quantum bits ('qubits') are extremely error-prone and lose their state ("decohere") almost instantly. Google and others have previously claimed narrow, lab-only 'quantum supremacy' wins on contrived math problems with little practical value, and those claims were sometimes later matched by improved classical algorithms. IBM's new claim is different in kind: it says the results are on a **useful, verifiable** class of problem, backed by a public 'Quantum Advantage Tracker' where any team can try to reproduce the result classically and prove IBM wrong.

stories.title: Aiden Markram plays down talk he'll be named Lucknow Super Giants' next IPL captain
stories.what_happened: Asked directly about the vacant LSG captaincy on Monday, Aiden Markram said, **'I've got no idea,'** adding that the decision belongs to the franchise: **'They can decide whatever they think is best. There are some quality leaders in that group that we have there, so I'm not too fussed about it.'** He said 'the thoughts haven't been there just yet' on his own candidacy, despite being widely seen as a frontrunner given his experience captaining South Africa's T20 side. The vacancy opened after Rishabh Pant's trade to Delhi Capitals for Kuldeep Yadav left LSG without its previous leader. Mitchell Marsh, Australia's T20I captain and another senior figure in LSG's squad, is viewed as the other realistic contender for the role.
key_points: **Aiden Markram** downplayed speculation he'll take over as **Lucknow Super Giants (LSG)** captain for the next IPL season.
The captaincy question opened up after **Rishabh Pant** stepped down and was **traded to Delhi Capitals** for Kuldeep Yadav.
Markram said 'the thoughts haven't been there just yet' and pointed to **other 'quality leaders'** in the squad.
Australia's T20I captain **Mitchell Marsh**, also on LSG's roster, is seen as the other obvious contender.
Markram is South Africa's own **T20 captain**, making him a natural favorite despite his reluctance to commit.

depth.background: Rishabh Pant had captained Lucknow Super Giants, but he was traded to Delhi Capitals in exchange for spinner Kuldeep Yadav, leaving the IPL franchise without a permanent leader heading into its next campaign. Markram, South Africa's white-ball captain, is widely regarded as a natural choice given his existing captaincy credentials, but LSG also has Australia's T20I captain Mitchell Marsh on its roster as an alternative option.

stories.title: Supreme Court rejects Brinda Karat's bid to reopen the 'goli maaro' hate-speech clean chit for two BJP leaders
stories.what_happened: Brinda Karat, a senior CPI(M) leader, had asked the Supreme Court to review its own April 29, 2026 judgment, arguing the Court reached its conclusion **without a detailed examination of the evidence** or full arguments on the merits of the alleged hate speech. She pointed to the Election Commission's own January 2020 findings that the speeches had the potential to **'aggravate existing differences and promote mutual hatred between religious communities.'** On Monday, a bench of Justices **Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta** dismissed the review plea, finding **no apparent error** in the original ruling and declining Karat's request for an open-court hearing — meaning the case was decided on paperwork alone rather than live arguments. The dismissal makes the April clean chit to Thakur and Verma final, with no further review avenue within the Supreme Court itself.
key_points: The Supreme Court **dismissed a review petition** filed by CPI(M) leader **Brinda Karat** against its own April ruling.
That April ruling gave a **clean chit** to BJP leaders **Anurag Thakur and Parvesh Verma** over 2020 Delhi election hate-speech allegations.
Justices **Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta** found **no error** in the earlier judgment and declined an open-court hearing.
Karat had cited **Election Commission orders** from January 2020 that found the speeches violated the Model Code of Conduct.
The case centers on the infamous **'goli maaro saalon ko' ('shoot the traitors')** slogan controversy from the 2020 Delhi campaign.

depth.background: During campaigning for the 2020 Delhi Assembly election, BJP leaders including Union minister Anurag Thakur and MP Parvesh Verma made speeches that critics said incited violence against a religious minority — including a crowd chant of 'goli maaro saalon ko,' or 'shoot the traitors.' The Election Commission at the time found the speeches breached the Model Code of Conduct and temporarily barred both men from campaigning. Years later, in April 2026, the Supreme Court ruled that the speeches did not disclose a 'cognisable offence' — meaning no crime serious enough to require police investigation without a magistrate's order — effectively clearing the two leaders of criminal liability.

stories.title: Lewis Hamilton says a race engineer he'd 'never spoken to' before this year reignited his love of F1 after his first Ferrari win
stories.what_happened: Lewis Hamilton has opened up about his relationship with race engineer Carlo Santi, who was initially brought in as a temporary stand-in for Hamilton's original 2026 engineer, Riccardo Adami. Hamilton said he and Santi had **never even spoken before being paired together**, yet the partnership clicked almost immediately, with Santi's clear, direct communication marking a sharp contrast to Hamilton's earlier struggles at the team. That chemistry culminated in Hamilton's **first-ever race win in a Ferrari**, at the Barcelona Grand Prix, where Santi joined him on the podium. Hamilton has since nicknamed Santi his 'Italian Bono,' referencing his legendary former Mercedes engineer Peter Bonnington. A Ferrari spokesperson confirmed there are no plans to replace Santi, telling reporters the pair are 'working pretty well together.'
key_points: Hamilton credits race engineer **Carlo Santi** with 'reigniting' his passion for F1 after a difficult start at Ferrari.
The pair had **never spoken before this season**, yet clicked instantly once paired together.
Santi stepped in as a **temporary replacement** for Hamilton's original engineer, Riccardo Adami.
Their partnership delivered Hamilton's **first-ever win in Ferrari colours**, at the Barcelona Grand Prix.
Ferrari has confirmed **no plans to replace Santi**, calling the pairing a clear success.

depth.background: Lewis Hamilton, a seven-time world champion, joined Ferrari for the 2026 season in one of the most closely watched driver moves in F1 history — but his start was rockier than expected as he adjusted to a new team, car, and crucially, a new race engineer relationship, historically one of the most important bonds in the sport. His long-time Mercedes engineer **Peter 'Bono' Bonnington** was famous for their close communication style, and replicating that trust with a new voice in his ear proved difficult at first with original engineer Riccardo Adami. Carlo Santi, a 52-year-old veteran Ferrari engineer from Verona, has a long history at the team, having previously guided Kimi Räikkönen to his final F1 win in 2018.

stories.title: Mercedes boss Toto Wolff suggests Ferrari will 'run out' of cost-cap budget for its relentless upgrades
stories.what_happened: Mercedes team principal **Toto Wolff** said he is **'a little bit surprised'** that Ferrari can keep bringing major updates to its car within F1's $215 million cost cap, adding he believes the Italian team will **'be running out of money soon.'** Wolff said Mercedes has been more conservative with upgrades this season specifically because it lacks the financial buffer to match Ferrari's development rate, and that he's holding back some of Mercedes' own updates for the second half of the year. Ferrari team principal **Fred Vasseur** responded angrily, treating Wolff's comments as bordering on an accusation of rule-breaking. Wolff has since clarified he has **no evidence** of any wrongdoing and there is no FIA investigation into Ferrari's spending — his comments were speculation about how Ferrari is managing its budget, not a formal complaint.
key_points: Wolff says he's **'surprised'** Ferrari can keep bringing major upgrades under F1's **$215 million** 2026 cost cap.
He predicts Ferrari will be **'running out of money soon'** if it keeps upgrading at this rate.
Ferrari boss **Fred Vasseur** has pushed back angrily at suggestions bordering on a cheating accusation.
Wolff says Mercedes lacks the **'buffer'** to match Ferrari's pace of upgrades this season.
There is **no official FIA investigation or evidence** — Wolff's comments are suspicion, not a formal accusation.

depth.background: Formula 1 introduced a cost cap in 2021 to limit how much teams can spend on car development each season, aiming to level the playing field between wealthy manufacturers and smaller teams. For 2026, that cap sits at **$215 million**. Ferrari has brought a rapid stream of upgrades to its car this season while competing for the championship, and rival teams have increasingly questioned how it's affording the pace of development within the cap's limits.

stories.title: Verstappen-McLaren contract talks reportedly reach 'closing stages' as his Red Bull exit clause looms
stories.what_happened: Multiple F1 outlets, including The Race and Autosport, report that **Verstappen and McLaren are in the closing stages** of talks about a potential move for the 2027 season. The reports say Verstappen's Red Bull contract contains an exit clause allowing him to leave if he isn't inside the **top two of the drivers' championship** by the summer break — a threshold he was unable to meet after a difficult stretch of results earlier in the season. Verstappen would have until **October** to formally decide whether to activate that clause, according to reports. His manager, **Raymond Vermeulen**, has pushed back on the idea of an imminent switch, saying Verstappen wants to honor his Red Bull deal through 2028 and that the clause existing doesn't mean it will be used. Separately, Verstappen's personal management brand has already begun informally collaborating with McLaren's junior driver program, a smaller sign of warming ties between the two camps.
key_points: Multiple paddock reports say **Max Verstappen and McLaren** are in the 'closing stages' of talks over a possible **2027 move**.
Verstappen's Red Bull contract runs to **2028**, but contains an **exit clause** tied to his championship position.
The clause requires him to be **inside the top two** in the standings by the summer break — reports say that threshold was missed.
Verstappen's manager, **Raymond Vermeulen**, says Max wants to fulfill his Red Bull contract and downplays an imminent exit.
Any Verstappen move would trigger one of the biggest **'silly season'** driver shuffles in years, given he's a **4-time champion**.

depth.background: **Max Verstappen** is a four-time Formula 1 world champion who has driven for Red Bull since 2016, becoming the team's defining driver of the 2020s. His current contract runs until **2028**, but like many top F1 drivers, it includes performance-linked exit clauses that let him leave early if the team or his results fall below a certain bar. McLaren, by contrast, has resurged as the sport's form team behind drivers **Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri**, who fought a close title battle in 2025. Driver contracts for the following season are typically negotiated during the sport's August summer break, a period nicknamed **'silly season'** for the flurry of rumors and deals that emerge.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine trade their deadliest attacks in weeks, killing at least 22 combined
stories.what_happened: Russia and Ukraine exchanged some of their heaviest attacks in weeks on **August 3**, according to local officials on both sides. In Ukraine, a Russian strike on a petrol station in the **Kryvyi Rih district of Dnipropetrovsk region** killed an emergency responder and his 8-year-old son, part of a toll of **11 dead** across the country; a separate strike sparked a major fire at food warehouses in **Dnipro**. In Russia's **Krasnodar region**, debris from an intercepted drone fell on the Black Sea resort village of Arkhipo-Osipovka near Gelendzhik, killing **7 people, including 3 children**, and wounding nearly 40 — bringing Russia's toll to 11. Ukraine also said its new **Magura naval attack drone** struck ground targets in Crimea for the first time, expanding the range of weapons it uses against Russian-held territory.
key_points: At least **11 killed in Ukraine** and **11 in Russia** in a single day of strikes, officials on both sides say.
A Russian strike on a petrol station in Dnipropetrovsk region killed an emergency worker and his **8-year-old son**.
Drone debris fell on the Russian resort village of Arkhipo-Osipovka near Gelendzhik, killing **7 people including 3 children**.
Ukraine's new **Magura naval drone** struck Russian ground targets in Crimea for the first time.
A Russian strike sparked a **major fire at food warehouses** in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro.

depth.background: Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in **February 2022** and has settled into a grinding war of attrition, with neither side controlling much more territory than a year ago but both able to strike deep behind the front lines using long-range drones and missiles. Russia regularly targets Ukrainian energy and civilian infrastructure; Ukraine has increasingly hit Russian territory, including the Crimean peninsula that Russia annexed in **2014**, using domestically built drones. Peace talks have repeatedly stalled, with both sides accusing the other of escalating rather than negotiating.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine's drone war spreads to Black Sea shipping lanes, as a major Moscow drone attack grounds 200+ flights
stories.what_happened: On Monday, six or seven drones struck the Ro-Ro cargo ship **Nadhezna**, which was carrying fruit and vegetables from Turkey's Samsun to Russia's Novorossiysk port, injuring four crew members roughly 30 nautical miles from its destination; Ukraine is the suspected source, per the ship's captain. Separately, Ukrainian drones sank the Russian-owned container ship **Yanina** near the same port. Russia's Transportation Ministry announced Monday it is stepping up protection for ships in the Azov-Black Sea basin and standing up a joint task force with the Defense Ministry to reroute freight and shift cargo to alternative transit modes. Meanwhile, a large Ukrainian drone attack on Moscow this week caused **more than 200 flight delays and cancellations**.
key_points: Drones hit the Turkish-flagged cargo ship **Nadhezna** near Novorossiysk, injuring **four crew members**.
Ukraine says it sank the Russian-owned container ship **Yanina** in a separate strike days earlier.
Russia is forming a **joint task force** with its Defense Ministry to reroute cargo and protect ships.
A major Ukrainian drone attack on Moscow **delayed or canceled over 200 flights** this week.
Russia's transport ministry says it's shifting cargo to alternative routes as **grain exports** come under threat.

depth.background: Russia and Ukraine have fought for over two years, but a newer front has opened over **shipping and infrastructure** rather than front-line territory. The Black Sea is a critical export route for Russian oil and grain, and for goods moving between Turkey and Russian ports like Novorossiysk. Ukraine has increasingly used long-range drones to strike targets far from the battlefield — inside Russia and on ships tied to Russia's economy — as a way to pressure Moscow without a ground offensive.

stories.title: Visa agrees to buy AI-fraud detection firm BioCatch for $2.4 billion as account-takeover scams surge
stories.what_happened: Visa announced on **August 3** that it will acquire BioCatch for **$2.4 billion in cash**, buying the company from funds advised by Permira and other shareholders. BioCatch's technology continuously monitors behavioral signals — typing rhythm, swipe patterns, how a device is held — to distinguish a genuine account holder from a fraudster in real time, stopping fraud before a payment is even attempted. The company already protects **1.8 billion devices** and **760 million users**, serving more than **350 banking clients** across **21 countries**, including over 100 of the world's largest banks. Visa framed the deal as a direct response to the explosion of AI-powered scams, which the companies say now cost the global economy more than **$1 trillion annually**. The transaction is expected to close in Visa's **fiscal second quarter of 2027**, pending regulatory approval.
key_points: Visa will pay **$2.4 billion in cash** for BioCatch, an AI-driven fraud-detection firm, in a deal announced **August 3**.
BioCatch protects **1.8 billion devices** and **760 million users** across more than **350 banks** in 21 countries.
It flags fraud using **behavioral biometrics** — how a person types, swipes, and holds their phone — to spot imposters before money moves.
Account takeovers and scams cost the global economy over **$1 trillion a year**, a toll AI is now supercharging.
The deal, bought from Permira-backed shareholders, is expected to **close in fiscal Q2 2027**.

depth.background: As generative AI makes scams — fake voices, deepfake video calls, convincingly-written phishing messages — dramatically easier to pull off at scale, banks and payment networks have been racing to build AI defenses of their own. **Visa**, the world's largest payment network, has been expanding into fraud-prevention and risk services beyond its core card-processing business for several years. **BioCatch**, an Israeli-founded cybersecurity firm, built its business on 'behavioral biometrics' — using how someone physically interacts with their device as a fingerprint to catch account takeovers that passwords and one-time codes miss.

stories.title: India's Textiles Ministry launches Centre of Excellence for Handloom Technology at IIT Delhi to modernize a 3.5-million-weaver industry
stories.what_happened: **Union Textiles Minister Giriraj Singh** inaugurated the **Centre of Excellence for Handloom Technology (CoE-HT)** at **IIT Delhi** today, an initiative built with an investment of roughly **₹12 crore**. The centre will work on **loom modernization and ergonomics** (making looms easier and safer to physically operate), **artificial intelligence**, sustainability, and digital knowledge systems for the handloom sector. Alongside the launch, the ministry rolled out **five specific initiatives**: 'Handloom 4.0,' which gives weavers digital tools to measure loom productivity and sustainability; 'Handloom e-Vidya,' a digital learning platform for weavers; and 'HandloomX,' an incubation and accelerator platform for handloom-related startups, among others. Senior officials including Minister of State **Pabitra Margherita** and Textiles Secretary **Neelam Shami Rao** attended the event.
key_points: Union Textiles Minister **Giriraj Singh** inaugurated the **Centre of Excellence for Handloom Technology (CoE-HT)** at IIT Delhi today.
The centre was set up with an investment of about **₹12 crore (₹11.99 crore)**.
It will focus on **loom modernization, AI, sustainability and digital tools** for India's handloom sector.
**Five new initiatives** launch alongside it, including 'Handloom 4.0' (digital productivity tools) and 'HandloomX' (a startup accelerator).
The goal is to connect **academia, industry, designers and weavers** who have historically worked in isolation from each other.

depth.background: India's handloom sector is one of the largest sources of rural, non-farm employment in the country, sustaining millions of weaver households, many working with techniques passed down for generations on manually operated looms. Despite its cultural and economic importance, the sector has long struggled with **low productivity, poor market access, and outdated equipment** compared to power-loom and mill-made textiles, making it hard for traditional weavers to compete or earn a stable living. The government has periodically launched schemes to modernize the sector, and this new centre — a partnership between the **Ministry of Textiles** and one of India's top engineering institutes — is the latest attempt to bring modern technology and design thinking directly to weavers.

stories.title: India's factory growth cools to a near five-year low, even as exports pick up
stories.what_happened: S&P Global released the HSBC India Manufacturing PMI for July on Monday, showing the headline index easing to **53.5** from June's **54.2** — still comfortably above the 50-line, but the softest expansion pace in almost **five years**. Output and new orders both kept rising, but overall sales growth was among the slowest in more than four years, pointing to softer domestic demand. Hiring told a similar story: employment growth weakened for a third straight month and job creation was the slowest recorded in the current 29-month expansion run, as companies reined in purchasing and staffing plans. The bright spot was trade — new export orders picked up pace, driven by fresh demand from markets including Canada, Egypt, Indonesia, Kenya, Nepal, South Africa, Thailand and the UAE. On costs, input-price inflation eased, but companies raised their own selling prices at a faster clip, suggesting manufacturers are protecting profit margins by passing costs on to customers. Business confidence improved from June's recent low, with firms citing hopes of stronger demand, infrastructure spending and new client enquiries ahead.
key_points: The HSBC India Manufacturing PMI slipped to **53.5 in July** from **54.2 in June**, the weakest pace of growth since **August 2021**.
The index stayed above the **50-mark** that separates growth from contraction — India's factory sector has now expanded for **29 straight months**.
**Job creation slowed for a third consecutive month**, hitting its slowest pace of the entire 29-month growth streak.
**New export orders strengthened**, led by demand from Canada, Egypt, Indonesia, Kenya, Nepal, South Africa, Thailand and the UAE.
Firms raised the **prices they charge customers** even as their own input costs cooled — meaning margins are being protected by passing costs downstream.

depth.background: The Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) is a monthly survey of factory managers that has become one of the most closely watched early signals of economic health, because it lands weeks before official government output data. A reading above 50 means more managers report improving conditions than worsening ones; below 50 signals contraction. India's manufacturing PMI has stayed in expansion territory for well over two years, seen as a bright spot as global supply chains diversify away from China and India courts more manufacturing investment. HSBC and S&P Global jointly compile the India survey each month from responses at roughly 400 manufacturing companies.

stories.title: Red Bull's replacement for Helmut Marko is confirmed: ex-Mercedes talent chief Gwen Lagrue
stories.what_happened: **Red Bull** has confirmed it has poached **Gwen Lagrue** away from Mercedes to become **Director of the Red Bull Junior Programme**, taking up the post at the start of **2027** after Mercedes releases him from his current duties. Lagrue spent more than **11 years** at Mercedes' Brackley base, and his standout achievement was spotting **Kimi Antonelli** in karting at age **11** and fast-tracking him to an F1 debut at **18** — Antonelli is now leading the **2026 world championship** in only his second F1 season. Red Bull team principal **Laurent Mekies** called Lagrue 'one of the very best talent developers in F1', framing the hire as the long-term answer to the void left by Marko's departure. Today, former Haas team boss **Guenther Steiner**, appearing on The Red Flags Podcast, praised the move, saying Lagrue 'has been doing it longer than anybody else' and that landing him was 'a very good hire' for Red Bull's future grid presence. Mercedes has since confirmed the exit publicly, meaning the very team whose success was partly built on Lagrue's eye for talent must now find its own replacement.
key_points: Red Bull has hired **Gwen Lagrue**, Mercedes' junior-programme boss of over a decade, to run its own junior driver pipeline from **2027**.
Lagrue effectively replaces **Helmut Marko**, the Austrian power-broker who built Red Bull's driver factory and left at the end of **2025**.
Lagrue is the scout who spotted and signed both **George Russell** and championship leader **Kimi Antonelli** as karters.
Former Haas boss **Guenther Steiner** publicly praised the move today, calling it 'a very good hire' by Red Bull team principal **Laurent Mekies**.
Mercedes has confirmed Lagrue's exit, meaning the team that discovered Russell and Antonelli must now replace its own talent chief too.

depth.background: Every F1 team with big ambitions runs a 'junior programme' — a pipeline that spots karting talent as young as **10 or 11**, funds their climb through junior racing series, and grooms whoever looks like a future world champion. For over a decade, **Mercedes'** programme was run by Frenchman **Gwen Lagrue**, who is widely credited as the scout who identified and signed both **George Russell** and current 2026 championship leader **Kimi Antonelli** long before either had proven anything. On the other side of the paddock, **Red Bull's** equivalent pipeline was built and run for two decades by the outspoken Austrian **Helmut Marko**, whose eye for talent produced champions like **Max Verstappen** and **Sebastian Vettel** — but Marko left the team at the end of **2025**, leaving a hole at the top of Red Bull's driver factory that the team has spent months trying to fill.

stories.title: Sensex and Nifty close up for a 4th straight session as falling crude oil keeps lifting Indian markets
stories.what_happened: India's benchmark stock indices extended their rally through the close of trading on **Monday, August 3**: the **Sensex ended up 544.39 points (0.7%) at 78,639.03**, and the **Nifty 50 climbed 390.70 points (1.60%) to close at 24,774.30**, giving both indices their **fourth consecutive day of gains**. The rally moderated somewhat from the morning's sharper 788-point Sensex jump, but held up through the session on continued **crude oil price weakness**. **IT stocks led the advance**, with the sector index up more than 3% on the day, while investors also positioned ahead of the **RBI's rate decision**, due Wednesday, August 5, where a Reuters poll of 72 economists found 68 expect the repo rate to stay unchanged at **5.25%**.
key_points: The **Sensex closed up 544.39 points (0.7%)** at **78,639.03**; the **Nifty 50 gained 390.70 points (1.60%)** to close at **24,774.30**.
It's the **4th straight winning session** for both benchmark indices.
**Falling crude oil prices** remained the single biggest driver, since India imports over 80% of its oil.
The **IT sector led gains**, with the Nifty IT index up over **3%** on the day.
Markets are now positioning ahead of the **RBI's rate decision on August 5**, where most economists expect the repo rate to stay unchanged at **5.25%**.

depth.background: India imports more than **80% of the crude oil** it uses, so global oil prices move Indian markets almost as directly as domestic company news — cheaper oil lowers the country's import bill, eases inflation, and boosts margins for oil-consuming businesses like airlines and paint makers. Oil prices have been falling as fears of a Middle East supply shock from the Iran conflict have eased in recent days. Meanwhile, India's central bank, the **RBI**, is in the middle of a **3-day Monetary Policy Committee meeting** (August 3–5) that will decide whether to change the **repo rate** — the interest rate at which it lends to banks, which ripples through to loan and deposit rates across the economy.

thread.previously: We reported that the Sensex opened up 788.7 points and the Nifty added 189 points to cross 24,550 on the morning of August 3, driven by falling crude oil prices after the US held off on new Iran strikes, with markets also positioning ahead of the RBI's August 5 rate decision.
thread.changed: By the close of trading on August 3, some of that morning surge had faded, but the Sensex still finished up 544 points at 78,639.03 and the Nifty closed above 24,750 (up 390.70 points) — marking a 4th consecutive winning session, still powered by the same falling crude oil tailwind.

stories.title: Pierre Gasly says Alpine's upgrades at the Dutch Grand Prix are 'critical' to save its F1 season
stories.what_happened: Pierre Gasly said Alpine's upcoming upgrade package for the **Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort (August 21–23)** — the race immediately after F1's summer break — is **'critical'** to keeping the team's 2026 season alive. Alpine has fallen **5 points behind Racing Bulls** in the constructors' standings after going five races without any car upgrades, even as rivals introduced new parts. Team managing director **Steve Nielsen** confirmed the Zandvoort update will include **'pretty big new aero parts,'** as the team tries to arrest its slide. The Hungarian Grand Prix, run just before the break, marked the **third time in four races** that Gasly failed to score any points, adding urgency to the team's development push.
key_points: Gasly calls Alpine's planned upgrade at Zandvoort **'critical'** for the team's remaining 2026 chances.
Alpine has slipped **5 points behind Racing Bulls** in the standings after five races with no upgrades.
Managing director **Steve Nielsen** says the Zandvoort package will include **'pretty big new aero parts.'**
The Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort runs **August 21–23**, right after F1's summer break.
Hungary marked the **third time in four races** Gasly failed to score points.

depth.background: Alpine, formerly Renault's F1 team, has struggled for competitiveness for years and entered 2026 hoping new technical regulations would level the playing field with front-running teams. It started the season as F1's leading **midfield** team — the cluster of teams fighting just behind the top contenders — sitting fifth in the constructors' championship after a podium finish for Gasly at Monaco. Since then, rival midfield teams have out-developed Alpine's car (the A526) with new parts, while Alpine has gone without a major upgrade since round four in Miami, causing it to slide back down the order.

stories.title: The US and Japan jointly intervene to prop up a collapsing yen — first time since 2011
stories.what_happened: Japan's Finance Minister **Satsuki Katayama** confirmed in Tokyo on Monday that the government had bought yen in the open market, working in coordination with the **US Treasury Department** — the first time the two countries have intervened together since **2011**. After the announcement, the dollar fell about **1%** against the yen, from recent lows near 163 to about **156.34**. Financial Times estimates put Japan's spending at roughly **¥8.45 trillion (~$52.8 billion)**. President Trump confirmed US involvement and framed it as a favor to an ally, at one point joking about Japan's history with the US ('with the exception, of course, of Pearl Harbor') while calling the move 'good for the world economy.'
key_points: Japan's Finance Minister confirmed Tokyo **bought yen** in coordination with the **US Treasury**, Monday.
It's the **first joint US-Japan currency intervention since 2011** — a 15-year gap.
The dollar dropped **about 1%**, from a 40-year-low **163.24 yen** last month to **156.34 yen**.
Analysts estimate Japan spent roughly **¥8.45 trillion (about $52.8 billion)** on the move.
Trump called it a **'signal of friendship'** and said the US got 'financial benefit' from it.

depth.background: The yen has been sliding for months, hit by **higher US interest rates** (which make dollar assets more attractive than yen ones), rising oil prices, and persistent money leaving Japan for higher-yielding markets abroad. Last month it touched **163.24 per dollar**, its weakest level since **1986**. A currency that weak makes imports — energy, food, chips — more expensive for ordinary Japanese households, which is why Tokyo eventually judged the slide too dangerous to leave alone.

stories.title: RBI's rate-setting committee begins its 3-day meeting — markets bet on a fourth straight pause
stories.what_happened: India's six-member Monetary Policy Committee, headed by RBI Governor **Sanjay Malhotra**, convened Monday for its scheduled three-day bi-monthly review, with the rate decision due at **10am on Wednesday, August 5**, followed by a 12pm press conference. A Reuters poll of 72 economists found **68 expect the repo rate held at 5.25%**, continuing the pause that began after December's 25-basis-point cut. The RBI had already lifted its FY27 retail inflation forecast to **5.1%** from an earlier 4.6% estimate, citing mounting input costs, while projecting real GDP growth of **6.6%** for the year. The decision comes as India's factory growth has cooled to a near five-year low even as industrial output posted its fastest pace in nearly two years in June — a mixed picture that gives the MPC little clear signal to move in either direction.
key_points: The **Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** began its bi-monthly meeting today, running **August 3-5**.
Governor **Sanjay Malhotra** will announce the decision at **10am on Wednesday**, followed by a press conference.
**68 of 72 economists** polled by Reuters expect the **repo rate held at 5.25%** — a fourth straight pause.
The RBI already raised its **FY27 inflation forecast to 5.1%** (from 4.6%) on rising input costs, even as growth is pegged at **6.6%**.
A hold would come even as **global peers have hiked rates** in response to Iran-war-driven inflation pressure.

depth.background: The repo rate is the interest rate at which the RBI lends to commercial banks — it's the central lever India's central bank uses to control inflation and growth; cutting it makes borrowing cheaper (stimulating the economy), while raising it cools inflation by making money more expensive. The RBI last cut rates by 25 basis points in December 2025, to the current 5.25%, and has held steady at its last three reviews since. This meeting lands against a backdrop of easing crude oil prices (helping the inflation outlook) but the recent US tariffs on Indian goods complicating the growth picture.

stories.title: Sensex jumps 788 points as falling crude oil prices and RBI rate-decision hopes lift Indian markets
stories.what_happened: Indian equity benchmarks opened sharply higher on **August 3**: the **Sensex gained 788.7 points to 78,883.34**, and the **Nifty50 rose to above 24,550**, up nearly 190 points, as crude oil prices fell on news that the US would not carry out threatened new strikes on Iran. **ITC, IndiGo-parent InterGlobe Aviation, and Bajaj Finance** were among the top Nifty gainers. The move comes just two days before the **RBI's Monetary Policy Committee announces its rate decision on August 5**, where most economists expect the repo rate to be held at **5.25%**. It also comes in the middle of India's **busiest Q1 earnings week**, with over 350 companies — including **Bharti Airtel, ONGC, Power Grid, SBI and Titan** — reporting results this week.
key_points: The **Sensex opened up 788.7 points** at 78,883, and the **Nifty added 189 points** to cross **24,550**.
The rally is driven by a **sharp drop in crude oil prices** after the US held off on new strikes on Iran, easing fears of a Middle East oil-supply shock.
**ITC, InterGlobe Aviation (IndiGo) and Bajaj Finance** led the gainers on the Nifty50.
Markets are also positioning ahead of the **RBI's rate decision on August 5** and a heavy week of **Q1 earnings** from Bharti Airtel, SBI, ONGC and others.
**Foreign investors bought a modest ₹277 crore** of Indian equities on July 31, while domestic investors bought far more, **₹2,260 crore**.

depth.background: India imports over 80% of its oil, so **crude oil prices** move Indian markets almost as directly as domestic news does — a fall in oil prices lowers the country's import bill, eases inflation pressure, and is read by markets as good news for corporate margins and the rupee. The past week has been dominated by Middle East tension: **Trump ordered and then called off new strikes on Iran**, and Iran has reportedly signalled openness to reopening the **Strait of Hormuz**, a critical oil shipping chokepoint. That de-escalation is what's pulling oil prices — and by extension Indian stocks — in a positive direction today.

stories.title: Aston Martin begins locking in its 2027 car's architecture as Adrian Newey bets big on F1's new rules
stories.what_happened: Adrian Newey confirmed that Aston Martin is now making the **'big architectural decisions'** — engine position in the wheelbase, chassis layout, and other long-lead-time choices — for its **2027 car**, internally named the **AMR27**. He highlighted the front **'tea tray'** (the leading edge of the car's underbody floor) as the single most important rule change for 2027: it moves forward by roughly **300 millimetres**, allowing teams to run the front of the car lower to the ground for more downforce. Other 2027 changes include a **shallower rear wing** to cut overall downforce, a reduction in the floor's **'bear claw' vents from five to three**, the banning of various exhaust and rear-wing aerodynamic tricks teams currently exploit, and power-unit tweaks including **5% more fuel allowance** and adjusted energy storage and deployment rules. Newey said Aston Martin is now a **'much more mature'** team than six months ago and is well placed to capitalize on the regulation reset.
key_points: Aston Martin design chief **Adrian Newey** says the team is now making the **'big architectural decisions'** for its **2027 car, the AMR27**.
Those decisions — engine placement, chassis layout — are **long-lead-time choices** that are hard to reverse once locked in.
F1's 2027 rules move the floor's front edge (the **'tea tray'**) forward by about **300mm**, letting cars run lower at the front.
The rear wing shrinks and the floor's **'bear claw' vents drop from five to three**, while engines get **5% more fuel** and tweaked energy deployment.
Newey says Aston Martin is now a **'much more mature'** organisation than it was six months ago, positioning the team to exploit the new rules.

depth.background: **Adrian Newey** is widely regarded as the most successful car designer in Formula 1 history, having designed championship-winning cars for Williams, McLaren and Red Bull before joining **Aston Martin** in 2025 specifically to lead its push for competitiveness. F1 periodically rewrites its technical rulebook — the last major reset was in 2022 — and a new set of changes lands in **2027**, which teams are already designing around more than a year in advance because chassis and engine architecture decisions can't easily be changed once committed. Aston Martin has struggled to match the sport's front-runners since Newey's arrival, making how well it reads and exploits the 2027 rules a major test of his tenure.

stories.title: Mercedes teases a 'sizeable' upgrade for its championship-leading car after F1's summer break
stories.what_happened: Mercedes' deputy technical director **Simone Resta** said the team is preparing a **'sizeable' upgrade** for its W17 car once F1 returns from its summer break, after largely running smaller updates since introducing a major package at the **Canadian Grand Prix** earlier this season. Team principal **Toto Wolff** confirmed the strategy was deliberate — Mercedes chose to weight its development toward the second half of 2026 rather than front-loading upgrades. The tease comes as Mercedes has dominated the season so far, winning **8 of the first 11 races** between Russell and Antonelli, with Antonelli holding a **50-point lead** over Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton in the drivers' standings at the break.
key_points: Deputy technical director **Simone Resta** says Mercedes will bring a **'sizeable' upgrade** to the W17 after the break.
Mercedes has won **8 of the opening 11 races** this season between George Russell and Kimi Antonelli.
Antonelli holds a **50-point championship lead** over Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton heading into the break.
Team boss **Toto Wolff** confirms Mercedes deliberately weighted upgrades toward the **second half of the season**.
Mercedes' last major package came at the **Canadian Grand Prix**; it has mostly run smaller updates since.

depth.background: Mercedes enters 2026 as the early pacesetter under F1's new technical regulations, a reversal after several seasons of being outpaced by Red Bull. Its driver lineup pairs experienced racer **George Russell** with rookie sensation **Andrea Kimi Antonelli**, who has emerged as a genuine title contender in his first full season. F1 teams typically stagger their development budget across a season under the sport's **cost cap** rules, choosing when to spend on new parts — an early upgrade can lock in points now, while a late one can matter more if a title fight is still close deep into the year.

stories.title: India's stock exchanges quietly switch to an auction-based closing price for F&O stocks
stories.what_happened: **SEBI (India's markets regulator)** and the **NSE** launched the **Closing Auction Session (CAS)** on **August 3, 2026** for all F&O-eligible stocks. Under the new system, continuous trading for these stocks stops at **3:15pm**, then a **Closing Auction Session** runs until **3:35pm**, where all outstanding buy and sell orders are pooled together and matched at a single **'equilibrium price'** — the price at which the maximum number of shares can be traded. That single matched price becomes the official closing price. Non-F&O stocks continue trading normally until 3:30pm with no change, while F&O derivatives themselves trade until 3:40pm with a brief post-close session from 3:50-4:00pm.
key_points: From **August 3**, SEBI's new **Closing Auction Session (CAS)** sets closing prices for F&O-eligible stocks.
It replaces the old **VWAP-based** method with a **single-price auction**, matching all buy/sell orders at once.
Continuous trading for these stocks now ends at **3:15pm**, followed by the auction window until **3:35pm**.
Non-F&O stocks are **unaffected** — they keep trading normally until 3:30pm.
The goal: **harder-to-manipulate closing prices** and better execution for large institutional orders.

depth.background: Every trading day, exchanges need an official **'closing price'** for each stock — it's used to value mutual funds, settle derivative contracts, and calculate index levels. Until now, India used a **Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP)** method for stocks with **F&O (futures & options)** contracts — essentially an average of prices over the last few minutes of trading. Critics have long argued VWAP-based closes can be nudged by large last-minute trades, especially on days when derivative contracts expire, because a trader with a big options position has an incentive to move the underlying stock's closing price in their favor.

stories.title: A Ukrainian drone hits a crowded Russian beach resort, killing 7 including 3 children
stories.what_happened: On the morning of **August 3**, a drone strike hit a crowded public beach in **Gelendzhik**, a resort city in Russia's Krasnodar region on the Black Sea. Krasnodar Governor **Veniamin Kondratyev** said the incident killed at least **7 people, including 3 children**, and injured about **40 others**, with around 20 hospitalized. Ukraine's government did not confirm it launched the drone but did not deny it either, instead arguing that Russia's own air-defense system shot the drone down over the beach and caused the casualties — with one Ukrainian official saying **'it was Putin who killed these Russians.'** Russia accused Ukraine of deliberately targeting civilians, which would constitute a war crime under international law, and launched a **fresh wave of aerial strikes** against Ukraine in response.
key_points: Debris from a Ukrainian drone struck a **packed beach** in **Gelendzhik**, a Black Sea resort city in Russia's **Krasnodar region**.
At least **7 people died, including 3 children**, and roughly **40 more were injured**, with dozens hospitalized.
Ukraine did not deny launching the drone but said Russia's own **air defenses shot it down** over the beach — blaming Moscow for the deaths.
Russia called it a **deliberate attack on civilians**, which would be a war crime, and responded with a **fresh barrage of strikes on Ukraine**.
It's one of the **deadliest single incidents** in the Krasnodar region since the drone war expanded to Black Sea tourist areas.

depth.background: Russia's Krasnodar region, on the Black Sea coast, has increasingly become a target as **Ukraine's long-range drone campaign** has expanded beyond front-line military targets to hit refineries, ports, and now — accidentally or not — a civilian beach. Both countries operate extensive **air-defense networks** that can misfire or send falling debris into populated areas even when they successfully intercept a drone. Summer is peak tourist season on Russia's Black Sea coast, meaning beaches like Gelendzhik's are typically crowded with families on holiday.

thread.previously: Russia and Ukraine traded their deadliest attacks in weeks, together killing at least 22 people, as the drone war spread to Black Sea shipping lanes and grounded 200+ flights around Moscow.
thread.changed: A new strike has now killed 7 more, including 3 children, at a crowded civilian beach resort far from the front line — with both sides publicly disputing who is actually responsible for the deaths.
