stories.title: F1 shuts down for two weeks — literally: teams are banned from touching their cars until August 17
stories.what_happened: Formula 1 entered its FIA-mandated summer break after the **Hungarian Grand Prix** (held July 24–26), with most teams observing the factory shutdown from roughly **August 3 to 17** — no wind-tunnel running, no car development, no simulator work anywhere in the paddock. The season so far has been unusually competitive: **Kimi Antonelli** leads the drivers' championship after 11 of the year's rounds, with **five different winners** in the last five races alone. Mercedes has already said it's targeting a **'sizeable' upgrade** once the team is legally allowed to resume work, aimed at the next race. Racing resumes at the **Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort, August 21–23** — notably the last running of the race under F1's current contract with the venue.
key_points: F1's **mandatory summer shutdown** runs roughly **August 3–17**, with most teams observing it.
During the shutdown, teams can't do **wind-tunnel testing, car development, or simulator work**.
**Kimi Antonelli** leads the championship after 11 rounds, with five different race winners in the last five races.
Racing resumes at the **Dutch Grand Prix, August 21–23** — the final edition at Zandvoort under F1's current contract.
Teams are expected to return with saved-up upgrades once the factory freeze lifts.

depth.background: F1's summer shutdown is a rule written into the sport's regulations, not a scheduling accident: it forces every team to fully close their factories for a fixed period, with **no development work of any kind** allowed — from full-scale car updates down to late-night simulator sessions. It exists partly to protect the wellbeing of team staff who otherwise work relentlessly through a 24-race season, and partly to help enforce F1's **cost cap** by putting a hard stop on development spending for two weeks.

stories.title: Australia confirms its first mass bird-flu die-off, warns worse spread is coming
stories.what_happened: Australian authorities said on **Monday** that helicopter surveillance teams found **49 dead and 35 sick greater crested terns** on rocks off Cape Jaffa, about **250km (155 miles) from Adelaide**, on the preceding Friday. Testing confirmed these were infected with **H5N1**, making it the **first confirmed mass mortality event** linked to the virus in Australian wildlife. Agriculture Minister Julie Collins told reporters in Canberra that **'Australians should expect to see more spread and larger numbers now of wildlife being affected,'** adding that once the virus is circulating in the wild, **'it is not possible to avoid significant losses.'** The national tally has now reached **74 confirmed cases**, roughly **tripling within about a week**, spread across South Australia (54), Western Australia (10), Victoria (7), New South Wales (2) and Queensland (1). Officials stressed there is still **no evidence of the virus on Australian poultry farms**, many of which locked down biosecurity measures after the first detection in June.
key_points: Australia recorded its **first-ever mass mortality event** from H5N1 bird flu: **49 dead and 35 sick** greater crested terns found off Cape Jaffa, South Australia.
The country's confirmed case count has now hit **74**, nearly **tripling in about a week**.
Agriculture Minister Julie Collins warned **'significant losses' can no longer be avoided** once the virus spreads through wildlife.
Cases span **five states** — South Australia, Western Australia, Victoria, New South Wales and Queensland — but **no poultry farms are infected yet**.
Scientists warn the outbreak also threatens **endangered Australian sea lions**, which feed near infected seabird colonies.

depth.background: **H5N1 bird flu** is a highly contagious strain of avian influenza that has been sweeping through wild birds and mammals worldwide since **2021**, killing millions of birds and infecting poultry farms, dairy cattle, and even some farmworkers across the Americas and Europe. Australia had largely been spared until this year, in part due to its geographic isolation from major bird migration routes, but the virus was first detected in the country in **June 2026**. Since then, authorities confirmed the virus was spreading **locally between wild birds themselves** — not just arriving from outside — which experts say makes containment far harder because it can now take root permanently in Australia's native wildlife.

stories.title: Assam's flood death toll climbs to 82 as Kerala reports 8 deaths in a separate monsoon crisis
stories.what_happened: Assam's flood death toll rose to **82** as monsoon rains and river swelling continued to batter the northeastern state, with more than **6,53,100 people affected across 11 districts**, according to state disaster authorities. Separately, and unrelated geographically, Kerala reported at least **8 deaths** from days of relentless rain, landslides and flash floods, concentrated in the state's high ranges — four of the deaths came from landslides in **Kottayam and Idukki districts** alone. Search operations are ongoing for **6 missing fishermen** (four from Thiruvananthapuram, two from Kollam) swept out into the Arabian Sea, plus two Kannur residents swept away by a river. Kerala has moved over **5,700 people** into relief camps, and the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an **orange alert for 12 districts** warning of continued intense rainfall.
key_points: Assam's flood toll has risen from 80 to **82 dead**, with over **6.53 lakh people affected** across 11 districts.
Kerala separately reports **8 dead** from landslides and flash floods, with **8 more missing**.
Six missing Kerala fishermen were swept out to sea near Thiruvananthapuram and Kollam.
The IMD has issued fresh **rain warnings** for Assam, Kerala, Gujarat and Chhattisgarh as the monsoon intensifies nationwide.
The Centre has pre-deployed **NDRF teams** and is coordinating relief with state governments.

depth.background: India's June-September monsoon is a lifeline for its farm economy but also its biggest recurring disaster risk, with the northeast (Assam) and the southwest coast (Kerala) both especially flood- and landslide-prone due to heavy terrain rainfall. Assam's flood toll had already reached **80** as of yesterday, prompting the government to announce a six-month loan moratorium for affected families. The crisis has since widened rather than eased, now stretching across multiple, unrelated states simultaneously.

thread.previously: Yesterday we reported Assam's flood toll at 80 dead, with the government announcing a six-month loan moratorium for affected families.
thread.changed: The toll has since risen to 82, and a second, separate flood emergency has emerged in Kerala with 8 dead and 8 missing, including 6 fishermen swept out to sea.

stories.title: India closes out its best-ever Commonwealth Games with 39 medals — and takes the baton as 2030 host
stories.what_happened: The Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games concluded on **Sunday, August 2**, with a closing ceremony at the Hydro arena. India ended the Games with **39 medals** — 13 gold, 17 silver and 9 bronze — its best tally at a Commonwealth Games to date, even with a smaller sports program than previous editions. **Boxing** was the standout, delivering a best-ever **10 medals including 7 golds**, headlined by wins from **Preeti Pawar** and **Arundhati Choudhary**. India's **judo** team won its first-ever CWG golds through **Asmita Dey** and **Harsh Singh**, building a four-medal tally in a sport where the country had no prior history of Commonwealth success. At the closing ceremony, Indian performers **Shankar Mahadevan** and **Manushi Chhillar** led a 20-minute cultural showcase before the Commonwealth Games flag was formally handed over to representatives of **Ahmedabad**, confirmed as host of the **2030 Games**.
key_points: India finished the Glasgow 2026 Games with **39 medals**: **13 gold, 17 silver, 9 bronze** — its best-ever tally despite a curtailed sports program.
Boxing delivered India's best-ever CWG haul: **10 medals, including 7 golds**.
India's judo team won its **first-ever CWG judo golds**, taking its tally to four medals in the sport.
At the closing ceremony, India performed a **20-minute cultural showcase** led by Shankar Mahadevan and Manushi Chhillar as the Games flag was formally **handed to Ahmedabad**.
**Ahmedabad will host the 2030 Commonwealth Games** — India's first time hosting since Delhi in 2010.

depth.background: The 2026 Commonwealth Games ran in Glasgow from **July 23 to August 2**, a scaled-down edition of the event after several traditional host cities passed on bidding. India has steadily built up its Commonwealth Games strength in boxing, wrestling and weightlifting over the past two decades, and this edition marked a breakthrough in judo, a sport where India had never previously won gold at the Games. Ahmedabad's selection as 2030 host — confirmed in the run-up to this year's Games — makes it India's first Commonwealth Games since Delhi 2010, a Games remembered as much for infrastructure and corruption controversies as for sport.

stories.title: Sri Lanka Women wrap up a 2-0 T20I series sweep over Pakistan — with a whitewash decider today
stories.what_happened: Sri Lanka Women beat Pakistan Women by **six wickets** in both the 1st T20I (July 31) and the 2nd T20I (August 2) at the Rangiri Dambulla International Stadium, sealing the three-match series with a match to spare. In the second game, Pakistan posted **175/5**, built around a 48-run knock from opener **Shawaal Zulfiqar** and 45 from Muneeba Ali, but Sri Lanka chased it down comfortably, reaching **178/4 in 17.4 overs**. **Sanjana Kavindi's** 46 off 24 balls earned her Player of the Match. Pakistan's bowling attack has struggled to defend competitive totals against Sri Lanka's aggressive chasing across both matches. The two sides meet for the **series-ending 3rd T20I today**, with Sri Lanka aiming to complete a full 3-0 sweep.
key_points: Sri Lanka Women won the **1st and 2nd T20Is** (July 31 and August 2) to seal the series **2-0**.
In the 2nd T20I, they chased **178 in just 17.4 overs**, with **14 balls to spare**.
**Sanjana Kavindi** (46 off 24) was Player of the Match, backing skipper **Chamari Athapaththu's** in-form batting.
Sri Lanka have now chased down **two 170+ totals** in consecutive matches — a sign of real depth, not luck.
The **3rd and final T20I** in Dambulla today is a dead rubber, but Sri Lanka are chasing a clean **3-0 whitewash**.

depth.background: Pakistan Women, captained by **Muneeba Ali**, are on a tour of Sri Lanka playing a three-match **T20I series** against the hosts, led by veteran opener **Chamari Athapaththu**. Sri Lanka's batting unit has been the standout of the series so far, repeatedly chasing down big totals with room to spare.

stories.title: Rain and Mohammad Abbas's shock axing shape Day 1 as West Indies close on 165/3 in the series-deciding 2nd Test
stories.what_happened: Rain repeatedly disrupted play on Day 1 of the series-deciding second Test between **West Indies and Pakistan** at the Queen's Park Oval — only **9.5 overs** were bowled before an early lunch forced by rain, with West Indies **49/1** at that point. Pakistan's bowling was built around spin rather than pace after the team made the **surprise call to leave out fast bowler Mohammad Abbas**; spinners **Ali Usman and Sajid Khan** bowled a combined **25 overs** and took two of the three wickets to fall. **Shai Hope and Justin Greaves** counterattacked in the last 45 minutes of play, pushing West Indies to **165/3** by the close, with Greaves unbeaten on 52. West Indies, who won the series opener by 90 runs, need only a draw or win here to take the series; Pakistan must win to level it.
key_points: West Indies closed Day 1 on **165/3** at the **Queen's Park Oval, Port of Spain**, with **Shai Hope and Justin Greaves** counterattacking late.
Only **9.5 overs** were possible before an early, rain-forced lunch, with West Indies at **49/1** at the break.
Pakistan's **shock decision to omit pacer Mohammad Abbas** was the pre-match talking point, with spinners **Ali Usman and Sajid Khan** bowling 25 of the day's overs instead.
West Indies arrive **1-0 up** in the two-match series after a **90-run win** in the opener, meaning this Test decides the series.
The pitch is shaping up as **spin-dominant**, a shift from the pace-friendly conditions of the first Test.

depth.background: **Pakistan** came into this tour after already losing the **series opener by 90 runs** at the Brian Lara Cricket Academy, meaning they had to win this second and final Test in **Port of Spain, Trinidad** just to level the series — any other result and **West Indies win the series**. The **Queen's Park Oval** is historically one of the more spin-friendly venues in the Caribbean, which shaped both sides' team selection, most notably Pakistan's decision to leave out a frontline pace bowler.

stories.title: Sri Lanka Women seal a rare series win over Pakistan, snapping a 12-year drought
stories.what_happened: Sri Lanka Women beat Pakistan Women by **6 wickets** in the second T20I at the Rangiri Dambulla International Stadium, chasing down Pakistan's total of **175/5** with balls to spare, to win the two-match series **2-0**. **Harshitha Samarawickrama** finished unbeaten on 37 off 22 balls to see her team home, and was named player of the series after scoring 173 runs across the two matches, including an unbeaten century in the first game. For Pakistan, **Shawaal Zulfiqar** top-scored with a maiden WT20I half-century, but it wasn't enough to prevent the loss. The win ends a **12-year wait** for Sri Lanka to beat Pakistan in a bilateral T20I series.
key_points: Sri Lanka won by **6 wickets** to seal the T20I series **2-0** with a match to spare
It's Sri Lanka's first bilateral T20I series win over Pakistan in **12 years**
**Harshitha Samarawickrama** hit an unbeaten 37 to guide the chase and was named player of the series
Pakistan's **Shawaal Zulfiqar** scored a maiden WT20I half-century, but it wasn't enough
Sri Lanka chased down Pakistan's **175/5** with balls to spare

depth.background: Sri Lanka Women and Pakistan Women don't play each other often in bilateral series, and Pakistan has historically had the upper hand — Sri Lanka hadn't beaten Pakistan in a bilateral **T20I series in 12 years**. This series, played in **Dambulla**, was a chance for Sri Lanka to end that streak against a Pakistan side searching for form of its own.

stories.title: Sophie Ecclestone rips through MI London's top order as Manchester Super Giants Women keep winless MI London bottom of The Hundred
stories.what_happened: At **The Oval** in London, MI London Women won the toss, chose to bat, and collapsed to just **92 all out**, playing without regular player Danni Wyatt-Hodge. **Sophie Ecclestone**, bowling the opening spell of the innings for the first time this season, struck twice early — dismissing both Alice Davidson-Richards and Hayley Matthews — to leave MI London reeling at 1 for 2, before finishing a tight spell conceding just **7 runs off 20 balls**. In reply, **Manchester Super Giants Women** chased the target down comfortably, reaching **95/4** with 28 balls remaining to win by **6 wickets**. Ecclestone was named Player of the Match for her spell.
key_points: **Manchester Super Giants Women** beat **MI London Women** by **6 wickets**, with 28 balls to spare, at The Oval.
England spinner **Sophie Ecclestone**, opening the bowling for the first time this season, took out both openers cheaply and was named **Player of the Match**.
MI London were bowled out for just **92**, having also been without star player **Danni Wyatt-Hodge**.
Manchester chased the target down comfortably, reaching **95/4**.
The result leaves **MI London still winless** and rooted to the **bottom of the table** in this year's Hundred Women's Competition.

depth.background: The Hundred is England's 100-ball cricket franchise competition, running men's and women's tournaments in parallel each summer since 2021, and has become a key summer showcase for both international and domestic women's talent. **Sophie Ecclestone** is one of the world's best left-arm spin bowlers and a regular fixture for England, making her performances a headline draw whenever she plays. MI London have struggled all season and came into this match already at the bottom of the points table, still searching for their first win.

stories.title: Assam's flood death toll passes 80 as over 2 lakh people remain displaced
stories.what_happened: As of the latest official figures from Assam's Disaster Reporting and Information Management System, the flood death toll in the state has reached **80**, with **2,12,441 people** affected across **eight districts** — Golaghat, Sivasagar, Biswanath, Charaideo, Kamrup Metropolitan, Jorhat, Dhemaji and Nagaon. The flood emergency now covers **437 villages** across **21 revenue circles**, and floodwaters have submerged roughly **17,198 hectares** of agricultural land, wiping out standing crops in some of the state's most fertile farming belts. The Centre has sanctioned **₹379.35 crore** in disaster relief funds specifically for Assam, as part of a broader relief package that also allocated ₹500 crore each to Gujarat, Maharashtra and Odisha, ₹193.95 crore to Himachal Pradesh, and ₹44.55 crore to Arunachal Pradesh. Separately, **Gautam Adani** contributed ₹11 crore to the state's Chief Minister's Relief Fund. Rescue and relief operations remain active, with floodwaters receding in some areas but localized flooding and riverbank erosion persisting elsewhere.
key_points: Assam's flood death toll has climbed to at least **80**, with more than **2.12 lakh people** (212,000) affected across **eight districts**.
The worst-hit districts include **Golaghat, Sivasagar, Jorhat, Dhemaji and Nagaon**, spanning **437 villages** in 21 revenue circles.
Nearly **17,200 hectares of cropland** are underwater, threatening farmers already squeezed by an uneven monsoon.
The central government has sanctioned **₹379.35 crore** in relief funds for Assam, part of a wider package that also covers Gujarat, Maharashtra, Odisha, Himachal Pradesh and Arunachal Pradesh.
Industrialist **Gautam Adani** donated **₹11 crore** to the Assam Chief Minister's Relief Fund as rescue and rehabilitation work continues.

depth.background: Assam sits on the floodplain of the **Brahmaputra river** and its tributaries, and severe monsoon flooding hits the state most years between June and September as the river swells with rainwater from Assam itself and upstream in the Himalayas. This year's floods have been unusually deadly and prolonged, coming on top of separate flood and landslide emergencies already hitting Kerala and Himachal Pradesh this monsoon season. Assam Chief Minister **Himanta Biswa Sarma** has been personally coordinating relief and rehabilitation operations, including door-to-door outreach by state ministers in the worst-affected districts.

stories.title: Fernando Alonso's F1 retirement call is coming — he says he'll decide this summer break
stories.what_happened: Fernando Alonso has said he intends to make a decision about his Formula 1 future during the sport's two-week **summer shutdown**, which began July 31, with a call expected around **mid-August** — before the season resumes at the Dutch Grand Prix on August 21-23. Alonso's current Aston Martin contract runs through the end of **2026**, by which point he will be 45. He has said the team's forthcoming car upgrades are "not really connected" to his decision, implying the choice hinges more on his own appetite to keep racing than on the car's competitiveness. Sky Sports F1 pit-lane reporter Ted Kravitz has predicted Alonso will retire at season's end, framing it as a desire to pursue other pursuits rather than dissatisfaction with results. Alonso himself has given conflicting signals in recent months, at times suggesting he isn't ready to stop and hopes to race on beyond this year.
key_points: **Fernando Alonso**, F1's two-time world champion, says he will decide on his racing future during the sport's mandatory **summer break**, with a call expected around **mid-August**.
Alonso is contracted to **Aston Martin through the end of 2026**, when he will be **45 years old**.
He insists Aston Martin's upcoming car upgrade package is **"not really connected"** to his decision — suggesting motivation, not results, is the deciding factor.
Sky Sports pit-lane reporter **Ted Kravitz** predicts Alonso will retire at season's end, saying it's about wanting to do "other stuff," not frustration with the car.
Alonso has sent mixed signals himself, at other times saying he isn't ready to walk away and hopes to keep racing beyond 2026.

depth.background: Alonso made his F1 debut in **2001** and won back-to-back world titles in **2005 and 2006**, making him one of the sport's most decorated active drivers. He has raced on and off at the sport's front and back of the grid for over two decades, including a mid-career detour into other racing series before returning to F1. His current team, Aston Martin, has been investing heavily to build a championship-capable car, and design chief Adrian Newey has been working on future models — all while Aston Martin is simultaneously reported to be chasing other drivers, including Williams's Carlos Sainz, adding extra intrigue to what Alonso decides.

stories.title: Modi launches a 100-week nationwide drive to pledge India's youth against drug abuse
stories.what_happened: Modi launched the campaign at 11 AM on August 2 via video conference, with Union ministers Mansukh Mandaviya and Piyush Goyal among those publicly backing it. The stated goal is to get more than **1 crore youth** to take a formal pledge against substance abuse, organized through MY Bharat volunteers. Unlike a single pledge-and-forget event, the plan runs for **100 weeks**, with recurring Sunday activities — sports, walkathons, meditation sessions, cultural programs, nukkad nataks (street plays), art competitions and community discussion forums — intended to sustain public participation. Goyal described it as laying 'the foundation for a Viksit Bharat,' tying the anti-drug message directly to the government's 2047 developed-nation goal.
key_points: PM Modi launched the **'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan'** (Drug-Free Youth for a Developed India pledge campaign) on **August 2** via video conference.
The campaign aims to unite over **1 crore (10 million) youth** in a pledge against substance abuse, coordinated through **MY Bharat** volunteers nationwide.
It kicks off a **100-week** 'Jan Bhagidari' (people's-participation) drive, not a one-day event.
Weekly Sunday activities — sports, walkathons, meditation, street plays, art contests — are meant to keep the campaign active rather than symbolic.
The push is framed as part of the government's **'Viksit Bharat 2047'** vision — reaching developed-nation status by India's 100th year of independence.

depth.background: India has one of the world's youngest populations, often called its **'demographic dividend'** — the idea that a large working-age youth cohort can drive decades of economic growth. Officials have grown increasingly vocal about drug abuse, including synthetic drugs, as a threat to that advantage, particularly in border and northeastern states. **MY Bharat** is the government's existing youth-volunteer platform, used here as the delivery mechanism for the pledge drive. The launch fits a pattern of large, symbolic national campaigns (similar in style to past sanitation or digital-literacy drives) meant to shift public behavior through sustained, repeated engagement rather than a single announcement.

stories.title: Sudanese army drone strike kills dozens at a rural court in Darfur
stories.what_happened: On **Sunday**, Sudanese army drones struck a traditional community court in **Garra al-Zawaya**, a village near Kabkabiya in North Darfur under RSF control. The strike landed at around **1pm local time (11:00 GMT)**, while tribal and community leaders were holding an open-air hearing under a tree to settle local land and tribal disputes. A rights group monitoring the war reported at least **35 people killed**, while the RSF's own local administration put the toll higher, at **37 dead and 50 wounded**. Among the dead were **four tribal leaders** and **two RSF commanders** who were present for the hearing. The village lies about **150km west of El-Fasher**, the city the RSF captured after a long siege last October, and the strike fits an escalating pattern of drone warfare on that front since then.
key_points: A Sudanese army drone strike killed at least **35 people** at a community court in North Darfur's Garra al-Zawaya village.
The dead included **four tribal leaders** and **two RSF commanders** attending a land-dispute hearing held under a tree.
The RSF-run local administration says the real toll is **37 killed and 50 wounded**.
The site sits **150km west of El-Fasher**, the city the paramilitary RSF captured from the army in a bloody siege last October.
The UN says over **1,000 civilians** have died in drone strikes in Sudan's war so far this year alone.

depth.background: Sudan's civil war has raged since **April 2023** between the regular army (SAF) and the **Rapid Support Forces (RSF)**, a paramilitary force descended from the government-backed 'Janjaweed' militias that once terrorized Darfur and later turned into a rival power center. The war has caused the **world's largest displacement crisis**, uprooting more than 13 million people, with famine already declared in parts of Darfur. Since the RSF seized **El-Fasher**, the army's last major foothold in Darfur, after a prolonged and bloody siege last October, both sides have leaned harder on cheap, widely available armed drones to hit each other's territory — often striking the civilians living under the other side's control rather than soldiers.

stories.title: SBI Research raises India's Q1 growth estimate to around 7%, days before the RBI's rate decision
stories.what_happened: SBI Research said in a note that India's economy likely grew around **7%** in the April-June quarter, well above the RBI's 6.6% projection, citing stronger auto sales, power demand, exports and industrial production than expected. The bank also pointed to a turnaround in the monsoon: July brought surplus rainfall that cut the nationwide rainfall deficit to roughly **13%**, with reservoir levels back to normal — good news for farm output and rural spending later in the year. The report comes just before the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee meets from **August 3 to 5**, with most economists still expecting the RBI to hold its key repo rate steady at **5.25%** for a sixth straight meeting, since inflation is expected to stay above 5% for two more quarters.
key_points: SBI Research now expects **~7% GDP growth** for April-June, above the RBI's own forecast
The RBI had cut its own Q1 forecast to **6.6%**, citing the Middle East conflict
**July's surplus monsoon rain** cut the nationwide rainfall deficit to about 13%
Strong **auto sales, power demand, exports and factory output** are driving the upgrade
The RBI's rate-setting panel meets **August 3-5**, with a decision due August 5

depth.background: India's central bank, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, sets interest rates roughly every two months through its **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**. Heading into this month's meeting, the RBI had actually lowered its own growth forecast for the April-June quarter — called **Q1 of FY27**, India's fiscal year running April to March — to 6.6%, partly due to uncertainty from the Israel-Iran war and its effect on oil prices. State Bank of India's research arm, one of the most closely watched private forecasters, publishes its own 'pre-policy' estimate ahead of each RBI meeting.

stories.title: West Indies win the toss and bat first in the series-deciding 2nd Test against Pakistan
stories.what_happened: At the toss for the second and final Test in Port of Spain, Pakistan's Babar Azam lost the call and West Indies opted to **bat first** — a decision that puts early pressure on Pakistan's bowling attack, led by Mohammad Ali and Sajid Khan, against a home side already 1-0 up. Pakistan's batting order shows Azan Awais opening alongside Imam-ul-Haq, with Abdullah Shafique also in the XI, reflecting the uncertainty in Pakistan's top order after the first-Test loss. West Indies field their settled top order of Tagenarine Chanderpaul, Brandon King, and Kavem Hodge in front of captain Roston Chase.
key_points: West Indies won the toss and **chose to bat first** at Queen's Park Oval, Port of Spain.
West Indies lead the two-match series **1-0** after winning the first Test by **90 runs**.
Pakistan, missing usual captain Shan Masood from the leadership role, are led by **Babar Azam** for this series decider.
Pakistan's XI includes **Azan Awais** and **Abdullah Shafique** both in the top order as the batting group is reshuffled.
A West Indies win completes a **series sweep**; Pakistan must win outright to level it.

depth.background: Pakistan arrived in the Caribbean already under pressure, having lost the first Test of this two-match series by **90 runs** on July 25 — a defeat built on a five-wicket haul from West Indies quick **Jayden Seales** and a lone fighting fifty from Babar Azam that wasn't enough. That defeat saw the captaincy handed to **Babar Azam** instead of Shan Masood for this decider. West Indies, under **Roston Chase**, sense a rare chance to complete a clean sweep of Pakistan at home.

thread.previously: We reported Pakistan, trailing 0-1 in the series, had handed the captaincy to Babar Azam instead of Shan Masood for this must-win Test, with Abdullah Shafique and Kamran Shakeel competing for the final specialist-batting spot.
thread.changed: Play has now started: West Indies won the toss and chose to bat first, meaning Pakistan must bowl first in the match they need to win to level the series, and the confirmed XI shows both Azan Awais and Abdullah Shafique in the top order.

stories.title: Babar Azam — not Shan Masood — leads Pakistan into today's must-win second Test as Shafique and Shakeel fight for a spot
stories.what_happened: As the second Test began today, **August 2**, at Queen's Park Oval in Port of Spain, Pakistan's likely playing XI confirmed **Babar Azam as captain**, with **Mohammad Rizwan** behind the stumps. Head coach **Sarfaraz Ahmed** said the choice between **Abdullah Shafique** and **Saud Shakeel** to fill Masood's middle-order spot would only be finalized at the **toss**, with uncapped batter **Awais Zafar** still technically in contention as a third option. Masood's **fractured left index finger** — sustained batting through pain during Pakistan's first-Test century — was formally confirmed by the **Pakistan Cricket Board** on Thursday following a scan and clinical assessment, and rules him out of this match entirely. Pakistan enter the Test trailing the series **1-0** after their 90-run defeat in Tarouba, meaning only a win keeps the series alive.
key_points: Pakistan's likely XI for the second Test has **Babar Azam as captain**, with **Mohammad Rizwan** keeping wicket.
Head coach **Sarfaraz Ahmed** said the final call between **Abdullah Shafique** and **Saud Shakeel** — both filling in for the injured Shan Masood — won't be made until the **toss**.
Uncapped batter **Awais Zafar** remains a **third option** for Masood's middle-order spot.
Masood's finger fracture was **confirmed by PCB on Thursday** after a scan and clinical assessment.
Pakistan trail the series **1-0** and must win at Queen's Park Oval just to draw it.

depth.background: Pakistan lost the first Test of this two-match series by 90 runs at Tarouba despite a Shan Masood century, collapsing to 120 all out while chasing 211. Masood was hit on the finger by West Indies quick Jayden Seales during that innings and has since been ruled out of the second Test. Abdullah Shafique and Saud Shakeel were added to the squad earlier in the tour after another batter, Abdullah Fazal, was ruled out with a back injury — meaning Pakistan already had cover in place before Masood's injury.

thread.previously: We reported Masood was ruled out of the second Test with a fractured finger, and that Pakistan — already 1-0 down — would have to win this match just to draw the series.

stories.title: Jasprit Bumrah ruled out of India's upcoming Test series in Sri Lanka with a knee injury
stories.what_happened: India's team management confirmed that **Jasprit Bumrah** will not be available for the upcoming **two-match Test series in Sri Lanka**, with the first Test starting in **Galle on August 15** and the second in **Colombo from August 23**. Bumrah has been nursing discomfort in his **left knee** since the T20 World Cup earlier this year, and re-aggravated the issue while fielding during a recent **ODI against England in Cardiff**. The BCCI's medical staff have advised that he needs more time to fully recover rather than risk returning early. **Auqib Nabi**, a seam-bowling all-rounder from Jammu & Kashmir, has emerged as the front-runner to be added to the squad as his replacement.
key_points: India's premier fast bowler **Jasprit Bumrah** will miss the **two-Test series in Sri Lanka**, starting **August 15** in Galle.
The injury is **left knee discomfort** that Bumrah has been managing since the **T20 World Cup** earlier this year.
He first aggravated it while **fielding against England** in an ODI in Cardiff.
BCCI's medical team has advised **against rushing him back** before he's fully recovered.
**Auqib Nabi**, a Jammu & Kashmir seam-bowling all-rounder, is the **front-runner** to replace him in the squad.

depth.background: Jasprit Bumrah is widely regarded as the best fast bowler in world cricket and has carried a heavy fast-bowling workload for India across formats for years, including through this year's T20 World Cup. India's team management has been managing his workload carefully given a history of back and now knee issues, resting him from some matches to keep him available for the biggest series.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill nine in Gaza for a second straight day as a top minister says there's 'no deal' to stop the attacks
stories.what_happened: Israeli forces carried out strikes across Gaza on **Sunday, August 2**, killing at least **nine Palestinians** — the second consecutive day of fatal strikes after seven were killed on Saturday. Israeli Energy Minister **Eli Cohen** said on Sunday that **no deal exists** to stop the attacks, and argued that since Israel already controls about **70% of Gaza**, it should move to take the rest. His comments directly contradict the picture of a de-escalating ceasefire that the Trump administration and the Board of Peace have been describing since Hamas signed its disarmament framework on July 31. Hamas, for its part, has said it will not implement its side of the deal — handing weapons to Palestinian-run storage sites vetted by Israeli intelligence — until Israel fulfils its own commitment to withdraw troops from Gaza. Neither side has publicly declared the ceasefire framework dead, but the gap between the announced deal and events on the ground is widening by the day.
key_points: Israeli strikes killed at least **nine Palestinians** in Gaza on **Sunday**, the second straight day of deadly attacks.
Israeli Energy Minister **Eli Cohen** said publicly there is **no deal to halt the attacks** on Gaza.
Cohen said Israel — which already controls **70% of the Strip** — should take **full control** of the rest.
The strikes come despite Trump's announced **breakthrough** on implementing last year's Gaza ceasefire and Hamas's **disarmament agreement**.
Hamas has said it won't act on the disarmament deal unless Israel first **withdraws its forces** as promised.

depth.background: In late July, Hamas signed a **15-point disarmament framework** — agreeing to hand its weapons into Palestinian-run storage sites — in the biggest step yet toward ending nearly two years of war in Gaza. But Israel never fully signed on, saying the deal doesn't meet its demand for **complete demilitarization**, and Israeli strikes have continued through the two-week window meant to work out how the plan is actually carried out. The US-backed **Board of Peace**, which oversees the plan, published the disarmament mechanics on July 31, but implementation on the ground hasn't matched the diplomacy.

thread.previously: We reported Israeli strikes had killed at least seven Palestinians on Saturday and destroyed medicine warehouses next to a hospital, even as the Board of Peace published its first detailed blueprint for how Hamas's weapons would move into Palestinian-run, Shin Bet-vetted storage under international oversight.
thread.changed: The strikes continued into a second day, killing nine more people on Sunday, and — for the first time — a senior Israeli minister publicly said no deal exists to stop the attacks and floated Israel taking full control of Gaza, directly contradicting the diplomatic narrative around the disarmament framework.

stories.title: Kerala floods and landslides kill at least 11, with a Karnataka landslide adding 3 more
stories.what_happened: Intense monsoon rainfall from the night of **July 31 into August 1** triggered flash floods and landslides across Kerala, killing at least **8 people** with **8 more missing** and **13 injured**, according to figures confirmed by Kerala's Chief Minister. A separate landslide across the border in **Karnataka** killed at least **3 more people**. Kerala's State Disaster Management Authority placed **12 districts** — including Idukki, Kottayam, Pathanamthitta, Wayanad and Kozhikode — under an **orange rainfall alert**. Nearly **5,792 people** were evacuated to **209 relief camps**, and officials reported **27 houses destroyed** and **196 more partially damaged**, with rescue teams still working through hill villages in the Western Ghats.
key_points: Heavy rain triggered **floods and landslides across Kerala**, killing at least **8 people confirmed dead**, with **8 more missing** and **13 injured**.
A separate landslide in neighbouring **Karnataka killed at least 3 people**.
Kerala's disaster authority placed **12 districts under an orange alert**, including Idukki, Kottayam, Wayanad and Kozhikode.
Nearly **5,792 people were moved to 209 relief camps**; **27 houses were destroyed** and 196 more damaged.
The worst-hit districts sit in the **Western Ghats**, a steep hill range that turns intense rain into fast landslides.

depth.background: Kerala's hilly **Western Ghats** districts — Idukki, Wayanad, Kottayam among them — flood almost every monsoon because steep, deforested slopes can't absorb heavy rain fast enough, sending water and loosened earth downhill in landslides that can bury homes with little warning. The state has suffered major flood disasters before, most notably in **2018**, when the worst floods in nearly a century killed hundreds and displaced over a million people. This year's rain arrived in an intense burst overnight from **July 31 into August 1**, catching several hill villages off guard.

stories.title: A 2.9-magnitude earthquake rattles north Delhi before dawn — the second tremor to hit the capital region in two days
stories.what_happened: A **magnitude-2.9 earthquake** struck Delhi's North district at **4:14am on Sunday**, according to India's National Center for Seismology, with its epicentre at a shallow depth of about **8 kilometres** near latitude 28.72°N, longitude 76.96°E. It was the **second earthquake felt across Delhi-NCR in as many days**. Tremors were described as mild, and because the quake struck in the pre-dawn hours, many residents who were asleep did not notice it at all. No damage or injuries were reported.
key_points: A **magnitude-2.9 earthquake** struck Delhi's North district at **4:14am** on Sunday, per the National Center for Seismology.
The quake's epicentre was at a shallow depth of **8 kilometres**.
It was the **second tremor** felt in the Delhi-NCR region within two days.
**No damage or injuries** were reported; many residents asleep at the time didn't notice it.
Delhi sits in a **moderate-to-high seismic risk zone** due to its proximity to Himalayan fault systems.

depth.background: Delhi and the surrounding National Capital Region (NCR) lie in **Seismic Zone IV** on India's four-tier hazard map — the second-highest risk category — because of their proximity to active Himalayan fault lines where the Indian tectonic plate is slowly pushing under the Eurasian plate. Small tremors like this one are common and rarely cause damage on their own, but seismologists watch clusters of minor quakes in the same area as a possible sign of stress building up along a fault.

stories.title: An 'unknown projectile' hits another tanker off Oman, showing the Strait of Hormuz crisis still isn't over
stories.what_happened: The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency (**UKMTO**) said a tanker was struck by an **unknown projectile** early Saturday about **12.5 nautical miles off Lima, Oman**, with the impact damaging the vessel's **engine room**. No injuries were reported and the ship remained afloat, but it lost some maneuverability. In a separate, nearby incident the same day, another vessel reported a **large explosion close to it**, without direct impact. Both incidents sit inside the same narrow shipping lane that has already absorbed a string of similar strikes in July, including on a Qatari LNG tanker. Neither Iran nor any other party has directly claimed this specific attack, continuing a pattern where Tehran neither confirms nor denies individual strikes while keeping the region on edge. The incident adds to evidence that, despite talk of a **ceasefire framework**, the Strait of Hormuz remains a live conflict zone for merchant shipping.
key_points: A tanker was struck by an **unknown projectile** roughly **12.5 nautical miles off Lima, Oman**, damaging its engine room — no injuries reported.
Britain's maritime watchdog, **UKMTO**, logged **two separate incidents** in the same stretch of water within hours of each other.
This is at least the **fourth distinct tanker-strike incident** near the Strait of Hormuz in barely a week, on top of the near-total shipping shutdown already in place.
Traffic through the strait — a passage that normally carries **~88 ships a day** — has been running at roughly **10 ships a day** since the crisis deepened.
**No group has claimed responsibility**; Iran has not directly claimed this specific strike, continuing its pattern of ambiguity around the attacks.

depth.background: The **Strait of Hormuz** is a narrow chokepoint between Iran and Oman that roughly **one-fifth of the world's oil and a fifth of its liquefied natural gas** pass through — there is no practical detour for most of that volume. Since a **US-Iran war broke out in late February 2026**, Iran has repeatedly threatened and periodically attacked shipping in the strait as leverage, while insisting it isn't fully closing the waterway. Independent trackers like **Kpler** have shown traffic collapsing even when Iran doesn't formally claim a blockade, because insurers and shipowners simply stop sending vessels through a war zone. Multiple tankers — Qatari, Saudi and now this latest one — have already been hit by projectiles in the weeks before this incident.

thread.previously: We reported that transits through the strait had collapsed to roughly 10 ships a day (from a normal ~88), after Iran claimed intercepting two more vessels on July 31 and oil prices rose over 1% — a crisis running since late February 2026.
thread.changed: A new, distinct tanker strike has now hit a vessel's engine room off Oman, with UKMTO logging a second nearby incident the same day — showing the danger to shipping hasn't eased even as talk of a ceasefire framework continues.

stories.title: Guyana Amazon Warriors beat San Francisco Unicorns by 6 runs to defend their Global Super League title
stories.what_happened: **Guyana Amazon Warriors** successfully defended their **Global Super League** title, beating the **San Francisco Unicorns by 6 runs** in Saturday's final at **Providence Stadium** in Guyana. Batting first, Guyana were bowled out for **85**, a modest total built around a late unbeaten **17 from Dwaine Pretorius**. In reply, the Unicorns fell short at **79**, with the match wrapped up inside **18.3 overs** in a low-scoring, tightly contested finish. **Pretorius** was named **Player of the Match** for his all-round contribution — 17 not out with the bat and **3 wickets for 24 runs** with the ball. Teammate **Mohammad Nabi** was named **Player of the Series**, having contributed **53 runs and 10 wickets** across the tournament. For the Unicorns, it capped a remarkable run that included a **Major League Cricket 2026** title and a comprehensive **8-wicket win over Desert Vipers** in the qualifier — but their first-ever GSL final appearance ended in a narrow defeat.
key_points: **Guyana Amazon Warriors** successfully defended their title, beating **San Francisco Unicorns by 6 runs** in the 2026 Global Super League final at Providence Stadium.
Guyana posted **85 runs**; the Unicorns fell just short at **79**, with the match decided inside **18.3 overs**.
All-rounder **Dwaine Pretorius** was Player of the Match, finishing unbeaten on **17 and taking 3 wickets for 24 runs**.
**Mohammad Nabi** of Guyana was named Player of the Series, having scored **53 runs and taken 10 wickets** across the tournament.
For the Unicorns — fresh off winning **Major League Cricket 2026** in the US — it was a first-ever GSL final appearance, ending in heartbreak.

depth.background: The **Global Super League (GSL)** is a T10-style franchise tournament based in Guyana, drawing teams and players from across the global T20 circuit, including US-based franchises expanding the sport's footprint in North America. San Francisco Unicorns arrived at this final on a hot streak, having just won **Major League Cricket 2026** in the United States and then beating Desert Vipers by 8 wickets in Friday's qualifier to reach their first-ever GSL final. Guyana Amazon Warriors, by contrast, were the tournament's most consistent side all season — finishing top of the league table and entering the final as defending champions with home advantage at Providence Stadium.

thread.previously: We reported the Unicorns had reached their first-ever GSL final by beating Desert Vipers by 8 wickets, setting up a title clash against defending champions and league table-toppers Guyana Amazon Warriors at Providence Stadium.
thread.changed: The final has now been played and decided — Guyana Amazon Warriors won by 6 runs to defend their title, with Dwaine Pretorius named Player of the Match and Mohammad Nabi Player of the Series.

stories.title: A 'heat dome' sends Las Vegas to 115°F and Phoenix toward 116°F, spiking wildfire risk across the Western US
stories.what_happened: The National Weather Service issued an Extreme Heat Warning on **August 1 at 5:22pm PDT**, in effect through **August 2 at 8:00pm PDT**, covering the Mojave Desert with forecast highs of **110–120°F**. Las Vegas reached **115°F on Saturday** — about 10°F above normal and its hottest day of 2026 — with Sunday forecast at 114°F, just shy of the all-time daily record of 116°F. Phoenix was forecast to hit **116°F (47°C)**, while El Centro, California, was expected to tie or break its own record at **118°F (48°C)**. Heat advisories were also issued for the Los Angeles Basin, Salt Lake City, and other parts of the Mountain West. Meteorologists described the heat dome as likely to be relatively short-lived, easing after the weekend.
key_points: A **heat dome** — a ridge of high pressure trapping hot air near the ground — settled over the Southwest and Mountain West this weekend.
Las Vegas hit **115°F on Saturday**, its hottest day of 2026, just one degree off the all-time daily record.
Phoenix was forecast to reach **116°F (47°C)**; El Centro, California, to a record **118°F (48°C)**.
The National Weather Service issued **Extreme Heat Warnings** across the Mojave Desert, in effect through Sunday night.
Forecasters warn the extreme heat plus dry vegetation is **raising wildfire ignition risk** across the region.

depth.background: A heat dome forms when a large area of high-pressure air gets trapped over a region and compresses as it sinks, warming the air below and blocking clouds that would otherwise cool things down — it's the mechanism behind most major US summer heat waves. The Western US, especially the desert Southwest, has seen increasingly extreme and longer-lasting heat events in recent summers, which climate scientists link to a warming baseline climate. This weekend's dome stretched from Arizona to Montana, hitting cities from Las Vegas to Salt Lake City.

stories.title: An Indonesian ferry fire kills 5 and leaves dozens missing off Java, as passengers jumped into the sea to survive
stories.what_happened: The passenger ferry Mutiara Sentosa 2 caught fire in the Java Sea between 6 and 7 a.m. local time on Sunday, August 2, while en route from Surabaya to Makassar with 232 passengers, 39 crew, and 181 vehicles — mostly trucks and an excavator — on board. A survivor said the blaze started from a truck on the vehicle deck and spread across it in under half an hour. Panicked passengers jumped into the sea, some floating for hours before a passing ship began pulling them out of the water. By Monday, officials said roughly **225–230 people had been rescued**, but conceded the vessel had likely been carrying more people than its manifest listed, making the true number still missing genuinely unclear. Four other vessels stood by near the burning ferry but could not approach directly because of the fire risk from flammable materials on board. Indonesian search-and-rescue teams have continued combing the Java Sea for survivors and bodies in the days since.
key_points: The ferry **Mutiara Sentosa 2** caught fire between **6 and 7 a.m.** while carrying 232 passengers, 39 crew, and 181 vehicles.
**5 people confirmed dead**, with dozens still unaccounted for after some jumped overboard.
Around **225–230 people were rescued**, many pulled from the water by a passing ship.
A survivor says the blaze started from a **truck on the lower vehicle deck**, then spread within half an hour.
Standby rescue vessels initially **couldn't approach** because flammable cargo on board made the fire too dangerous.

depth.background: Indonesia is a vast archipelago of over **17,000 islands**, and overloaded, aging inter-island ferries are one of the country's most persistent safety hazards — regulators have repeatedly been criticized for lax enforcement of passenger and cargo limits. The **Mutiara Sentosa 2** was sailing a routine but long overnight route from Surabaya (East Java) to Makassar (South Sulawesi) when the fire broke out at sea, far from immediate help. Vehicle decks carrying trucks and heavy cargo are a known fire risk on these ferries because leaking fuel or electrical faults can ignite quickly in cramped, poorly ventilated spaces.

stories.title: Iran says a deal with Oman on a new Strait of Hormuz shipping route is in its 'final stages'
stories.what_happened: Iranian Foreign Minister **Abbas Araghchi** said Tehran's negotiations with Oman over a new Hormuz shipping arrangement are in their **'final stages'** and are 'on the way to being finalized.' Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson described the goal as **a route acceptable to both sides** — 'neither the northern route nor the southern route, but one that respects the sovereign rights of both.' This comes just a day after President Trump said direct US-Iran negotiations would begin Monday and claimed a deal was **'imminent,'** including the full reopening of the Strait and an end to Iran's nuclear program. Iran's spokesperson pushed back hard on that framing, stating flatly that Tehran is **'not negotiating with the United States at this time'** — suggesting the real, concrete progress is happening in the Iran-Oman channel, not the US-Iran one Trump is publicizing.
key_points: Iran's FM Abbas Araghchi says Oman talks on Hormuz are in **'final stages.'**
The plan is a **new maritime route** — not the existing shipping corridors either side already uses.
Iran's Foreign Ministry insists there are **no direct talks with the US** right now, contradicting Trump.
Trump has said any deal must include **'complete and total opening'** of the Strait and an end to Iran's nuclear threat.
About **one-fifth of global oil and gas** passes through this single 33km-wide chokepoint daily.

depth.background: The **Strait of Hormuz** is the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman that connects the oil-rich Persian Gulf to the open ocean — roughly **20% of the world's oil and LNG** sails through it every day, making it one of the most strategically important chokepoints on Earth. Tensions escalated sharply after a US-Iran military confrontation earlier this year, and Iran has periodically threatened to close or disrupt the Strait, which would spike global energy prices overnight. Because Iran and the US don't trust each other enough to negotiate directly in public, **Oman has stepped in as the go-between**, a role it has played in past US-Iran diplomacy (including the original 2015 nuclear deal talks).

thread.previously: We reported that Trump said direct US-Iran talks would begin Monday to lock in a deal reopening the Strait of Hormuz, but Tehran denied any imminent session with Washington.
thread.changed: Iran has now confirmed real progress — but not with the US directly. Tehran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says talks with Oman (acting as mediator) over a new shipping route through the Strait are 'on the way to being finalized,' even as Iran's Foreign Ministry insists it is 'not negotiating with the United States at this time.'

stories.title: England has its earliest harvest on record — and farmers warn it means food shortages ahead
stories.what_happened: The Agriculture and Horticulture Development Board's first 2026 harvest report found England had its **earliest harvest since records began in 2006**, with many farmers across the south and east finishing **two to three weeks ahead** of the long-term average — a sign crops matured under stress, not abundance. NFU president **Tom Bradshaw** said wheat and oat yields were **'very, very poor'** this year and warned plainly that **'it does feel like there is going to be some shortages of food products,'** with Britain likely to lean more heavily on imports to cover the gap. Drought has been formally declared across large parts of England and the whole of Wales, and **more than 20 million people** are now living under hosepipe bans restricting garden and non-essential water use. This is the **third drought in five years** to hit UK farming, and Bradshaw is pushing the government for tax breaks that would let farmers invest in on-farm water storage.
key_points: NFU president Tom Bradshaw says **'there is going to be some shortages of food products'**
England's harvest is the **earliest since records began in 2006**, finishing 2-3 weeks early
Wheat and oat yields are **'very, very poor'** this year, Bradshaw says
More than **20 million people** in England and Wales are now under **hosepipe bans**
This is the **third drought in five years** — farmers call it the 'new normal'

depth.background: The UK doesn't usually associate itself with drought and food-supply fears — but a run of **successive heatwaves** in 2026 has left soil across southern and eastern England bone-dry, on top of two similarly dry years in the past five. Farming groups have warned for years that climate change is shifting Britain's weather toward more frequent extreme heat and rainfall swings, stressing a food system built around a fairly stable, temperate climate. The **National Farmers' Union (NFU)** is the main lobbying voice for British agriculture, and its president publicly pushing the government for action signals the industry sees this as more than a one-off bad year.

stories.title: China's coast guard 'deeply destabilizing' patrols near Taiwan draw a rare US rebuke
stories.what_happened: China's Coast Guard said a formation led by the vessel **Xiushan** has intensified patrols in waters east of Taiwan, part of 'special maritime law enforcement operations' Beijing has run since **June**. The United States government publicly called the patrols **'deeply destabilizing'** and urged Beijing to end what it described as a pressure campaign against Taipei — a notably sharp choice of words for a coast guard deployment rather than a military one. Taiwan's Coast Guard Administration says it is closely monitoring the patrols and has sent its own **4,000-tonne Chiayi-class vessel, the Taipei (CG5005)**, to the area. China says the operations are a response to talks between Japan and the Philippines over maritime boundary lines in the same waters, and insists its patrols are 'beyond reproach.' Taiwan says China's move asserts authority over territory it has never actually controlled.
key_points: US officials call China's patrols **'deeply destabilizing'**, an unusually blunt condemnation
China Coast Guard's **Xiushan-led task force** has intensified patrols in waters **east of Taiwan** since July
Beijing has run **'special maritime law enforcement operations'** in the area since **June**
Taiwan deployed the **4,000-tonne Chiayi-class vessel Taipei (CG5005)** to monitor the patrols
China frames the escalation as a response to **Japan-Philippines talks** on maritime boundaries

depth.background: Taiwan is a self-governing island of **23 million people** that China's Communist Party claims as its own territory, despite never having ruled it. For decades, Beijing has used a mix of military drills, coast guard patrols, and diplomatic pressure — short of actual invasion — to assert its claim, a strategy often called a **'gray-zone' campaign** because it stays just below the threshold of war. The waters **east of Taiwan** matter because they sit outside the narrower Taiwan Strait and touch areas Taiwan has quietly administered for **over 70 years**. China's coast guard, unlike its navy, lets Beijing project force while framing it as civilian law enforcement — making it harder for the US and allies to respond without escalating.

stories.title: Damon Hill says George Russell vs Kimi Antonelli reminds him of his own 1996 title fight
stories.what_happened: Hill said Antonelli's trajectory mirrors his own experience with Villeneuve: **'Kimi's had a season in F1, and over the winter there's a kind of gestation period where all the things you've learned in the year sink in, and you suddenly come out fighting.'** In 1996, Hill took **eight race wins** and never qualified outside the top two en route to the title, beating rookie Villeneuve by **19 points**. Hill's comparison implies Antonelli, now in his **second F1 season**, has gone through the same learning curve and is emerging as a genuine threat to Russell inside the same Mercedes garage, rather than an external rival.
key_points: Hill compares Russell-Antonelli to his **1996 rivalry with Jacques Villeneuve**
Hill won that **1996 title** with eight wins, beating Villeneuve by **19 points**
Hill says a rookie's first season is a **'gestation period'** before they come back stronger
Antonelli, in his **second F1 season**, is now genuinely challenging teammate Russell

depth.background: **Damon Hill** won the 1996 Formula 1 World Championship driving for Williams, in a season defined by his rivalry with rookie teammate **Jacques Villeneuve**, who pushed him hard before Hill won out. Nearly three decades later, Mercedes finds itself with a similar dynamic: **George Russell**, an established team leader, now faces a serious title challenge from his own young teammate, **Kimi Antonelli**, in Antonelli's second season. Hill, now a respected F1 pundit, draws the parallel because both cases involve an experienced number-one driver getting pushed by a fast-improving teammate from within their own team — arguably the most uncomfortable kind of rivalry in racing, since there's nowhere to hide within the same garage.

stories.title: BCCI will keep paying Ajinkya Rahane a ₹70,000 monthly pension even after his retirement
stories.what_happened: Days after Ajinkya Rahane announced his retirement from all international cricket, it's been confirmed he qualifies for the BCCI's **elite player pension scheme**, thanks to a long international career spanning **85 Tests, 90 ODIs, and 20 T20Is**. Under the board's **2022-revised pension structure**, he'll receive **₹70,000 per month** — up from the ₹50,000 top-tier former players received under the earlier scheme. There is one condition: if Rahane takes on a **full-time BCCI role**, such as a national or state coaching position or a selector's post, the monthly pension will be **temporarily suspended** for as long as he holds that job, and can resume once he leaves it.
key_points: Rahane qualifies for BCCI's **elite pension scheme** after playing **85 Tests, 90 ODIs and 20 T20Is** for India
He'll receive **₹70,000 a month** under the board's **2022-revised pension scheme**, up from ₹50,000 previously
The pension gets **suspended** if he takes a full-time BCCI role like coach or selector — but can resume if he later leaves that role
This follows his retirement from all international cricket, announced **July 30**

depth.background: The BCCI (Board of Control for Cricket in India) runs a **pension scheme for former international players** who meet career-length thresholds, as a form of long-term financial security once players stop earning central contracts and match fees. The scheme was **revised upward in 2022**, raising payouts for senior former players. Rahane retired from all formats of international cricket on **July 30, 2026** — a career that included being the hero of India's historic **2020-21 Border-Gavaskar Trophy win in Australia**, widely seen as one of Indian cricket's greatest overseas triumphs.

thread.previously: Rahane announced his retirement from all formats of international cricket, capping a career defined by his heroics in India's historic 2020-21 series win in Australia.
thread.changed: It's now been confirmed he qualifies for BCCI's elite pension scheme and will receive ₹70,000 a month, with a clause suspending payments if he takes a full-time BCCI role.

stories.title: Two firefighting helicopter crew killed in mid-air collision as Greece's wildfires spiral
stories.what_happened: On Sunday, August 2, two Bell helicopters dropping water on a fast-spreading wildfire near Psatha, in Greece's Boeotia region, collided in mid-air. Video showed the lower helicopter's rotor striking the underside of the aircraft above it before it crashed and caught fire. The Greek and Danish crew of one helicopter died; the Greek and British crew of the second aircraft survived after an emergency landing. The fire they were fighting had ignited the previous day and spread rapidly in gale-force winds, destroying more than **100 homes** and triggering evacuations across the Boeotia and Attica regions. Greek authorities deployed nearly **500 firefighters**, with reinforcements flown in from France and Romania, but officials said high winds meant aircraft in many cases cannot draw water or carry out drops due to turbulence.
key_points: Two water-dropping helicopters collided mid-air over **Psatha**, in the Boeotia/Attica region about **45 miles** northwest of Athens, on Sunday
**2 of 4** crew died — a Greek and a Danish national; a British and a Greek crew member on the other aircraft survived
The wildfire they were fighting has already destroyed more than **100 homes** and forced evacuations across two regions
Nearly **500 firefighters**, backed by reinforcements from France and Romania, are battling the blaze amid gale-force winds
It's part of a wider European wildfire season already burning close to **half a million hectares** since January, ahead of 2025's record pace

depth.background: Southern Europe has faced a brutal heatwave-driven wildfire season through July and August 2026, with France, Spain and Greece all fighting major blazes that have collectively burned close to **half a million hectares** since January — already outpacing 2025, itself the worst year on record. The EU's shared rescEU firefighting fleet, made up of planes, helicopters and pre-positioned crews from member states, has been stretched thin fighting fires in multiple countries at once. Aerial firefighting — using aircraft to scoop up water and drop it on flames — is inherently risky, especially amid the high winds and smoke that accompany major fires.

stories.title: Ben Duckett becomes The Hundred's leading run-scorer as Trent Rockets edge SunRisers Leeds
stories.what_happened: Batting first, Trent Rockets got a rapid start from **Aneurin Donald**, playing his first match of the campaign, who smashed **40 not out** off just 19 balls including three sixes. **Ben Duckett** then took over, reaching his third half-century of the tournament from 35 balls and adding a 50-run stand with Tim David before falling for **64** — a knock that made him the competition's leading run-scorer, overtaking England team-mate Phil Salt. Rockets posted **146 for 4**. In reply, Mitchell Marsh and Zak Crawley gave SunRisers Leeds a solid start, reaching 32 for 1 after the powerplay. Harry Brook threatened to take the game away before being caught by Duckett off Mohammad Amir for 46. Amir then struck twice more in the death overs, finishing with **2 for 20**, as SunRisers fell 5 runs short on **141 for 4**.
key_points: **Trent Rockets** beat **SunRisers Leeds** by **5 runs** at Trent Bridge to stay top of the Men's Hundred table.
**Ben Duckett** smashed **64** off 47 balls, overtaking Phil Salt to become the competition's **leading run-scorer**.
**Aneurin Donald**, playing his first game of the tournament, blitzed a 19-ball **40 not out** with three sixes.
Pakistan pace veteran **Mohammad Amir** took 2 wickets for 20 runs in the death overs to seal the win.
Harry Brook fell for 46, caught by Duckett himself, as SunRisers fell 5 runs short chasing 147.

depth.background: The Hundred splits each match into 100-ball innings rather than the usual 120-ball T20 format, rewarding explosive hitting and tight death bowling. **Trent Rockets** have been one of the standout men's teams this season, and this was their third successive win, while **SunRisers Leeds**, led by Australian all-rounder Mitchell Marsh, came into the game looking to keep pace near the top of the table.

stories.title: Audi shelves further F1 engine upgrades until 2027, blaming the budget cap
stories.what_happened: Audi racing director **Allan McNish** said the team will not bring a second power-unit upgrade before the 2026 season ends, having already used its one opportunity at the **Barcelona Grand Prix** in June. That update focused mainly on "driveability" — how smoothly the engine responds to throttle input — rather than outright horsepower, according to driver Nico Hulkenberg. McNish said the bigger, more powerful parts are being held back for **2027** because Audi simply doesn't have the budget to develop this year's and next year's engines at the same time within F1's cost cap. Asked whether the 2027 engine would be a big performance leap, McNish joked "That's '27... we're only halfway through '26," but confirmed it will mostly be new hardware rather than a quick fix. Audi qualified for F1's ADUO catch-up system — which grants extra development chances to manufacturers measured more than 4% off the fastest engine — earning two upgrade windows this year and two more in 2027. Even without more power, Audi's chassis has held up: the team has scored points in three consecutive races, with Gabriel Bortoleto (8 points) and Nico Hulkenberg (2 points) helping it edge past Williams for eighth in the constructors' championship.
key_points: Audi racing director Allan McNish confirmed the team won't bring a **second** power-unit upgrade before 2026 ends
Audi already used its one upgrade at the **Barcelona Grand Prix**, aimed mainly at driveability, not raw power
Bigger engine parts are being saved for **2027** because Audi can't afford to develop both years' engines within F1's roughly **$190 million** cost cap
Audi qualified for F1's catch-up rule (ADUO) after being measured more than **4%** off the pace-setting engine, earning two upgrade windows in 2026 and two more in 2027
Despite the underpowered engine, Audi has scored points in **three straight races**, passing Williams for 8th in the constructors' standings

depth.background: Audi entered Formula 1 in 2026 as a full manufacturer, taking over the former Sauber team and building its first power unit from scratch. Team boss is ex-Ferrari chief **Mattia Binotto**, who has always said the engine wouldn't be competitive immediately and that Audi's real goal is fighting for titles by **2030**. Under F1's 2026 rules, most engine development is frozen except for a new mechanism called **ADUO**, which hands lagging manufacturers limited catch-up upgrades. Every manufacturer also has to fit all of this inside a strict shared **cost cap** covering both engine and chassis work.

stories.title: Louisiana becomes the third state to open a criminal probe into Anthony Fauci over his COVID-19 testimony
stories.what_happened: On July 29, 2026, Fauci testified before a Senate committee investigating the origins of COVID-19 and the government's public messaging during the pandemic, and he **pleaded the Fifth** more than 100 times rather than answer questions. Newly released pages from his personal diary, kept throughout the pandemic, appear to show discrepancies between what he told the public and what he privately believed or knew. Florida's attorney general moved first, announcing a state investigation into Fauci's conduct; Alabama followed within days. On August 2, **Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill** announced her state would do the same, citing the hearing and the diary's contents as grounds for a fresh look at whether Fauci made false statements to state or federal bodies. No charges have been filed in any of the three states; each has only opened a preliminary investigation.
key_points: **Louisiana's attorney general** launched a probe into Anthony Fauci, joining **Alabama and Florida**
Fauci invoked his **Fifth Amendment right** more than **100 times** at a July 29 Senate hearing
Senators released **over 1,000 pages** of his pandemic-era diary, citing gaps with his public statements
A **2025 pardon from President Biden** covers only federal crimes — state charges can still proceed

depth.background: Anthony Fauci led the US National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases for decades and became the public face of America's COVID-19 response, championing lockdowns, mask mandates, and vaccine rollout. He has since become a lightning rod for Republican lawmakers who accuse him of downplaying the possibility that the virus leaked from a Chinese lab and of misleading Congress about US-funded research there. Before leaving office in January 2025, President Biden issued Fauci a **preemptive pardon** covering any federal offenses connected to his pandemic-era conduct. That pardon does not shield him from prosecution under **state law**, which is the opening several Republican attorneys general are now using.

stories.title: Independent Bihar MP Pappu Yadav is attacked with a shoe by a knife-carrying man during a Delhi press conference
stories.what_happened: During a press conference at his Delhi residence on Sunday, August 2, a man threw a shoe at Yadav before being tackled by his supporters. Yadav says the attacker, identified as Sumit, a resident of Bulandshahr in Uttar Pradesh, was carrying a knife that he intended to use, though he was stopped before he could act. The knife was handed over to police, who detained the attacker. Yadav alleged the assailant targeted him over remarks he had made that the attacker perceived as insulting to Hindu sadhus, and said he had received prior death threats and had already filed complaints with authorities about his safety.
key_points: A man hurled a **shoe** at Purnia MP **Pappu Yadav** during a Sunday press conference at his Delhi residence
Yadav says the attacker, identified as **Sumit** from Bulandshahr (UP), was also carrying a **knife**
Yadav's **supporters overpowered** the man before he could cause harm; police have detained him
The attacker reportedly acted over a **perceived insult to Hindu sadhus (holy men)** by Yadav

depth.background: Pappu Yadav is a well-known independent Lok Sabha MP from Purnia in Bihar, known for blunt, often controversial public remarks and a long history of run-ins with rivals and law enforcement over the years. He regularly holds press conferences at his Delhi residence, which is where Sunday's incident took place.

stories.title: Rashid Khan claims his maiden Hundred five-wicket haul as MI London thump Manchester Super Giants Men
stories.what_happened: MI London posted 183 for 6, built around fifties from **Will Jacks (62)** and **Nicholas Pooran (54)**, at their home ground. In reply, Manchester Super Giants Men were bowled out for 138, with Rashid Khan tearing through their middle and lower order to finish with figures of 5 for 17 — his best-ever return in the tournament. **Aiden Markham's 50** was the only substantial score MSG could muster as they slipped to a 45-run defeat. The win moves MI London up to second place in the men's points table as the group stage heads toward its business end.
key_points: **Rashid Khan** took a career-first **5 for 17** in the Men's Hundred, dismantling Manchester Super Giants
**MI London** won by **45 runs**, posting 183/6 (Jacks 62, Pooran 54) before bowling MSG out for 138
**Aiden Markham's 50** was the lone resistance as Rashid ran through the rest of the batting order
The win lifts **MI London to second place** in the men's competition table

depth.background: The Hundred is England's 100-balls-per-innings franchise tournament, running men's and women's competitions in parallel each August. Rashid Khan is one of world cricket's most respected leg-spinners, a veteran of franchise leagues worldwide, but had never previously taken a five-wicket haul in this specific competition despite years of taking wickets in it.

stories.title: India shakes up its coaching staff for the Sri Lanka Tests, naming a new fielding coach and losing an assistant to the IPL
stories.what_happened: The BCCI announced on Monday that **Subhadeep Ghosh**, a 57-year-old former Assam and Railways cricketer from Digboi, has been appointed India men's new fielding coach, replacing **T Dilip**, ahead of the upcoming two-Test tour of Sri Lanka. Ghosh previously spent two years coaching the **India women's team**, and was part of the support staff during the **2022 Women's ODI World Cup** and the **2023 Women's T20 World Cup**. As a player, he represented Assam and Railways in 17 first-class and 17 List A matches. Separately, assistant coach **Ryan ten Doeschate** has left the India setup to join the **Kolkata Knight Riders** as Head of Cricket Strategy, an IPL role.
key_points: BCCI appointed **Subhadeep Ghosh** as India men's new fielding coach ahead of the Sri Lanka Tests.
Ghosh, 57, from **Assam**, replaces **T Dilip** in the role.
He previously coached the **India women's team** for two years, including at two World Cups.
Assistant coach **Ryan ten Doeschate** has left to join **Kolkata Knight Riders** as Head of Cricket Strategy.
The changes land just before India's **two-Test series in Sri Lanka**, starting August 15 in Galle.

depth.background: India's tour of Sri Lanka is an important early assignment for **Shubman Gill's** side in the current World Test Championship cycle, and it comes as the team is already dealing with a personnel setback — pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah was ruled out of the series with a knee injury. Coaching staff changes like this one are less visible than playing XI news but shape how the team prepares and performs, and India's franchise T20 league, the IPL, regularly recruits national-team support staff — as it has here with ten Doeschate.

stories.title: Carlos Sainz says he still hasn't decided his F1 future, as Aston Martin's chase for him heats up
stories.what_happened: Carlos Sainz said in comments reported Sunday that **no decision has been made** about his Formula 1 future, as speculation continues to build around a potential move to Aston Martin. His current Williams contract runs through the end of **2026**, with an option that could extend it to 2027/28. Williams has struggled badly this season, sitting **ninth in the constructors' championship** with only **11 points**, compared to the 16 points Sainz alone had reached by this stage last year. Sky Sports pundit **Martin Brundle** said he fears Sainz's F1 career is **'stalling,'** describing him as **'down a cul-de-sac'** at a critical career moment. Sainz had reportedly asked his management to keep him out of driver-market conversations until the summer break — which has now arrived, putting pressure on him to start making a call.
key_points: Carlos Sainz says **no decision has been made** yet about his F1 future.
His Williams contract runs out at the end of **2026** unless he exercises a 2027/28 option.
Williams sits **P9 in the constructors' standings** with just **11 points**, well below last year's pace.
Sky Sports pundit **Martin Brundle** says Sainz's career risks **'stalling'**, calling him **'down a cul-de-sac'**.
Sainz had asked to be kept out of driver-market talk until the **summer break**, which has now arrived.

depth.background: Carlos Sainz joined Williams for the 2025 season after being replaced at Ferrari by Lewis Hamilton, aiming to help rebuild the historic team. Aston Martin, backed by owner Lawrence Stroll and newly recruited design chief Adrian Newey — considered one of F1's greatest car designers — has been positioning itself as a future front-runner and has identified Sainz as its top choice to replace the aging Fernando Alonso. F1's 2026 season introduced a major regulation overhaul, and Williams' underwhelming start under the new rules has raised doubts about the team's trajectory just as Sainz weighs whether to stay.

thread.previously: We reported that Aston Martin owner Lawrence Stroll had identified Williams driver Carlos Sainz as his top target to replace Fernando Alonso, with design chief Adrian Newey personally pushing for the signing, and that Sainz's own decision partly hinged on gains from Williams' upcoming upgrade package.
thread.changed: Sainz has now confirmed publicly that no decision on his future has been made, as Williams' struggling 2026 season and pundit Martin Brundle's warning that his career risks 'stalling' add pressure just as F1's summer break — when he said he'd start weighing his options — has arrived.
