stories.title: 1.4-million-year-old footprints reveal our extinct cousin Paranthropus boisei was nearly human-sized — and may have roamed in male groups
stories.what_happened: An international team of US and Kenyan researchers analyzed a trail of footprints preserved along the ancient shore of Lake Turkana, dated to about **1.4 million years ago**. The prints came from **eight Paranthropus boisei individuals** moving together in one place at one time — a rare snapshot of group behavior that bones alone could never show. By measuring the size and depth of the footprints, the team calculated that these individuals stood as tall as **1.8 meters** and weighed roughly **75 kilograms**, meaning some were considerably larger than previous fossil-bone estimates implied. Nearly all the individuals appear to have been adults, and the researchers found no clear signs of females or children traveling with the group, hinting the group may have been all-male. The findings were published in the **Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS)**, a leading peer-reviewed science journal.
key_points: Fossil footprints at Kenya's **Lake Turkana** are **1.4 million years old**.
They belong to **Paranthropus boisei**, an extinct side-branch relative of modern humans, not a direct ancestor.
Individuals stood up to **1.8 meters (about 5'11")** tall and weighed around **75 kilograms** — far bigger than earlier bone-based estimates suggested.
Researchers found tracks from **eight individuals**, apparently traveling together, with **no clear evidence of females or children** in the group.
The find, published in the journal **PNAS**, is reshaping ideas about this species' social behavior.

depth.background: Millions of years ago, several different human-like species coexisted in East Africa, and only one lineage — ours — survived to the present. **Paranthropus boisei** was one of these extinct 'cousins,' known mostly from a handful of skulls and jawbones with massive teeth built for chewing tough plant food, which is why it's nicknamed 'Nutcracker Man.' Because complete skeletons are so rare, scientists have had to guess at how big these creatures actually were, and footprints — a rare kind of fossil that captures a living moment rather than just bones — offer a much more direct measurement. The tracks were preserved in ancient lakeshore mud at **Lake Turkana**, a site that has produced some of the most important human-evolution fossils ever found.

stories.title: Indonesian ferry Mutiara Sentosa 2 catches fire off Madura island, killing at least 5 with 41 still missing
stories.what_happened: The ferry caught fire between roughly **6 and 7am local time on Sunday, August 2**, while traveling from Surabaya in East Java to Makassar in South Sulawesi. It was carrying **271 people** when the blaze broke out; passengers described jumping overboard or being evacuated as smoke and flames spread through the vessel. Indonesian search-and-rescue teams, coast guard vessels, and nearby ships responded, pulling **225 people** to safety so far. At least **5 deaths have been confirmed**, and **41 passengers remain missing**, with the search-and-rescue operation still active as of the latest reports. Officials have not yet determined what started the fire.
key_points: The ferry **Mutiara Sentosa 2** caught fire early Sunday while carrying **271 passengers and crew**.
At least **5 people are confirmed dead** and **41 remain unaccounted for**.
**225 people were rescued**, most jumping into the sea or pulled out by nearby boats.
The vessel was sailing from **Surabaya (Java) to Makassar (Sulawesi)** when the blaze broke out around dawn.
The cause of the fire is **still under investigation** by Indonesian search-and-rescue authorities.

depth.background: Indonesia is an archipelago of over **17,000 islands**, and ferries are a primary way ordinary people travel between them since flights are expensive and there's no bridge network like in many countries. That means these boats are often old, overcrowded, and poorly regulated compared to airlines — and fires or capsizes happen with grim regularity; a similar Indonesian ferry fire killed three people in July 2025. The **Mutiara Sentosa 2** was on a routine overnight route between two of Indonesia's biggest islands, Java and Sulawesi, a journey many Indonesians take for work or to visit family.

stories.title: Death toll in Spain's Ceuta border crisis climbs past 70 as tens of thousands who crossed from Morocco are sent back
stories.what_happened: Spanish authorities say the death toll from the Ceuta crossing attempt has now reached **at least 72**, while local officials cited by Sky News put it as high as **86**; most victims drowned trying to swim around the breakwater fence or were crushed in the crush of bodies trying to climb over it. By July 31, Spain said about **50,000 of the roughly 60,000 who crossed had gone back to Morocco**, either on their own or through coordinated returns. Spain has begun installing a **500-metre barrier extension** into the sea at the breakwater to close the gap that let people swim around the existing fence. The Spanish government has called the immediate crisis 'almost entirely reversed,' but the death toll continues to be revised upward as more bodies are recovered.
key_points: At least **72 people have died** (Spanish officials) — some sources report as high as **86** — after roughly **60,000 people** rushed the Ceuta border fence from Morocco in late July.
Most died **drowning near the Tarajal breakwater** or were **crushed in a stampede** climbing the sea barrier that separates Morocco from the Spanish enclave.
About **50,000 of the crossers have already returned to Morocco**, voluntarily or by force, Spanish officials say.
Spain is now building a **500-metre sea barrier extension** to stop future breakwater crossings.
Ceuta and Melilla are Spain's only **land borders with Africa**, making them Europe's most-tested migration chokepoint.

depth.background: **Ceuta** is a small Spanish city on the North African coast, technically part of the European Union even though it sits on Moroccan soil — which makes its fence one of the few places a migrant can walk (or swim) directly onto EU territory from Africa. Morocco has, at times, loosened its own border patrols during diplomatic disputes with Spain, and large numbers of people have surged the fence before, including a similar mass-crossing in 2021. This time roughly **60,000 people**, mostly young men, attempted to cross in a matter of days in late July 2026, overwhelming Spanish police and rescue services.

stories.title: Hadjar says it's 'a bit sad' that F1's 2026 rules turn classic tracks like Spa into some of the worst on the calendar
stories.what_happened: Red Bull driver **Isack Hadjar** said it is 'a bit sad' that F1's 2026-spec cars have effectively re-ranked the calendar's circuits based on how much energy they let cars recover and redeploy, rather than by the quality of racing itself. He singled out **Spa-Francorchamps**, historically one of the sport's most respected tracks, as now among the worst-suited under the new regulations. By contrast, he praised the recent **Hungarian Grand Prix** as feeling like 'classic racing' because its layout favours the new power units. Hadjar made the comments during the summer break, having built a strong second Red Bull season with **regular top-six finishes**.
key_points: **Isack Hadjar** says F1's **2026 regulations** rank circuits by how much energy drivers can recover, not by how good the racing is.
Under the new rules, **Spa-Francorchamps** — one of F1's most iconic tracks — is now considered **'one of the worst' on the calendar** for that reason.
Hadjar praised the **Hungarian Grand Prix** as a return to 'classic racing' because its layout suits the new energy-recovery-focused cars.
The comments come from Red Bull's Hadjar, who has impressed with **consistent top-six finishes** in his second Red Bull season.
The remarks add to a growing driver debate about whether F1's 2026 technical rules are reshaping which tracks 'work' well, independent of their racing history.

depth.background: F1's **2026 regulations** introduced a major technical overhaul, including new power units that lean more heavily on **electrical energy recovery and deployment** — meaning how much energy a car can harvest and reuse now shapes lap time more than in previous eras. This changes which circuits produce good racing: tracks with long straights and heavy braking zones (which help energy recovery) tend to suit the new cars, while others don't. **Spa-Francorchamps** in Belgium is one of the sport's most historic and beloved circuits, making its slide down the 'best tracks' rankings under the new rules a sensitive topic among drivers and fans.

stories.title: Hamilton warns Ferrari is 'pushing hard' on upgrades as he chases Antonelli's championship lead
stories.what_happened: Lewis Hamilton won the **Spanish Grand Prix in Barcelona**, his **first race win since joining Ferrari**, and says the team is now 'pushing hard' to deliver a meaningful upgrade package for the second half of the 2026 season. Despite the win, Hamilton remains well off the championship pace: **Kimi Antonelli leads the drivers' standings by 50 points over Hamilton**, and by 59 over Mercedes teammate **George Russell**. The season now pauses for F1's mandatory **summer break**, with racing resuming at the **Dutch Grand Prix on August 21-23**. Hamilton's comments signal Ferrari intends to use the break to close the performance gap rather than accept a season defined by Antonelli's early dominance.
key_points: **Lewis Hamilton** says Ferrari is pushing hard on upgrades for the second half of the season, after his **first win for the team at the Spanish Grand Prix** in Barcelona.
**Kimi Antonelli leads the drivers' championship**, **50 points ahead of Hamilton** and **59 ahead of George Russell**.
The Barcelona win was Hamilton's **first as a Ferrari driver**, marking a turning point in an otherwise difficult first two seasons at the team.
F1 enters its **summer break** now, with the next race — the **Dutch Grand Prix** — not until **August 21-23**.
Ferrari's upgrade push is aimed at closing the gap to Mercedes' Antonelli before the title fight resumes at Zandvoort.

depth.background: **Lewis Hamilton** joined Ferrari for the 2025 season after over a decade at Mercedes, in one of F1's biggest-ever driver moves, but his start at the team was rockier than expected — many races without a win. **Kimi Antonelli**, the young driver who replaced Hamilton at Mercedes, has instead emerged as the season's championship frontrunner. Every F1 season has a mandatory mid-season **summer break** where teams are barred from working on the cars, giving a natural pause point for reflecting on form and planning upgrades for the run-in.

stories.title: Auqib Nabi set to replace the injured Bumrah in India's Test squad for Sri Lanka
stories.what_happened: BCCI sources indicate **Auqib Nabi**, a seam-bowling all-rounder from Jammu & Kashmir, is set to be added to India's Test squad for the Sri Lanka tour as Bumrah's replacement. Nabi has picked up more than 100 wickets across the last two Ranji Trophy seasons and was central to J&K's recent red-ball success domestically, making him a rewarded, form-based pick rather than a like-for-like swap for Bumrah's pace and experience. India's squad is scheduled to arrive in Sri Lanka on August 4, ahead of the first of two Tests starting August 15 in Galle, with the second in Colombo on August 23.
key_points: **Auqib Nabi** is set to replace Jasprit Bumrah in India's Test squad for Sri Lanka.
Nabi has taken **100-plus wickets** across the last two Ranji Trophy seasons for Jammu & Kashmir.
He was the **chief architect** of J&K's red-ball success in domestic cricket.
Bumrah's knee injury, from the England ODI series, hasn't healed enough for him to bowl.
India's squad is set to arrive in Sri Lanka on **August 4**, with the first Test starting **August 15 in Galle**.

depth.background: Jasprit Bumrah, India's premier fast bowler, picked up a left knee injury while fielding during the ODI series in England and had been undergoing rehabilitation at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru. Despite reports he had passed some fitness tests, he had not resumed bowling, and the medical team judged he needed more time rather than risk aggravating the injury — leading to his exclusion from the two-Test tour of Sri Lanka. That left a spot open in India's fast-bowling attack for the series.

thread.previously: We reported Jasprit Bumrah had been ruled out of India's upcoming two-Test series in Sri Lanka after failing to recover from a left knee injury picked up during the England ODI series.
thread.changed: India now has a named replacement: Jammu & Kashmir pace-bowling all-rounder Auqib Nabi is set to be drafted into the squad in Bumrah's place.

stories.title: Adrian Newey is quietly building Aston Martin's future title car — and Carlos Sainz is tipped to drive it
stories.what_happened: Paddock reporting suggests Adrian Newey is working toward a future Aston Martin car capable of genuinely challenging for the world title, with **Carlos Sainz** — currently racing for Williams — increasingly named as the driver Newey wants behind the wheel when that car arrives. The current AMR26 has struggled through 2026, with Aston Martin bringing 16 upgrades to the car at the Hungarian Grand Prix alone in an attempt to close the gap to the front, so far without a breakthrough. Sainz himself has publicly praised the team's midfield downforce gains from those upgrades, while remaining coy about his own longer-term future, saying he'll weigh his options during the summer break. Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin's current lead driver, has also said he'll decide on his own future over the same break.
key_points: F1 design legend **Adrian Newey** is developing what insiders call a future **title-winning Aston Martin**.
**Carlos Sainz**, currently at Williams, is the name most tipped to eventually drive it.
Aston Martin's 2026 car, the **AMR26**, has struggled all season with an unreliable Honda power unit.
The team brought **16 upgrades** to the Hungarian Grand Prix alone trying to find pace.
Owner **Lawrence Stroll's** financial backing plus Newey's design pedigree is the bet behind the project.
Sainz's own future is unresolved — he's said he'll decide during the summer break.

depth.background: Adrian Newey, widely regarded as one of the most successful car designers in F1 history, joined Aston Martin as technical partner and later team principal after leaving Red Bull, arriving already months behind rivals on the 2026 car's development. That car, the AMR26, has had a difficult debut season hampered by reliability issues with its new Honda power unit, even as the team throws heavy upgrade packages at it race after race. The project is backed by owner Lawrence Stroll's deep pockets, betting that Newey's design expertise will eventually turn Aston Martin into a genuine title contender.

stories.title: Trump says Iran has agreed to a 'total' reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, as Tehran and Oman near a deal on the waterway
stories.what_happened: President Trump said Saturday night that Iran had agreed to a **'total' reopening of the Strait of Hormuz**, after he canceled a planned joint US-Israeli strike on Iranian energy infrastructure in order to let negotiations continue. Secretary of State **Marco Rubio** and Vice President JD Vance are leading the US side of the talks; Rubio said the earlier US strikes had targeted Iranian defense infrastructure and that Iran has agreed to a 'rough framework' for a broader peace deal, which would include easing sanctions and unfreezing Iran's overseas assets in exchange for Iran giving up nuclear weapons. Separately, Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said talks with Oman over a new maritime route through the strait — separate from existing shipping corridors — are in their 'final stages.' However, an Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson pushed back on the framing, saying the Oman understanding does not amount to a full reopening, and that the strait will never return to its pre-war status.
key_points: Trump says Iran agreed to an **'immediate, complete, and total opening'** of the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran's FM **Abbas Araghchi** says talks with Oman on a shipping mechanism are in their 'final stages.'
The move follows Trump **canceling a planned joint US-Israeli strike** on Iran's energy infrastructure over the weekend.
A wider deal would also **ease sanctions** on Iran and unfreeze its overseas assets, in exchange for no nuclear weapons.
Iran's own foreign ministry says the Oman talks do **not** mean the strait returns to its pre-war status — a real gap between Trump's framing and Tehran's.

depth.background: The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow shipping channel between Iran and Oman through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil and a large share of its liquefied natural gas passes daily — making it one of the most important **chokepoints** in global energy trade. Since a US-Israeli air war against Iran began in February 2026 (following the assassination of Iran's supreme leader), Iran has largely blocked the strait, boarding ships, laying mines, and attacking tankers, sending oil and shipping costs higher worldwide. Trump has repeatedly threatened and then paused further strikes on Iran over recent months while pushing for a deal to reopen the waterway.

thread.previously: We reported that Trump had called off a planned new round of strikes on Iran, saying a deal was 'in the works' to reopen the Strait of Hormuz — at that point still just a stated intention, with no details of an actual agreement.
thread.changed: Trump now says Iran has explicitly agreed to an **'immediate, complete, and total opening'** of the Strait, and Iran's foreign minister says talks with Oman on the mechanics of a safe-passage route are in their **'final stages.'** But Iran's own foreign ministry is already tempering expectations, saying this does not mean a full reopening of the strait to its pre-war status.

stories.title: India ends Commonwealth Games 2026 with 39 medals and a historic boxing haul — its best-ever Games boxing performance
stories.what_happened: India concluded the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games with **39 medals** — 13 gold, 17 silver, and 9 bronze — finishing 4th in the overall standings. Boxing was the standout: Indian boxers won 10 medals including a record **7 golds**, the most golds any country has won in boxing at a single Commonwealth Games, surpassing the previous mark of 6 held by England (at London 1934 and Gold Coast 2018) and matched by Canada at Edinburgh 1986. Gold medals came from Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria, Arundhati Choudhary, Priya Ghanghas, Sachin Siwach, Ankush Panghal, and Sakshi Chaudhary, with Jadumani Singh, Lovlina Borgohain, and Narender Berwal taking silver. India's para-athletes also had their best-ever Games, winning 7 medals — 3 gold, 2 silver, 2 bronze — matching the country's combined para medal tally from every previous Commonwealth Games put together.
key_points: India finished **4th overall** at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games with **39 medals**: 13 gold, 17 silver, 9 bronze.
Indian boxers won **10 medals including 7 golds** — the most golds by any nation in boxing at a single Commonwealth Games ever.
The previous record of **6 golds** was held jointly by England (twice) and Canada — India beat it by one.
India's **para-athletes** had their best Games yet, winning 7 medals — matching the combined tally of all previous editions.
The haul came despite a **reduced program** that excluded medal-rich sports like wrestling, badminton, and hockey.

depth.background: The Commonwealth Games are a multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from Commonwealth nations — a lower-profile cousin of the Olympics, but still a major stage for Indian athletes, especially in sports like boxing, wrestling, and weightlifting where India traditionally performs well. This year's Glasgow edition, held July 23 to August 2, notably dropped several sports India usually medals heavily in — wrestling, badminton, table tennis, hockey, and shooting — which made a strong overall tally harder to achieve and puts extra weight on India's performance in the sports that remained.

stories.title: Rain washes out Jaffna Kings' LPL clash, eliminating Dambulla Sixers and confirming the four playoff teams
stories.what_happened: Dambulla Sixers, batting first at Pallekele International Cricket Stadium, posted 203 for 8 in their 20 overs, with Pavan Rathnayake top-scoring on 47 off 28 balls and Dinesh Chandimal adding a quick 44 off 24. But persistent rain delayed the start of Jaffna Kings' chase and eventually forced match officials to abandon the game entirely, without Jaffna facing a single ball. Under the tournament's rules, the abandoned match meant points were shared between the two sides — enough to confirm Dambulla Sixers' elimination from playoff contention, while Galle Gallants, Jaffna Kings, Colombo Kaps, and Kandy Royals are the four teams through to the LPL 2026 playoffs.
key_points: Dambulla Sixers posted **203/8** batting first, but Jaffna Kings never got to bat as rain **abandoned the match**.
**Pavan Rathnayake (47)** and **Dinesh Chandimal (44)** led Dambulla's innings before the washout.
With points shared, **Dambulla Sixers are eliminated** from the LPL 2026 playoff race.
The confirmed **playoff four** are Galle Gallants, Jaffna Kings, Colombo Kaps, and Kandy Royals.
The result closes out the LPL 2026 group stage after 20 matches.

depth.background: The Lanka Premier League (LPL) is Sri Lanka's franchise T20 cricket tournament, run alongside other domestic leagues each year. Going into this match, Jaffna Kings had already secured a playoff spot as group leaders, while Dambulla Sixers sat bottom of the table and needed a win — and help elsewhere — just to have a chance of qualifying, making this final group-stage fixture effectively a knockout match for Dambulla even though Jaffna's own position was already safe.

thread.previously: We noted that table-topping Jaffna Kings, already through to the playoffs, were set to face bottom-placed Dambulla Sixers as the Lanka Premier League's group stage wrapped up.

stories.title: Ukraine hits a Russian air base and oil refinery deep inside Russia as strikes on both sides kill at least 14
stories.what_happened: Overnight into Sunday, swarms of Ukrainian drones struck multiple Russian regions, hitting a **Russian air base at Engels** (used to house long-range bombers) and an **oil refinery in Saratov Oblast**, while also setting ablaze a warehouse belonging to **Wildberries**, Russia's largest online retailer. Russia said it shot down 635 of the drones, but the attacks still killed at least **9 people** in Russian territory. Hours earlier, Russia had launched its own large barrage — **35 missiles, mostly ballistic, plus nearly 190 drones** — primarily targeting Kyiv and the surrounding region, killing at least **9** and injuring **40**. Combined, the two nights of strikes killed at least **14 people** across both countries. The exchange comes as Russia's ground offensive, running since roughly mid-May, continues to make minimal territorial progress.
key_points: Ukrainian drones struck a Russian **air base at Engels** and an **oil refinery in Saratov** overnight.
Russia claims it shot down **635 drones**, but the strikes still killed at least **9 people** on Russian soil.
A warehouse belonging to **Wildberries**, Russia's largest online retailer, was set ablaze.
Russia hit back with **35 missiles and ~190 drones** at Kyiv overnight, killing at least **9** and injuring **40**.
Russia's broader summer offensive has made **no operationally significant gains** in over two months.

depth.background: Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine has ground into its fifth year, with front lines largely static despite a **Spring-Summer 2026 offensive** Moscow launched to try to break the stalemate. Increasingly, both sides have shifted from grinding infantry battles to long-range drone and missile warfare — Russia pounding Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure, and Ukraine, lacking a large air force, using cheap long-range drones to hit Russian military and economic targets far from the front line, including refineries and air bases that keep Russia's war machine running.

thread.previously: Yesterday we reported Zelensky warning Ukraine's air defenses were being overwhelmed as Russia launched a second massive missile-and-drone strike in two days.
thread.changed: Today the picture flipped to show Ukraine hitting back hard — striking a Russian air base and oil refinery deep inside Russia — even as Russia's own barrage on Kyiv continued and killed more civilians.

stories.title: F1's return to Africa is 'progressing very well,' says F1 boss Domenicali, with South Africa and Rwanda competing to host
stories.what_happened: Speaking about F1's long-running effort to add an African round, CEO **Stefano Domenicali** said negotiations are **'progressing very well,'** while cautioning the process is deliberately not being rushed. F1 says any new African race needs three things confirmed first: investment that benefits the local community beyond race weekend itself, adequate infrastructure (hotels, roads, airports — not just a track), and an economic base able to sustain the event long-term. Two bids are currently in play: **South Africa**, where the government has opened a tender process for a race at either the historic **Kyalami** circuit or a new street circuit around Cape Town's **Green Point** district, and **Rwanda**, which has proposed a circuit on the outskirts of capital **Kigali**. Domenicali indicated a South African race realistically won't happen before **2029**, while separately suggesting Turkey could return to the calendar as soon as **2027**.
key_points: F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali says talks to bring a **Grand Prix back to Africa** are progressing well.
Africa is the only continent F1 currently has **no race on** at all.
**South Africa** (Kyalami or a Cape Town street circuit) and **Rwanda** (Kigali) are both bidding to host.
F1 wants guarantees on **community investment, infrastructure, and long-term economic viability** before committing.
Domenicali suggests a South African race is unlikely before **2029**, while Turkey could return sooner, in 2027.

depth.background: Formula 1 last raced in Africa at the **1993 South African Grand Prix** at Kyalami — over three decades ago. Since then the sport has expanded aggressively into new markets (Miami, Las Vegas, Saudi Arabia, Qatar), while Africa has remained the one continent with no round on the calendar at all, something F1's leadership has repeatedly called out as a gap it wants to close as the sport globalizes.

stories.title: California's AI Transparency Act kicks in today, forcing ChatGPT-scale AI tools to watermark what they generate
stories.what_happened: As of today, any generative-AI provider serving more than **one million monthly users in California** is legally required to embed a **latent (hidden) watermark** in every AI-generated image, video, and audio clip it produces, carrying machine-readable metadata about its origin. Providers must also let users add a **visible on-screen label** flagging content as AI-made, and must publish a **free tool** the public can use to check whether a piece of content was AI-generated. The law's scope was widened last year to also apply to **large online platforms that host AI content** and to **camera/device manufacturers**. Non-compliant companies face financial penalties under California law. The effective date, August 2, 2026, was chosen specifically to coincide with the **EU AI Act's** own deadline for high-risk AI systems, signaling regulators on both sides of the Atlantic are converging on the same rulebook.
key_points: California's **SB 942** becomes legally enforceable today, hitting any generative-AI provider with **over 1 million California users**.
Covered companies must embed a **hidden, machine-readable watermark** in AI-made images, video and audio, plus a visible label users can toggle on.
They must also offer a **free public detection tool** so anyone can check if a file was AI-generated.
The law's effective date was deliberately timed to **line up with the EU AI Act's** own high-risk enforcement date, a coordinated global push.
It followed years of delay: signed in **2024**, then amended in **October 2025** to widen its scope before finally taking effect.

depth.background: Generative AI tools that create photorealistic images, cloned voices and deepfake video have become cheap and widespread, and there has been no reliable, standardized way for an ordinary person to tell if something they're looking at is real. California's legislature passed the **AI Transparency Act (SB 942)** in 2024 to close that gap for the world's biggest AI makers, since California is home to most major AI labs. Regulators expanded the bill in 2025 (via a companion law, AB 853) to also cover **large platforms that host AI content** and even **device manufacturers**, not just the AI companies themselves. The rollout was delayed multiple times as companies lobbied over technical feasibility.

stories.title: F1 has gone dark for two weeks — here's the rule that forces every team to down tools at the same time
stories.what_happened: Every F1 team is currently in the middle of its **mandatory 14-day shutdown**, during which no work related to car performance is allowed to happen at all — that covers design, development, manufacturing of parts, and simulator running, and even extends to banning emails, calls, or meetings about performance topics. Teams must log their activity during the period, and those logs can be requested by the FIA at any time; the governing body also uses factory access-control systems to track who enters and exits team facilities, and can run random checks if it suspects a team is secretly working. The rule is designed to ensure no team gains a development advantage by simply outworking its rivals during the break, and to give F1's notoriously overworked staff two guaranteed weeks off.
key_points: F1's **mandatory summer shutdown** is underway: a **14 consecutive-day** period where all teams must stop performance-related work.
For 2026, the shutdown falls between the **Hungarian Grand Prix** (July 24-26) and the **Dutch Grand Prix** (August 21-23).
Banned activities include **car design, development, part production, and even simulator use** — plus emails or meetings about performance.
The **FIA enforces it** using factory access-control logs and can conduct **random checks** if it suspects a team cheated the rule.
The rule exists to **control costs** and give burned-out team staff a genuine break from F1's relentless calendar.

depth.background: F1 teams work on a punishing schedule — most of the grid runs **24 races a year** plus constant car development in between, which used to mean near year-round work for engineering staff. The FIA introduced the mandatory shutdown period years ago as both a cost-control measure (stopping wealthier teams from just working through the summer to gain an advantage) and a wellbeing measure for overworked staff. Each team picks its own two-week window, but it must fall within July and/or August, and the 2026 calendar naturally slots it into the gap between Hungary and the Netherlands.

stories.title: India's Cabinet approves ₹84,084 crore 'Samudra Manthan' plan to unlock offshore oil and gas
stories.what_happened: The Cabinet, chaired by PM Modi, approved the scheme with an outlay of **₹84,084 crore** for implementation through FY 2030-31. Unlike earlier exploration-only schemes, Samudra Manthan integrates geological surveys, deep-sea drilling, scientific research, production infrastructure, digital monitoring, domestic manufacturing support and workforce skilling under a single framework. The government projects it will catalyse reserve additions of more than **600 million metric tons of oil equivalent (MMTOE)**, substantially increase offshore exploration activity, and generate large-scale employment, while building a globally competitive domestic offshore-technology and services industry.
key_points: India's Union Cabinet approved **'Samudra Manthan'**, a **₹84,084 crore (~$10 billion)** National Offshore Exploration Scheme to boost domestic oil and gas output.
The scheme runs through **FY 2030-31** and targets unlocking more than **600 million tonnes of oil equivalent** in new reserves.
It bundles deep-sea drilling, geological surveys, digital monitoring and domestic manufacturing support into **one national framework**, not just exploration funding alone.
The core goal is cutting India's heavy reliance on **imported crude oil**, which leaves the economy exposed to global price shocks and shipping-route disruptions.
It also aims to build a domestic offshore-technology industry under the **'Make in India'** push, rather than relying on foreign drilling and survey firms.

depth.background: India imports the large majority of the crude oil it consumes, which means global oil-price swings and shipping disruptions hit the economy directly — a vulnerability already on display today with the ongoing Strait of Hormuz shipping crisis. 'Samudra Manthan' takes its name from an ancient Indian legend about churning the ocean to reveal hidden treasures, used here as a metaphor for extracting value from India's offshore waters. Previous Indian offshore exploration efforts have been criticized as underfunded and fragmented across agencies; this scheme is designed to consolidate exploration, production infrastructure and skill-building under one Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas program.

stories.title: Japan's Kumamoto earthquake death toll climbs to 38 as rescue crews keep clearing rubble a week on
stories.what_happened: Part of the second floor of Kumamoto City's Aeon Mall collapsed during the quake, and about an hour later a gas-fed structural explosion tore through the complex — staff had already evacuated roughly 200 shoppers before the blast. The Kyushu Expressway split apart in sections, cutting a key transport link, and a wall of the centuries-old Kumamoto Castle came down. As of August 2, the confirmed death toll stands at **38** (36 confirmed, 2 more under investigation), up from 34 on July 31 and just 18 in the immediate aftermath — meaning the toll has more than doubled as search teams dig deeper into the rubble. More than **9,200 people** are still sheltering in 210 evacuation centers, over **3,400 homes** have been damaged, and tap water remains cut to more than **69,000 households and businesses** in Kumamoto.
key_points: The confirmed death toll has nearly **doubled in a week**, from 18 right after the quake to **38** as of August 2.
More than **9,200 people** remain in 210 evacuation shelters, with tap water still cut to over **69,000 households**.
The magnitude **7.1 quake** partially collapsed a shopping mall, and a gas-fed explosion tore through it about an hour later.
A section of the **Kyushu Expressway split apart**, and a wall of the historic **Kumamoto Castle collapsed**.
Over **3,400 houses** were damaged in one of Japan's deadliest domestic disasters in years.

depth.background: On July 28, 2026, a magnitude **7.1 earthquake** struck Kumamoto Prefecture on the southern Japanese island of Kyushu. It triggered a tsunami warning and forced roughly **260,000 people** to evacuate. Kumamoto sits in a seismically active part of Japan that was hit by a devastating quake cluster in 2016, so its building codes and disaster-response systems have been tested before — but this event has proven unusually deadly, with a secondary mall explosion compounding the damage. The government of PM Takaichi has been managing the emergency response as rescue and recovery work stretches into its second week.

thread.previously: We reported the toll at 34 after a magnitude 7.1 quake hit Kumamoto on July 28 and an explosion tore through the Aeon Mall about 80 minutes later, with roughly 10,000 people displaced and rescue crews in their fourth day.
thread.changed: The confirmed toll has since risen to 38 (36 confirmed, 2 more still under investigation) — nearly double the 18 counted right after the quake. Over 9,200 people remain in 210 shelters, tap water is still cut to more than 69,000 households and businesses, and newly reported damage includes a split section of the Kyushu Expressway and a collapsed wall at Kumamoto Castle.

stories.title: Gujarat monsoon floods leave at least 4 dead and force tens of thousands to evacuate as IMD issues a red alert
stories.what_happened: Heavy monsoon rain has pounded Gujarat since July 31, with Surat recording as much as **24 inches of rain**. The IMD issued a **red alert for 15 districts**, including Ahmedabad and Vadodara, and orange alerts for 18 more. At least three farm labourers were killed in Navsari's Gandevi when their tempo truck touched a live high-tension wire, and an 11-year-old girl was swept away by floodwaters in Anand, taking the confirmed toll to at least 4-5. Evacuation numbers have climbed sharply, from an initial **16,500 to more than 38,000 people** across the worst-hit South Gujarat districts, as rescue operations intensified. Ahmedabad banned public entry to its lakefront gardens until August 2, and the Army (with boats and over 70 personnel in Valsad alone), NDRF, SDRF teams, and Air Force helicopters on standby at Jamnagar, Jodhpur, Vadodara, and Pune have all been mobilized. Gujarat's Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel has deputed his deputy and a state minister to the affected districts.
key_points: IMD issued a **red alert for 15 districts**, including Ahmedabad and Vadodara, plus orange alerts for 18 more.
Surat recorded up to **24 inches of rain**, and evacuation numbers have climbed from **16,500 to over 38,000** people.
**Three farm labourers were electrocuted** in Navsari when their vehicle touched a live high-tension wire; an 11-year-old was swept away in Anand.
The **Army, NDRF, SDRF, and Air Force helicopters** have been deployed for rescue operations across South Gujarat.
Ahmedabad has **banned public entry to lakefront gardens** until August 2 as authorities manage the flooding.

depth.background: Gujarat is in the middle of its annual monsoon season, which brings most of India's yearly rainfall between June and September but also regularly causes flash flooding when rain intensity outpaces drainage and river capacity. Torrential rain has been battering the state since **July 31**, hitting South Gujarat districts like Navsari, Valsad, and Surat hardest. This flooding is separate from — but adds to — this year's monsoon disaster picture alongside the Assam floods further east, which have already killed 80 people.

stories.title: Former Haas boss Guenther Steiner says FIA was too lenient on Carlos Sainz's Hungarian GP penalty
stories.what_happened: Stewards ruled Sainz **'wholly responsible'** for the collision but issued only a **5-second penalty**, citing a faulty GPS tracking system and a glitch in the blue-flag warning software as reasons Sainz may not have gotten a clear signal that Piastri was alongside. New onboard footage has since surfaced showing Sainz actually passed **seven trackside blue-flag panels** during the lap, and that his own Williams team had radioed him a warning about Piastri's approach before the crash — undercutting his defense that the warning system had failed him. Former Haas team principal **Guenther Steiner**, speaking on The Red Flags Podcast, and ex-F1 driver **Ralf Schumacher** have both since said publicly that the full 10-second penalty should have applied, to set a clear precedent for how backmarkers must treat race leaders. Piastri himself called the incident **'unacceptable'** and said Sainz should **'look in the mirror.'**
key_points: Sainz was deemed **'wholly responsible'** for a collision with Piastri's McLaren but got only a **5-second penalty**, not the standard 10.
Stewards cited a **faulty GPS tracking system** and a **blue-flag software glitch** as mitigating factors for the lighter penalty.
New onboard footage shows Sainz **passed seven trackside blue-flag panels** and that his own team **radioed a warning** about Piastri beforehand.
**Guenther Steiner and Ralf Schumacher** have both publicly said the full 10-second penalty should have applied.
**Piastri called the incident 'unacceptable'**, saying the collision effectively ended his shot at winning the race.

depth.background: During the Hungarian Grand Prix, Williams driver Carlos Sainz collided with race leader Oscar Piastri's McLaren while Piastri was lapping backmarkers — contact that ended Piastri's chance of victory (he later retired with a gearbox failure). F1 normally hands out a standard **10-second time penalty** to a driver deemed fully at fault for causing a collision, but stewards can reduce it if they find genuine mitigating circumstances, like a technical failure outside the driver's control.

stories.title: Trent Rockets Women edge Sunrisers Leeds Women by 5 runs in The Hundred
stories.what_happened: Batting first at Trent Bridge, Trent Rockets Women set a target of 140 from their 100 balls. Sunrisers Leeds Women's chase was built around a fighting innings from **Annabel Sutherland**, but the required rate crept up too far, and Leeds finished on 134/5 — five runs short of the target. Trent Rockets Women held on to win by 5 runs and pick up the points in the group-stage standings.
key_points: Trent Rockets Women posted **139/7** from their 100 balls at Trent Bridge, Nottingham.
Sunrisers Leeds Women fell **5 runs short**, finishing on 134/5.
**Annabel Sutherland** anchored the chase for Leeds with an unbeaten innings that ultimately wasn't enough.
The result is part of Match 17 of the **2026 Hundred Women's Competition** group stage.

depth.background: **The Hundred** is England's short-form cricket franchise competition — eight men's and eight women's teams, each city-based, playing a 100-ball-per-innings format designed to be faster and more TV-friendly than a normal T20. Trent Rockets and Sunrisers Leeds are two of the competition's franchises, based in Nottingham and Leeds respectively, and this fixture was the 17th match of the 2026 season's group stage.

stories.title: Ajinkya Rahane, hero of India's historic 2020-21 Australia comeback, retires from all cricket
stories.what_happened: Ajinkya Rahane announced his retirement from **international cricket and all formats**, closing out a career spanning more than **17 years**. In an emotional video message, he said: **"I have always relied on timing in my batting and I have always understood its importance. Today, I feel the timing is right for me to move on."** Across his career he played **85 Tests, 90 ODIs and 20 T20Is** for India, plus **212 IPL matches** for six different franchises. His last India appearance came in a **Test match in the West Indies in July 2023**. He continued playing in the IPL afterward, most recently captaining **Kolkata Knight Riders** in the 2026 season, where he scored **335 runs in 14 matches** at age 38.
key_points: Rahane retires from **international and all formats** after a **17-year** career.
He played **85 Tests, 90 ODIs and 20 T20Is**, plus **212 IPL matches** across six franchises.
He is best remembered for captaining India to a stunning series win in Australia in **2020-21**, with regular captain Virat Kohli away.
His last international appearance was a **Test in the West Indies in July 2023**.
He last played competitively in **IPL 2026**, captaining Kolkata Knight Riders to **335 runs in 14 matches**.

depth.background: Ajinkya Rahane built his reputation as one of Indian cricket's most reliable overseas Test batters, prized for gritty, patient innings in tough conditions rather than flashy stroke-play. His defining moment came during India's **2020-21 tour of Australia**, when he took over the Test captaincy after Virat Kohli returned home for the birth of his child — and led a weakened, injury-hit Indian side to a historic series win at the **Gabba in Brisbane**, a ground Australia had not lost at in over 30 years. He had not played for India since mid-2023, with his career since then largely continuing through franchise T20 cricket.

stories.title: Kerala landslides kill 8 as rain traps six fishermen at sea and forces 5,700 into relief camps
stories.what_happened: Kerala has been on high alert since Sunday after days of relentless rain left at least **8 people dead**, including **3 children**, and triggered fresh landslides that claimed **4 lives** in the **Kottayam and Idukki** districts alone. Search operations are continuing for **6 missing fishermen** — four from Thiruvananthapuram and two from Kollam — who went missing in the Arabian Sea, along with **2 Kannur residents** swept away after falling into a river. More than **5,700 people** have been moved to relief camps, with significant damage reported to homes and property across the state's high ranges. The IMD has issued an **orange alert for 12 districts**, warning of continued intense rainfall in the days ahead.
key_points: Days of relentless rain have killed **8 people** in Kerala, including **3 children**.
**4 of the 8 deaths** were caused directly by landslides in the state's high-range districts.
**6 fishermen** from Thiruvananthapuram and Kollam remain missing after being swept into the Arabian Sea.
Over **5,700 people** have been moved into relief camps as homes and property sustain heavy damage.
IMD has issued an **orange alert for 12 districts**, warning the intense rain is not yet over.

depth.background: Kerala's steep Western Ghats terrain makes it especially prone to landslides during India's monsoon, when saturated hillsides can give way with little warning, often burying homes downhill. The state has suffered deadly flood and landslide disasters in past monsoon seasons, and disaster-management protocols now include pre-emptive evacuations and fishing bans when heavy rain warnings are issued for coastal and hill districts alike.

stories.title: Chennai Super Kings join the race for Hardik Pandya as reports say seven IPL franchises now want him
stories.what_happened: Reports now indicate **Chennai Super Kings** have joined the race to sign Hardik Pandya, with as many as **seven IPL franchises** reportedly showing interest in the all-rounder ahead of the IPL 2027 trade window. Mumbai Indians have officially stated that **no negotiations are happening at this stage**, and that any decisions on trades, releases or retentions will wait until the team completes a **full end-of-season review** of its disappointing 2026 campaign. Speculation has also grown that **Rohit Sharma** could be restored as MI captain if Pandya does eventually move on. Any official confirmation on trades or releases is expected only closer to the **auction window**, likely a month or two before it takes place.
key_points: **Chennai Super Kings (CSK)** have become the latest IPL team to chase all-rounder **Hardik Pandya**.
Reports say as many as **seven IPL franchises** are now interested in signing him.
Mumbai Indians (MI) officially deny any trade talks are happening **at this stage**.
MI are conducting a **full end-of-season review** after a disappointing IPL 2026 campaign before deciding.
**Rohit Sharma** could be handed the MI captaincy again if Pandya does leave.

depth.background: Hardik Pandya has captained Mumbai Indians on and off since a high-profile move from Gujarat Titans, but MI's **IPL 2026 season disappointed** the five-time champions, fueling speculation the franchise could restructure its squad and leadership. Yesterday we reported MI had shut the door on trade talks with CSK, calling the saga stalled — but that appears to have been only a temporary pause rather than a resolution.

stories.title: The EU's new AI transparency law kicks in today — chatbots and deepfakes must now say what they are
stories.what_happened: As of today, any company offering a chatbot, AI voice assistant, or AI avatar to EU users must make it unmistakable, at first contact, that the user is talking to software, not a person. Separately, anyone who publishes a **deepfake** — a photo, video or audio clip that's been AI-generated or manipulated to look real — has to disclose that at the point the audience first sees or hears it, in a way that's "clear and distinguishable," not buried in fine print. AI systems that generate synthetic text, image, audio or video content also now have to mark their outputs in a machine-readable format (invisible metadata a platform can detect) wherever that's technically possible. Systems that read people's emotions or sort them into categories using biometric data (face, voice, gait) must tell those people what the system is doing to them. The rules cover professional and commercial use; a person using AI purely for personal, non-commercial reasons is exempt, as is clearly-labelled satire, art and fiction. National regulators in each of the 27 member states are responsible for enforcement, and the European Commission has already published a voluntary **Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content** that companies could sign by July 22 to get a legal safe harbour showing good-faith compliance.
key_points: **Article 50** of the EU AI Act becomes legally enforceable today, **August 2, 2026**, across all **27 EU member states**.
Any chatbot or AI agent must now tell a user **'you're talking to a machine'** the first time they interact.
AI-generated or altered images, audio and video — **deepfakes** — must carry a **clear, visible label** disclosing they're synthetic.
Companies that don't comply face fines up to **€15 million or 3% of global annual turnover**, whichever is bigger.
AI tools already on the market get a grace period to **December 2, 2026** to add invisible, machine-readable watermarks.

depth.background: The **EU AI Act**, passed in 2024, is the world's first broad law regulating artificial intelligence, and it doesn't switch on all at once — it phases in obligations over several years, toughest rules for the riskiest AI first. Most of the Act polices *how AI systems work* (banning certain uses, requiring risk assessments for high-stakes systems like hiring or credit tools); **Article 50 is different — it polices honesty, not safety**. It says people have a right to know when they're dealing with a machine or looking at something a machine made, no matter how safe or harmless that AI system otherwise is. This obligation was written into the law back in 2024 with a fixed countdown clock, and today is simply the day that clock hits zero.

stories.title: Trump calls off planned new strikes on Iran, citing a deal in the works to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
stories.what_happened: On Saturday night, Trump posted that he was calling off a planned attack because, in his words, **'the perimeters of a deal has been agreed to,'** after Iran and other Middle Eastern countries asked him to hold off. He said the emerging agreement includes the **'Immediate, Complete, and Total'** reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping, plus an end to Iran's nuclear weapons threat. Israel is joining the pause. Saudi Crown Prince **Mohammed bin Salman** personally raised concerns about the planned strikes with Trump and pushed for de-escalation. The pause is conditional — Trump said it only holds if a real deal gets done **'rapidly.'** Iranian state media, however, gave no public confirmation that Tehran views this as a settled agreement, and a separate report said Iran was still denying a specific Oman-brokered arrangement over how ships would cross the strait.
key_points: Trump says he'll hold off attacking Iran if a deal is **'rapidly'** reached
The emerging deal reportedly includes **fully reopening the Strait of Hormuz**
Qatar, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have been **mediating** behind the scenes
It's a sharp reversal from **just one day earlier**, when the US was readying a bigger strike
Iran's own public statements gave **no clear confirmation** that a deal is done

depth.background: For nearly five months the US and Israel have been at war with Iran, a conflict that escalated sharply in late July when Iran began targeting tankers and firing at ships to choke off the **Strait of Hormuz** — the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman that roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes through daily. On July 31, Trump had ordered a **new wave of strikes** aimed at forcing Iran's surrender and told American citizens across the Middle East to be ready to leave. Mediators from **Qatar, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia** have spent the days since trying to broker a face-saving off-ramp, using Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff as the go-between with Tehran.

thread.previously: We reported that Trump had ordered a new wave of strikes on Iran aimed at forcing a surrender, telling US citizens across the Middle East to be ready to leave, as the Strait of Hormuz remained effectively shut to shipping.
thread.changed: Trump abruptly reversed course, pausing the planned strikes and citing an emerging deal — brokered with help from Qatar, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia — to reopen the strait, though Iran hasn't publicly confirmed the same terms.

stories.title: A gunman killed 3 and wounded 7 at a brand-new Idaho In-N-Out Burger before turning the gun on himself
stories.what_happened: Around **3 p.m. on Saturday, August 1**, a gunman opened fire outside the restaurant, killing three people, including an employee, and wounding seven others. Police say an **off-duty Idaho state trooper and a private citizen** fired shots that helped drive the suspect away from the scene, which officials credit with preventing further casualties. The shooter, identified as 24-year-old Chad Williams, was found to have died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound. Twin Falls Police Chief Matthew Hicks said the pair's actions 'helped drive the suspect away from the scene, preventing further casualties.' As of Sunday, investigators had not identified a motive, and the community was described as 'reeling' in local coverage the next day.
key_points: A shooter opened fire at a **Twin Falls, Idaho** In-N-Out Burger just a week after it opened, killing **3** and wounding **7**
The suspect, **24-year-old Chad Williams**, died from a **self-inflicted gunshot wound**
An **off-duty state trooper and a bystander** are credited with confronting him and cutting the attack short
Police say a **motive has not been established**; the investigation is ongoing

depth.background: In-N-Out Burger, a popular West Coast fast-food chain, has been expanding into new states including Idaho, and the Twin Falls location had been open for barely a week. Mass shootings at public, everyday venues — restaurants, stores, schools — have become a recurring feature of American life, regularly reigniting the national debate over gun access and mental health support, without Congress passing major new restrictions in recent years.

stories.title: Jofra Archer's 4-9 sinks London Spirit at Lord's as Adil Rashid becomes The Hundred's all-time leading wicket-taker
stories.what_happened: At Lord's on August 1, London Spirit were bowled out for **105**, with Jonny Bairstow's 56 the only notable resistance, after Jofra Archer ripped through the middle order with figures of **4 for 9**. Marcus Stoinis chipped in with 3 for 17, extending his tournament-leading tally to **9 wickets in 4 matches**. Chasing 106, Southern Brave got home with **5 wickets and 3 balls in hand**, sealing a 5-wicket win. Adil Rashid, who took 2 for 17 in the match, became the **all-time leading wicket-taker in Hundred men's competition history**, overtaking previous record-holder Tymal Mills. Archer was named the match's Meerkat Match Hero for his bowling.
key_points: Jofra Archer took **4 for 9** to bowl out London Spirit for 105 at Lord's, winning the Meerkat Match Hero award.
Southern Brave chased down the target, winning by **5 wickets with 3 balls to spare**.
Adil Rashid's **2 for 17** made him The Hundred men's competition's **all-time leading wicket-taker**, passing Tymal Mills.
Marcus Stoinis took 3 for 17 and now leads the tournament's wicket charts with **9 wickets in 4 matches**.
The result keeps Southern Brave alive for the Eliminator, while London Spirit's playoff hopes take a big hit.

depth.background: The Hundred is England's 100-ball franchise cricket tournament, now in its sixth season, running through August with a finals day on August 16 at Lord's. Southern Brave and London Spirit were both fighting for a place in the knockout stages, making this match — the 16th of the men's competition — a genuine four-points swing for the table.

stories.title: India's boxing golden run continues at the Commonwealth Games: Arundhati Choudhary wins gold, Lovlina Borgohain takes silver
stories.what_happened: On the boxing finals day at Glasgow 2026, **Arundhati Choudhary defeated England's Chantelle Reid — an Olympic and World Championships bronze medallist — by a unanimous 5-0 verdict** to win the women's 70kg gold medal, taking India's tally to **five golds** in the ring. In the marquee women's 75kg final, **Lovlina Borgohain lost a tight 4-1 split decision to Australia's Emma-Sue Greentree**, who did enough across the bout to convince a majority of judges despite Lovlina's composed, technical performance. The silver adds to Lovlina's collection, giving her podium finishes at the Olympics, World Championships, Asian Games, and now the Commonwealth Games. Across the Games, **all 10 Indian boxers who reached finals medalled**, a clean sweep that officials are calling the country's best-ever Commonwealth Games boxing campaign.
key_points: **Arundhati Choudhary** beat Olympic and World Championships bronze medallist Chantelle Reid **5-0** to win women's 70kg gold.
It's India's **fifth boxing gold** of the Glasgow 2026 Games, extending the country's best-ever CWG boxing showing.
**Lovlina Borgohain** lost a close **4-1 split decision** to Australia's Emma-Sue Greentree in the women's 75kg final, settling for silver.
Lovlina's silver completes a **full medal set** — she now has medals from the Olympics, Worlds, Asian Games, and Commonwealth Games.
All **10 Indian boxers** who entered the finals this Games have now medalled, a historic sweep for the contingent.

depth.background: India sent an unusually large and talented boxing squad to the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games, and **all 10 boxers who reached the finals won at least a medal** — the best Commonwealth Games boxing performance in the country's history. Lovlina Borgohain, a Tokyo Olympic bronze medallist, is one of India's most decorated boxers, while 70kg gold medallist Arundhati Choudhary has been rising through the ranks against senior international opposition. Boxing has become one of India's most reliable medal sports at multi-discipline events, alongside wrestling and shooting.

stories.title: Joe Root's unbeaten 58 fires Welsh Fire past Birmingham Phoenix in The Hundred, days after his England Test captaincy was confirmed
stories.what_happened: In the men's Hundred match at Edgbaston, Welsh Fire chased down Birmingham Phoenix's total of 137 for 9 with four balls to spare, finishing on 138 for 3. Joe Root anchored the chase with an unbeaten 58, batting through the innings alongside Phil Salt's 46 to close out the win comfortably. In the earlier women's fixture at the same ground, Birmingham Phoenix's women beat Welsh Fire's women by seven wickets, with Ellyse Perry making 68 not out and Alice Capsey 51 to end Phoenix's long winless run in the competition, getting home with just one ball to spare while chasing 144.
key_points: **Joe Root** scored an unbeaten **58** in Welsh Fire's chase, steering them to a seven-wicket win at Edgbaston.
Welsh Fire chased down Birmingham Phoenix's **137 for 9**, reaching **138 for 3** with four balls to spare.
Root shared the chase with **Phil Salt (46)**, who also played a key role in the win.
The win comes just after Root's return as **England's full-time Test captain** was confirmed, with **Stephen Fleming** as new head coach.
Birmingham Phoenix's women's team, by contrast, ended a **winless run** on the same day thanks to Ellyse Perry's unbeaten 68.

depth.background: The Hundred is England's short-form, 100-balls-per-innings franchise cricket competition, played each summer alongside the international calendar. Joe Root, one of England's most experienced batters, was recently confirmed as England's full-time Test captain again, ending a four-year gap since he last held the role, with former New Zealand captain Stephen Fleming coming in as head coach. Welsh Fire and Birmingham Phoenix are two of the competition's eight men's franchises, both playing out of Edgbaston in Birmingham for this fixture.

stories.title: OpenAI says an unreleased model just solved 10 unsolved math problems — for about $2,000
stories.what_happened: OpenAI announced on **August 1, 2026** that an internal version of its next major model, Astra, had solved **ten open problems** spanning group theory, von Neumann algebras, high-dimensional geometry, quantum complexity, lattice cryptography, and extremal combinatorics. The company published every proof as a **Lean 4 certificate** — a machine-verifiable format — on its GitHub repository under an Apache 2.0 license, alongside a **249-page technical manuscript** and a **62-page account** of how the arguments were constructed. The standout result is a concrete, explicit **non-sofic group**, resolving a question that has been open since mathematician Mikhail Gromov introduced the concept of soficity in 1999. OpenAI says the entire set of ten proofs cost about **$2,000** in compute. Fields Medalist Timothy Gowers reviewed at least one of the proofs and said he would recommend it for publication in a top journal without hesitation.
key_points: OpenAI says an internal, not-yet-released model called **Astra** solved **ten long-standing open problems** in mathematics and theoretical computer science.
The headline result is the **first-ever explicit construction of a "non-sofic" group** — closing a question in group theory that has stood open since **1999**.
OpenAI published the full **machine-checked Lean proofs** on GitHub under an open license, so any mathematician can verify them line by line.
The total compute cost for all ten proofs was roughly **$2,000**.
**Fields Medal winner Timothy Gowers** said he'd recommend one of the proofs for a top journal **without hesitation**.

depth.background: AI models have been getting better at math competitions for a couple of years, but competition problems have known answers — the hard, more meaningful test is whether a model can produce genuinely **new** mathematics that nobody has proven before. A "Lean proof" is written in a formal computer language that a separate program can mechanically check step-by-step, so unlike a normal written proof, there's no room for a subtle logical gap to slip past a human reviewer. **Soficity** is a property mathematicians have studied in group theory since 1999; whether every group is "sofic" (has a certain approximable structure) was an open question, and constructing a definite non-sofic example had eluded mathematicians for over two decades.

stories.title: Odisha's Cabinet clears a plan to run its biggest cities as single economic zones, starting with Bhubaneswar-Cuttack-Puri-Paradeep
stories.what_happened: Odisha's Cabinet approved amendments to the state's **Odisha Development Authorities (ODA) Act** on Friday, creating a new legal category called an **Economic Region Development Authority (ERDA)** — a single planning and governing body for a cluster of cities and districts that together form one economic region. The **Bhubaneswar-Cuttack-Puri-Paradeep** cluster will become the state's first ERDA. The amendment inserts a new chapter into the ODA Act that lets the state government designate future ERDAs simply by government notification, rather than passing a new law each time. Three more regions have already been identified for eventual ERDA status: **Bargarh-Jharsuguda-Sambalpur**, **Berhampur-Chhatrapur-Gopalpur**, and **Jeypore-Koraput-Sunabeda**. The government says the goal is integrated infrastructure planning, easier investment approval and coordinated public services across what are currently separate municipal jurisdictions.
key_points: Odisha's Cabinet approved a bill creating **Economic Region Development Authorities (ERDAs)** — single bodies planning across city and district lines.
The first ERDA covers **Bhubaneswar, Cuttack, Puri and Paradeep**, a cluster of cities that today are each planned separately.
Three more regions are already earmarked: **Bargarh-Jharsuguda-Sambalpur**, **Berhampur-Chhatrapur-Gopalpur**, and **Jeypore-Koraput-Sunabeda**.
The law lets the state government create future ERDAs **by notification**, without needing a fresh act of the legislature each time.
The stated goal is **coordinated infrastructure, investment and jobs** across city clusters that currently compete rather than cooperate.

depth.background: Indian cities have historically been planned one municipality at a time, even when they function as a single economic unit — commuters, industry and infrastructure all cross city and district lines that planning bodies don't. Odisha's government has been trying to position clusters like Bhubaneswar-Cuttack-Puri-Paradeep as an integrated growth engine rather than four separate towns competing for the same investment. The **Odisha Development Authorities (Amendment) Bill, 2026** is the legal vehicle for that shift, moved by the state's Housing and Urban Development Department.

stories.title: Alonso shuts the door on Alpine again at the Hungarian GP — but Briatore and Gucci are reportedly still pushing hard for 2027
stories.what_happened: Speaking at the **Hungarian Grand Prix**, Alonso moved to firmly shut down the Alpine speculation, saying **'I have a contract, I'm not going to change teams,'** a notably more direct denial than his earlier comment that he was **'open to many scenarios.'** Despite that, multiple outlets reported that **Flavio Briatore** — who is both Alonso's personal manager and an Alpine advisor to Renault's board — and incoming Alpine title sponsor **Gucci** are actively pushing to bring Alonso back to the team for 2027. The connection: Gucci's parent company **Kering** is run by **Luca de Meo**, the former Renault CEO who originally brought Briatore into his Alpine advisory role — giving Briatore relationships and leverage on both sides of a potential deal. Aston Martin's team quickly and formally denied the rumours were true, calling them **'just a paddock rumour.'**
key_points: At the **Hungarian Grand Prix**, Alonso said flatly: **'I have a contract, I'm not going to change teams.'**
Multiple outlets report **Flavio Briatore** — Alonso's personal manager and an Alpine advisor — and incoming Alpine title sponsor **Gucci** are pushing hard to bring him back for **2027**.
**Gucci** is confirmed as Alpine's title sponsor from 2027, with the team set to race as **'Gucci Racing Alpine.'**
The Gucci connection runs through **Luca de Meo**, the former Renault (Alpine's parent) boss who is now CEO of Gucci's parent company **Kering** — and who originally brought Briatore into Alpine.
**Aston Martin** issued a formal denial, calling the rumours **'just a paddock rumour.'**

depth.background: Alonso is in the final year of his Aston Martin contract and said in May he'd decide his F1 future during the summer break, a decision made more urgent by Aston Martin's disappointing start to the 2026 season. Briatore returned to Alpine as a consultant to parent company Renault's board and remains Alonso's long-time personal manager — giving him unusual leverage to broker a deal on both sides if he wanted to. Alpine's cockpit alongside Pierre Gasly (signed through at least 2028) is open for 2027.

thread.previously: We reported Alonso said he'd decide his F1 future during the summer break and had shot down talk of an Alpine return.
thread.changed: At the Hungarian GP he denied it even more directly ('I have a contract'), but reports now name exactly who is pushing the move — Briatore and incoming sponsor Gucci — and Aston Martin has issued its own formal denial.

stories.title: Rajat Patidar to lead Central Zone's Duleep Trophy title defence, with Rinku Singh and two uncapped India quicks in the squad
stories.what_happened: Central Zone announced their squad for the 2026 season-opening Duleep Trophy, naming Rajat Patidar as captain to lead the team's title defence. The squad includes three other India internationals — Rinku Singh, left-arm spinner-allrounder Harsh Dubey, and fast bowler Yash Thakur — giving the side considerable top-level experience. Saransh Jain, Patidar's Madhya Pradesh teammate who recently earned a maiden India Test call-up for the Sri Lanka tour, will anchor the spin attack alongside Dubey and Uttar Pradesh leg-spinner Zeeshan Ansari, making his red-ball comeback after five years away following a recent India A tour of Sri Lanka. Vidarbha opener Aman Mokhade earns a spot after a standout 2025-26 Ranji Trophy season, scoring 760 runs in 11 innings at an average of 76, form that also earned him an India A call-up.
key_points: **Rajat Patidar** will captain Central Zone as they defend their **2025-26 Duleep Trophy** title.
The squad includes three other India internationals: **Rinku Singh**, Harsh Dubey and Yash Thakur.
Patidar's Madhya Pradesh teammate **Saransh Jain** — fresh off a maiden India Test call-up — leads the spin attack.
Vidarbha opener **Aman Mokhade** is picked after a breakout Ranji season: **760 runs in 11 innings** at an average of 76.
The Duleep Trophy is India's marquee **zonal first-class tournament**, historically a proving ground for Test selection.

depth.background: The Duleep Trophy is a first-class tournament contested between India's regional zones (North, South, East, West, Central), and has long served as a selection shop window — a strong run has historically helped uncapped players force their way into India's Test squad. Central Zone are the defending champions from the 2025-26 edition. Patidar, an established India international batter, captained Madhya Pradesh domestically and now leads Central Zone's title defence with a squad blending internationals and in-form domestic performers.

stories.title: Over 5.9 crore Indians filed income tax returns by the July 31 deadline — and this time, there was no extension
stories.what_happened: The Income Tax Department announced on **August 1** that more than **5.9 crore ITRs** had been filed for AY2026-27 by the July 31 deadline for taxpayers who don't need their accounts audited (mainly salaried individuals and small professionals filing ITR-1 through ITR-4). Filing built up steadily through July — crossing **1.7 crore by July 11**, **3 crore by July 22**, and **4 crore by July 27** — before a last-minute surge added over **40 lakh returns on the final day** as the portal saw heavy traffic. In the days before the deadline, taxpayers and chartered accountants had flagged **intermittent glitches** on the e-filing portal and pushed for a short extension, similar to what happened last year. The department did not extend the deadline this time, saying the portal was functioning and most earlier technical issues had been resolved. Because filing categories are staggered, this 5.9-crore figure is not the final tally for the year — non-audit businesses and professionals filing ITR-3/4/5 have until **August 31**, and entities requiring a tax audit have until **October 31** (with the audit report itself due September 30).
key_points: **5.9 crore** income tax returns (about **59 million**) were filed for Assessment Year 2026-27 by the July 31 deadline, the Income Tax Department said.
More than **40 lakh returns** were filed on the final day alone, as filers rushed the e-filing portal in the last hours.
Unlike last year, the department **held the deadline firm** this time despite reports of portal glitches and calls from tax professional bodies for an extension.
Filing was **more complex** this cycle — CBDT's revised ITR forms added fresh disclosure rules for capital gains, share-buyback losses, and certain trading transactions.
July 31 covers only **non-audit individual filers** — non-audit businesses have until **August 31**, and audited entities until **October 31**, so the final national count will keep climbing.

depth.background: An Income Tax Return (**ITR**) is the annual form every earning Indian above the tax-free threshold must file, declaring income and tax paid for a financial year. Filings are tagged to an **'Assessment Year'** — AY2026-27 covers income earned in FY2025-26 (April 2025–March 2026). Last year, the tax department **extended** the deadline for AY2025-26 from July 31 to **September 15, 2025**, after major changes to the ITR forms caused widespread filing delays, and total filings eventually crossed **7.3 crore**. This year, the **Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT)** again revised the forms — adding new disclosure fields — but chose not to extend the July 31 cut-off for non-audit filers.

stories.title: Sophie Molineux spins Southern Brave to a perfect start in The Hundred, beating London Spirit by 5 wickets
stories.what_happened: At Lord's, **London Spirit Women were restricted to 114 for 8** off their 100 balls, unable to find the boundaries needed to post a match-winning total. **Sophie Molineux was the difference**, taking **3 wickets for just 7 runs** to choke Spirit's innings and earn player of the match. In reply, **Southern Brave chased the target down comfortably, finishing 115 for 5**, sealing a **5-wicket win** and extending their unbeaten start to the Women's Hundred season.
key_points: Southern Brave chased down London Spirit's **114/8** with **115/5**, winning by **5 wickets** at Lord's.
**Sophie Molineux took 3 for 7**, strangling London Spirit's innings with spin and earning player of the match.
The result keeps Southern Brave **unbeaten** in the Women's Hundred competition this season.
London Spirit struggled to build partnerships, unable to push their total past **114** in their 100 balls.

depth.background: The Hundred is England's short-format, 100-ball domestic cricket competition, running men's and women's tournaments in parallel each August with eight city-based franchise teams. Southern Brave's women's side have been one of the tournament's strongest teams in recent seasons, and a perfect start to 2026 keeps them firmly in contention as the group stage progresses toward the knockouts. Left-arm spinner **Sophie Molineux**, an Australian international, is known for tying up batters with tight, disciplined bowling in the middle overs.

stories.title: Birmingham Phoenix chase down Warwickshire Fire with a ball to spare in The Hundred
stories.what_happened: Warwickshire Fire posted **144 for 3** from their 100 balls at Birmingham. In reply, **Birmingham Phoenix got over the line with 145 for 3**, winning by **7 wickets** but needing every ball bar one of their innings to complete the chase — finishing with just a single ball to spare. The tight finish reflects a competitive Women's Hundred season so far, with several matches decided in the closing stages.
key_points: Birmingham Phoenix chased **144/3** to beat Warwickshire Fire, finishing **145/3** with just **1 ball remaining**.
The win came in a tight run-chase that went down to the **final over** of the 100-ball innings.
It's another close finish in a **Women's Hundred** season already marked by tight group-stage matches.
The result affects the group standings as teams jostle for **knockout qualification**.

depth.background: The Hundred's Women's Competition runs alongside the men's tournament each English summer, with eight franchise teams playing a round-robin group stage before the top sides advance to knockouts. Birmingham Phoenix and Warwickshire Fire (based at Edgbaston) are regular rivals in the tournament given their shared home region, and close finishes between mid-table sides can be decisive for who ultimately reaches the playoffs.

stories.title: Sudan's army carries out its largest offensive since retaking Khartoum, cutting a key RSF supply corridor
stories.what_happened: Over two days of fighting across a **300-square-kilometer** stretch of North Kordofan state, Sudan's army, the Joint Force and allied militias recaptured **five towns** — Al-Baraka, Um Sayala, Um Qurfa, Jabrat Al-Sheikh and Bara. The offensive dismantled one of the RSF's most important logistics corridors, the route the paramilitary had used to move fighters, weapons and supplies between **Darfur and central Sudan**. Military officials called it the **largest ground offensive** since the army retook Khartoum last year. The gains also reopened a direct supply line to North Kordofan's capital, El Obeid, and secured a road linking the region to Omdurman, removing what officials described as one of the army's biggest vulnerabilities in central Sudan.
key_points: The army recaptured **five towns** in North Kordofan in two days of fighting
It's the **largest ground offensive** since the military retook Khartoum last year
The gains cut a **vital RSF corridor** used to move fighters and weapons between Darfur and central Sudan
It directly answers RSF leader Hemedti's **vow days earlier** to 'seize Khartoum'
Sudan's war has killed an estimated **40,000 people** and displaced 14 million

depth.background: Sudan has been at war since April 2023 between the national army and the paramilitary **Rapid Support Forces (RSF)**, led by Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo — known as **Hemedti**. The army recaptured the capital, Khartoum, from the RSF last year, but the RSF still controls large parts of Darfur and has kept fighting in central Sudan. A UN Fact-Finding Mission recently found that the RSF's campaign in Darfur, including mass killings and gang rapes, meets the legal definition of **genocide**. Just days ago, Hemedti released a video vowing to 'seize Khartoum' again, after his forces suffered setbacks on a key supply highway.

thread.previously: We reported that RSF leader Hemedti had released a video ordering his fighters to 'seize Khartoum,' as a UN probe found his campaign in Darfur amounted to genocide.
thread.changed: Sudan's army answered with its largest ground offensive since retaking Khartoum, capturing five North Kordofan towns and severing a key RSF supply corridor between Darfur and central Sudan.
